teile.einleitung: Anatta is a Pali word that means “non-self”. It is a central teaching of Buddhism. It says that there is no eternal, unchanging self in a person.
wichtigste: Anatta means “non-self”.
The teaching rejects an eternal, unchanging self, such as the Upanishads describe as the Atman.
Together with anicca and dukkha, anatta is one of the three marks of existence.
According to the teaching, a person is made up of five groups of existence, the skandhas.
The monk Nagasena explained the teaching with the comparison of a chariot.
Rebirth is often explained with a flame that passes from candle to candle.

abschnitte.text: In the Indian **Upanishads**, an eternal, unchanging self is described, the **Atman**. The Buddha, by contrast, taught **anatta**, “non-self”. He said that no lasting, independent self can be found in any part of a person. According to tradition, he presented this teaching to the five ascetics near Sarnath in the **Anattalakkhana Sutta**. It is regarded as his second sermon.

Anatta is one of the **three marks of existence**. The other two are **anicca**, impermanence, and **dukkha**, suffering or unsatisfactoriness. According to Buddhist teaching, these three marks characterise everything that has come about through conditions. Anyone who truly understands them can, according to the teaching, free themselves from clinging.

According to Buddhist teaching, a person is made up of **five groups of existence**, the **skandhas**. These are **rupa**, bodily form, then vedana, feeling, sanna, perception, the mental formations, and vinnana, consciousness. None of these groups is a lasting self. They change constantly.

In the Questions of King Milinda, the monk **Nagasena** explains the teaching with a **chariot**. A chariot is neither the axle nor the wheels nor the pole, but a name for their working together. In the same way, “Nagasena” is just a label for the groups of existence. The tradition often explains rebirth without a wandering self with a **flame** that is passed from candle to candle. The new flame is neither the same nor a completely different one.

Not all the early schools understood the teaching in the same way. The **Pudgalavada**, also called the Vatsiputriya, taught a “person” (pudgala) that was neither the same as nor different from the skandhas. Other schools criticised this as a relapse into the teaching of a self. The question of what makes up a person is still discussed in Buddhism today.

gewusst: According to tradition, the five ascetics reached liberation after hearing the sermon on non-self.
The comparison with the chariot is one of the best-known images in Buddhist philosophy.

teile.einleitung: The ban on face coverings forbids covering one's own face in public in Switzerland. It was narrowly accepted by the voters in 2021. The debate was mainly about the face veil that some Muslim women wear, such as the burka or niqab.
wichtigste: On 7 March 2021 the people and the cantons accepted the initiative “Yes to a ban on face coverings”, with 51.2 per cent Yes.
The ban has been in Article 10a of the Federal Constitution since 2021.
The national federal law has applied since 1 January 2025.
Anyone who breaks the ban can be punished with a fine of at most 1,000 francs.
There are exceptions, for example in places of worship, for reasons of health or safety, and for local customs such as carnival.
The cantons of Ticino and St Gallen already had bans of their own earlier.

abschnitte.text: The popular initiative “Yes to a ban on face coverings” was launched by the so-called **Egerkingen Committee**. The Federal Council and Parliament recommended rejecting it and put forward an indirect **counter-proposal**. On 7 March 2021 51.2 per cent of those voting nevertheless said Yes, and turnout was 51.4 per cent. The majority of the cantons, the **cantons' majority**, also agreed. With that the initiative was accepted.

The new **Article 10a** of the Federal Constitution forbids covering one's own face in public and in places open to the public. It comes directly after the article on the right to life and personal freedom. Covering the face is not forbidden in **places of worship**, that is, in houses of God such as churches or mosques. Further exceptions concern **health**, **safety**, **climatic conditions** and **local customs**. That is why hygiene masks, protective helmets, warm scarves in winter and carnival masks remain allowed.

So that the ban applies the same everywhere, in September 2023 Parliament passed a **federal law** on the ban on covering the face. It came into force on 1 January 2025. Anyone who does not comply risks a **fine** of at most 1,000 francs. The cantons and their police are responsible for enforcement.

Even before the Confederation there were bans in individual cantons. In **Ticino** the voters accepted a change to the cantonal constitution in 2013, and the law on it applied from 1 July 2016. **St Gallen** followed as the second canton: the cantonal parliament decided on the ban in 2017, and on 23 September 2018 the people agreed too. Other cantons rejected similar proposals.

**France** was the first country in Europe to introduce a nationwide ban, in 2011, and Belgium followed in the same year, later Austria and Denmark too. The **European Court of Human Rights** decided in 2014 in the case of S.A.S. v. France that such a ban can be permitted. It justified this by the protection of **living together**. Supporters see in the ban a sign of open encounter, safety and equality. Opponents stress **freedom of religion** and think the state should not prescribe clothing.

gewusst: The result of 2021 was so close that only a little over one person in a hundred tipped the balance.
Carnival masks are expressly allowed because they belong to local customs.
The court in Strasbourg did not consider safety reasons alone sufficient for a general ban.

teile.einleitung: The Egyptian Book of the Dead is a collection of spells that were placed in the tomb with the dead. The spells were meant to guide the dead person safely through the underworld into the afterlife. Most copies of the Book of the Dead are painted papyrus scrolls.
wichtigste: The Book of the Dead was meant to help the dead in the afterlife.
It was usually written on papyrus.
The Egyptians called it “Spells for Going Out by Day”.
The name “Book of the Dead” was given to it in 1842 by Karl Richard Lepsius.
It developed out of the Pyramid Texts and the Coffin Texts.
It became common in the New Kingdom, from about 1550 BC.

abschnitte.text: The ancient Egyptians believed in life after death. But the way there led through a dangerous **underworld**. The Book of the Dead contained **magic spells** that were meant to make this journey safe for the dead person. It was placed in the tomb. The Egyptians called the collection “**Spells for Going Out by Day**”: the dead person was supposed to be able to leave the tomb in daylight.

Most copies of the Book of the Dead are **papyrus scrolls**. Papyrus was made from the **papyrus plant**, which grew along the Nile. Next to the spells there are small, colourful pictures called **vignettes**. They show, for example, the dead person in front of the gods. One of the most beautiful copies is the **Papyrus of Ani**. It has belonged to the **British Museum** in London since the 19th century.

abschnitte.titel: How the Book of the Dead came about
abschnitte.text: The Book of the Dead had older forerunners. First came the **Pyramid Texts** inside the pyramids, then the **Coffin Texts** on coffins. At the start of the **New Kingdom**, around 1550 BC, the spells were then written on papyrus. That is how the Book of the Dead came into being. It was used until the **Late Period**.

According to Egyptian belief, the dead person’s **heart** was weighed at the judgement in the afterlife. So that it would not speak against the dead person, a **heart scarab** was laid on the mummy’s chest. This amulet in the shape of a beetle usually carried **Spell 30** from the Book of the Dead. It was meant to silence the heart.

The name “Book of the Dead” was given by the German Egyptologist **Karl Richard Lepsius**. In **1842** he published a papyrus from **Turin** and called it “Todtenbuch”, the spelling of the time. The name has lasted to this day, even though it is not a book in the modern sense.

gewusst: Every Book of the Dead was different: the people who ordered them could choose which spells went into them.
The scarab, a dung beetle, was a sign of the sun and of renewal for the Egyptians.

teile.einleitung: Nasreddin Hodja is the main character of countless funny stories. They come originally from Anatolia in present-day Turkey and are told today in many countries. Behind the joke there is often a clever lesson.
wichtigste: The stories of Nasreddin Hodja come from Anatolia.
His tomb stands in the Turkish town of Akşehir.
“Hodja” means teacher or scholar.
In many stories a donkey accompanies him.
Since 2022 the telling of the stories has been part of UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage.

abschnitte.text: Nasreddin is said to have lived in the Middle Ages in **Anatolia**. His title **“Hodja”** means **teacher** or **scholar**. Little is known for certain about his life. In the town of **Akşehir** in Turkey stands his **tomb**, and there he is celebrated every year with a festival. In many stories he rides on his **donkey**, sometimes even backwards.

Once Nasreddin comes to a feast in old clothes, and nobody pays him any attention. He goes home and puts on a **beautiful fur coat**. Now he is welcomed kindly and gets the best food. Then he dips the sleeve into the soup and says: **“Eat, my fur coat, eat!”** For it was not he but the fur coat that was invited.

In another story Nasreddin looks outside for his **key**, although he lost it in the house. Asked why, he answers: **“Because there is more light out here.”** Another time he sees the **moon** in the **well** and thinks it has fallen in. With a rope he wants to pull it out and falls on his back. Then he sees the moon in the sky and is glad that he has saved it.

The stories are told from Turkey to Central Asia, often under somewhat different names, such as **Molla Nasreddin**. In **2022** **UNESCO** included the telling of these stories in the **intangible cultural heritage**. Several countries made the application together. In books for children you can also find many of his adventures.

gewusst: The story of the key that people look for where there is light is told all over the world as an example of looking in the wrong place.
Many Nasreddin stories are so short that they can be told in a minute.

teile.einleitung: In Sunni Islam there are six articles of faith. They describe what a Muslim should believe in. Together they form iman, inner faith.
wichtigste: Sunni Islam knows six articles of faith.
They include God, angels, books, prophets, the Last Day and predestination.
The belief in predestination is called qadar.
The pilgrimage belongs to the five pillars, not to the articles of faith.
Muhammad is regarded as the “Seal of the Prophets”.
Inner faith is called iman in Arabic.

abschnitte.text: The Arabic word **iman** describes faith as inner conviction. The **six articles of faith** say what a Muslim believes in. To be distinguished from them are the five pillars, which are actions such as prayer and fasting. The **pilgrimage to Mecca** is therefore a pillar and does **not** belong to the articles of faith.

The first article is belief in the **one God**, Allah. He has no partner, and nothing is like him. The second article is belief in the **angels**. According to Islamic teaching they are servants of God. The angel Gabriel, in Arabic Jibril, brought Muhammad the revelation.

Muslims believe in the **books** that God has revealed. These include the **Torah** for Musa (Moses), the **Psalms** for Dawud (David), the Gospel, in Arabic **Injil**, for Isa (Jesus) and the Quran for Muhammad. They also believe in the **prophets**. Muhammad is regarded as the last prophet and bears the title **“Seal of the Prophets”**.

The fifth article is belief in the **Last Day**. On this day, according to Islamic teaching, all people will be raised and judged. The sixth article is called **qadar**, belief in predestination. It says that nothing happens without God's knowledge and will. Scholars have long discussed how this fits with the responsibility of human beings.

gewusst: Many prophets from the Quran also appear in the Bible, for example Abraham, Moses and Jesus.
The Shia sum up the foundations of their faith in a somewhat different list.

teile.einleitung: In Switzerland there are several hundred Muslim prayer rooms, but only four mosques with a minaret. Most Muslims pray in converted houses that you can hardly recognise from outside as a mosque. Since 2009 no new minarets may be built.
wichtigste: Only four mosques in Switzerland have a minaret.
They stand in Zurich, Geneva, Winterthur and Wangen bei Olten.
The Mahmood Mosque in Zurich was in 1963 the first mosque with a minaret in Switzerland.
The Great Mosque of Geneva was opened in 1978.
Since the vote of 2009 no new minarets may be built.
Most prayer rooms are in converted houses without a minaret.

abschnitte.text: The **Mahmood Mosque** stands in Zurich. It was opened in **1963** and was the **first mosque with a minaret** in Switzerland. It was built by the **Ahmadiyya** community. The small mosque with its slender minaret is still a well-known place in the city. It often invites visitors to conversations.

In **Geneva** the **Great Mosque** was opened in **1978**. It is one of the largest mosques in Switzerland and also has a minaret. It was paid for mainly with money from Saudi Arabia. In **Winterthur** in the canton of Zurich there is also a mosque with a minaret. This gives the canton of Zurich two of the four minarets.

The fourth minaret stands in **Wangen bei Olten** in the canton of **Solothurn**. A **Turkish cultural association** built it on its building. From 2006 there was a long dispute about it in the municipality and in court. This dispute gave the impetus for the **minaret initiative**. In **2009** the voters accepted it, and since then no **new minarets** may be built.

Most Muslim communities in Switzerland do not have a magnificent mosque. They pray in **converted houses**, flats or commercial buildings **without a minaret**. The rooms often belong to associations of people of the same origin, for example from the Balkans or Turkey. Here too there is a **mihrab**, a niche in the wall that shows the direction of prayer towards Mecca.

gewusst: The Mahmood Mosque was in 1963 not only the first mosque with a minaret in Switzerland but one of the first mosque buildings in the country at all.
From outside, many Swiss prayer rooms look like quite ordinary workshops or offices.

teile.einleitung: At the great Islamic festivals, Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha, many Muslims visit their family and friends. The visits are among the loveliest customs of the festival days. With them people show respect, togetherness and joy.
wichtigste: On the festival day people visit relatives and friends.
Younger people often go first to their parents and grandparents.
The festival is a time to make up after a quarrel.
Guests are offered tea, coffee and sweet things.
In many cantons parents can apply for a day off school for the festival day.

abschnitte.text: The festival day begins in the morning with the **festival prayer** in the mosque. After that the family comes together. Often there is a large **festive breakfast** with many treats. Many people wear beautiful or new clothes. Then the visits to **relatives and friends** begin.

Older people are especially honoured on the festival day. That is why younger people often visit their **parents and grandparents** first. In Turkey, children kiss the **hand** of older relatives and touch it to their forehead. This is a sign of respect. The children often get sweets or a little money for it. Some families also go to the cemetery and pray at the **graves** of their dead relatives.

Guests are very welcome on the festival day. **Tea, coffee and sweet things** are put on the table for them. Visitors like to bring a **small gift**, such as chocolates or pastries. The festival is also a time of peace. Anyone who has quarrelled should **make up**, shake hands and forgive one another.

Many Muslims in Switzerland have relatives in other countries. On the festival day they phone or see each other by **video call**. The festival is not an official public holiday in Switzerland. In many cantons, however, parents can submit a **request** for high religious festivals so that their child gets a day off. Some families also celebrate on the weekend after the festival.

gewusst: Because the Islamic calendar follows the moon, the festival days move forward by about eleven days every year.
In Turkey, Eid al-Fitr is also called the “Sugar Festival” because many sweets are given as presents.

teile.einleitung: The Seljuks were a ruling family from the Oghuz people, a Turkic people. In the 11th century they conquered a large empire from present-day Iran to Anatolia. Their advance changed the history of the Middle East and of Europe.
wichtigste: The Seljuks descended from the Oghuz, a Turkic people.
Tughril Beg entered Baghdad in 1055 and received the title sultan.
Alp Arslan defeated the Byzantine Empire at Manzikert in 1071.
The vizier Nizam al-Mulk founded the Nizamiyya colleges.
The capital of the Seljuks of Rum was Konya.
In 1243 the Seljuks of Rum lost to the Mongols at Köse Dağ.

abschnitte.text: The Seljuks came from the people of the **Oghuz**, a **Turkic people** from Central Asia. They are named after their leader Seljuk. They adopted Sunni Islam and moved westwards. **Tughril Beg** entered **Baghdad** in **1055**. The caliph gave him the title **sultan**, that is, “holder of power”.

In **1071** Sultan **Alp Arslan** defeated the **Byzantine Empire** at the **battle of Manzikert**. After that Turkic groups could advance into Anatolia, into present-day Turkey. The Byzantine emperor later asked for help in the West. This contributed to the beginning of the **First Crusade** in **1096**.

The vizier **Nizam al-Mulk** was a powerful minister of the Seljuks. He founded the **Nizamiyya colleges**, for example in Baghdad. There Islamic law and theology were taught. Under Sultan **Malik Shah** the scholar **Omar Khayyam** worked on a **calendar reform**. Khayyam is also famous as a poet.

In Anatolia an empire of its own arose, that of the **Seljuks of Rum**. “Rum” means “Rome” and referred to the territory of the Byzantines. The capital was **Konya**, where magnificent mosques and caravanserais were built. In **1243** the Seljuks of Rum lost the **battle of Köse Dağ** against the **Mongols**. After that their empire gradually fell apart, and later the Ottomans rose.

gewusst: Seljuk caravanserais offered merchants safe resting places along the trade routes, and some still stand today.
Omar Khayyam was at the same time a mathematician, astronomer and poet.

teile.einleitung: Salafism is a current in Sunni Islam. Its followers want to live the faith as, in their view, the first Muslims did. The movement is diverse and is divided by research into several branches.
wichtigste: The word comes from “al-salaf al-salih”, the pious predecessors.
What is meant are the first three generations of Muslims.
Salafis often appeal to the scholar Ibn Taymiyya (1263 to 1328).
They reject religious innovations, which they call “bid'a”.
Tawhid, the unity of God, is at the centre of their teaching.
Research distinguishes quietist, political and jihadist Salafis.

abschnitte.text: The Arabic word **salaf** means “predecessor” or “forefather”. By **al-salaf al-salih**, the “pious predecessors”, the first three generations of Muslims are meant. These include the companions of the Prophet Muhammad and the two generations after them. Salafis see in them a model for faith and everyday life. They want to align religion and life as closely as possible with this model.

Salafis appeal especially often to **Ibn Taymiyya**, who lived from 1263 to 1328. He fought against innovations and against the veneration of saints. His writings are also fundamental for Wahhabism in Saudi Arabia. In the 20th century the hadith scholar **Nasir al-Din al-Albani** (1914 to 1999) was very influential. He re-examined the authenticity of thousands of hadiths, that is, reports about the Prophet.

At the centre stands **tawhid**, the unity of God. Salafis see the veneration of saints and graves as a violation of this unity. As **bid'a** they reject religious innovations, that is, customs that did not exist in the time of the Prophet. They also criticise **taqlid**, the unquestioning following of one of the traditional schools of law. They want to rely directly on the Quran and sunna.

The researcher Quintan Wiktorowicz divided Salafis into three groups. **Quietists** withdraw from politics and concentrate on faith and teaching. **Political Salafis** want to change society according to their ideas. **Jihadists** support violence, and they are a small minority. Many states, including Switzerland, watch violent groups closely.

In the 19th century there was a movement called the **reform Salafiyya**. It wanted to combine Islam with reason and modern science. Today's Salafism differs clearly from it. It usually interprets the religious texts strictly literally. Despite the similar name, the two movements therefore pursue different aims.

gewusst: Most Salafis reject violence, and only a small group supports it.
The writings of Ibn Taymiyya are over 700 years old and are still read today.

teile.einleitung: Wahhabism is a very strict movement within Sunni Islam. It arose in the 18th century on the Arabian Peninsula and is still closely tied to the state of Saudi Arabia today.
wichtigste: Its founder was the scholar Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab (1703 to 1792).
The teaching arose in Najd, the highlands of central Arabia.
In 1744 Ibn Abd al-Wahhab made an alliance with the ruler Muhammad ibn Saud.
Its followers call themselves Muwahhidun, “those who affirm the oneness of God”.
Wahhabism builds on the Hanbali school of law.
Wahhabis strictly reject the veneration of saints and graves.

abschnitte.text: **Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab** came from the village of Uyaynah in **Najd**. He wanted Muslims to return to an Islam as it originally was, in his opinion. He considered many customs of his time wrong. After him the movement was later called “Wahhabism”. This name is a **name given from outside**, and the followers themselves speak of **Muwahhidun**.

At the centre is **tawhid**, the unity and oneness of God. Wahhabis think that only God may be worshipped. They saw the veneration of saints and graves as **polytheism**. That is why, for example, many tomb domes were torn down in Mecca and Medina. In law the teaching relies on the **Hanbalis**, regarded as the strictest of the four Sunni schools of law.

In 1744 Ibn Abd al-Wahhab allied himself in **Diriyah**, near Riyadh, with the ruler **Muhammad ibn Saud**. The scholar gave the religious teaching, the ruler the political power. From this alliance arose the **first Saudi state**. It was destroyed in 1818 by Egyptian troops on behalf of the Ottoman Empire, led by Ibrahim Pasha.

Later the Saud family rebuilt their rule, and in 1932 the kingdom of **Saudi Arabia** came into being. The ruling house relies to this day on the Wahhabi scholars. The teaching is also widespread in **Qatar**. Many other Muslims view Wahhabism critically and reject its strictness, while its followers hold it to be the right way.

gewusst: The descendants of Ibn Abd al-Wahhab and of Ibn Saud are still two important families in Saudi Arabia today.
The ruins of Diriyah are today part of UNESCO World Heritage.

teile.einleitung: Sufism is a mystical branch of Islam. Sufis seek an especially close, inner relationship with God. This includes prayer, remembrance of God and, in some orders, music and dance.
wichtigste: Sufism is a mystical branch of Islam.
The word “Sufi” is usually derived from the Arabic word for wool.
“Dervish” originally means “poor person” in Persian.
Remembrance of God by repeating formulas is called dhikr.
The mystic Rumi is buried in Konya.
The Mevlevi Order is known for its whirling dervishes.

abschnitte.text: The word **Sufi** is usually derived from the Arabic word **“suf”**, which means **wool**. Early Sufis wore simple garments of wool. In this way they showed that possessions were not important to them. Another word for Sufi is **dervish**. It comes from Persian and originally means **“poor person”**.

An important practice of the Sufis is **dhikr**, the **remembrance of God**. In it short prayer formulas or names of God are repeated often. This can happen quietly or aloud, alone or in a group. Sufis often join together in **orders**. A teacher, the sheikh, accompanies the pupils on their path.

The **Mevlevi Order** goes back to the poet and mystic **Rumi**. Rumi lived in the 13th century and is buried in **Konya** in Turkey. The Mevlevis are known for the ceremony **sema**. In it the dervishes slowly turn in a circle to music. Their white garments swing out wide as they do so.

The whirling dervishes wear a tall **felt hat**. It is meant to represent a **gravestone** and to recall transience. In the ceremony the **ney** is played, a **flute** made of reed. Its sound is regarded as the soul's longing for God. Rumi's poems are still read in many languages today.

gewusst: In some countries Rumi's poems are among the best-selling volumes of poetry.
The sema ceremony of the Mevlevis is on the UNESCO list of intangible cultural heritage.

teile.einleitung: In Bosnia and Herzegovina about half of the population belongs to Islam. Islam came to the country with the Ottomans in the 15th century. The Bosnian Muslims are called Bosniaks, and they have a tradition of their own, shaped by Europe.
wichtigste: The Ottomans conquered Bosnia in 1463, and afterwards many locals converted to Islam.
The Gazi Husrev-beg Madrasa in Sarajevo has been teaching since 1537.
The head of the Islamic Community is called the Reis-ul-Ulema.
Austria-Hungary recognised Islam in 1912 with an Islam Law.
In the 2013 census about 51 per cent described themselves as Muslim.
The Potočari memorial recalls the genocide of Srebrenica in July 1995.

abschnitte.text: The **Ottomans** conquered Bosnia in the year **1463**. In the following decades many locals converted to **Islam**. Mosques, bridges, baths and schools arose. In **Sarajevo**, Gazi Husrev-beg endowed a madrasa, an Islamic school, in **1537**. Because of its lead roof it is also called Kuršumlija. It has trained pupils for almost 500 years.

In the past, Bosnian was sometimes written with Arabic letters. This script is called **Arebica**. It is adapted to the sounds of the Slavic language. It was used from the 15th to the early 20th century, above all for religious and popular texts.

In 1878 **Austria-Hungary** took over the administration, and in 1908 it annexed Bosnia and Herzegovina. In 1882 the office of **Reis-ul-Ulema** was created, the head of the Islamic Community. In this way the Bosnian Muslims became independent of the religious administration in Istanbul. With the **Islam Law of 1912**, Austria-Hungary recognised Islam as a religious community. In Austria this law is still a basis for recognition today.

From 1992 to 1995 the **Bosnian War** raged. Many mosques were destroyed, among them the **Ferhadija** in Banja Luka from the 16th century. It was blown up in 1993 and reopened in 2016, and for this many original stones were recovered from the rubble. In July 1995 Bosnian Serb troops killed about 8,000 Bosniak men and boys in **Srebrenica**. International courts classified the crime as **genocide**. The **Potočari** memorial recalls the victims.

According to the **2013 census**, 50.7 per cent of the population were Muslims. Besides them live mainly **Orthodox Serbs** and **Catholic Croats** in the country. Many people from Bosnia and Herzegovina also live today in **Switzerland**. They have founded mosque associations of their own here.

gewusst: The Austrian Islam Law of 1912 came about because of the Muslims in Bosnia.
In Sarajevo a mosque, a church and a synagogue stand only a few minutes' walk from one another.

teile.einleitung: Agnosticism is the view that one cannot know for certain whether there is a God. Agnostics therefore commit themselves neither to belief nor to disbelief. The word comes from Greek and means roughly “not knowing”.
wichtigste: Agnostics say: “I do not know whether there is a God.”
The Greek word “ágnostos” means “unknowable” or “unknown”.
The word “agnostic” was invented by the naturalist Thomas Henry Huxley.
Charles Darwin too called himself an agnostic in his autobiography.
One distinguishes between strong and weak agnostics.
There are also agnostic theists and agnostic atheists.

abschnitte.text: Agnostics regard the question of God as **undecidable**. In their view his existence can be neither proved nor disproved. That is why they refrain from judgement. The word comes from the Greek **“ágnostos”**: “gnosis” means knowledge, “a-” means “not”. Agnosticism is therefore not a belief, but an attitude to knowledge.

The term was invented in the 19th century by the English naturalist **Thomas Henry Huxley**. He defended Charles Darwin's theory of evolution so fiercely that he was called **“Darwin's bulldog”**. **Charles Darwin** himself also wrote in his autobiography that the label “agnostic” described his attitude best. In his youth he had still been intended for the ministry.

In the USA **Robert G. Ingersoll** (1833 to 1899) became well known. He was a lawyer and a celebrated speaker. In his lectures he criticised religion and for that reason got the nickname “The Great Agnostic”. His speeches attracted many people.

**Strong agnostics** hold the question of God to be fundamentally unanswerable. **Weak agnostics** say only that one does not know it today, but perhaps will later. Belief and knowledge are two different questions here. An **agnostic theist** believes in God, but holds certain knowledge about him to be impossible. An **agnostic atheist** does not believe in God, but does not claim to be able to prove that he does not exist.

gewusst: Huxley invented the word because no existing label suited his attitude.
As a young man Darwin was intended for the ministry before he became a naturalist.

teile.einleitung: Anti-Muslim hostility means rejection, prejudice or hatred towards Muslims. People also speak of anti-Muslim racism. In Switzerland and in Europe this subject is studied with surveys and reports.
wichtigste: According to the FSO, in 2016 about 14 per cent of respondents were hostile towards Muslims.
In 2016, 33 per cent expressed distrust of Islam as a religion.
In 2019 about 35 per cent of Muslim respondents experienced discrimination because of their religion.
The Federal Commission against Racism published a topic dossier on it in 2023.
About 10 per cent of the proceedings under the anti-racism law since 1995 concerned anti-Muslim racism.
In 13 EU states, according to the FRA in 2024, about 47 per cent of Muslims experienced racist discrimination.

abschnitte.text: People speak of **anti-Muslim hostility** when people are rejected, insulted or disadvantaged because of their Muslim faith. In this, a whole group is often judged with **prejudices** instead of each person individually. The difference matters: criticism of ideas or actions is allowed. Treating people worse because of their religion, by contrast, is **discrimination**.

The Federal Statistical Office (**FSO**) regularly asks about living together. In **2016**, according to the FSO, **14 per cent** of respondents were hostile towards Muslims. **33 per cent** expressed distrust of Islam as a religion. In **2020**, **20 per cent** agreed with negative prejudices about Muslims. In the study “Security 2017”, **46 per cent** regarded Islam as a threat to the security of Switzerland.

Muslims themselves were also asked. According to an FSO survey of **2019**, about **35 per cent** of them experienced **discrimination** because of their religion in the previous twelve months. This can happen when looking for a flat or a job, at school or on the street. Women with a headscarf report it especially often.

Since **1995** Switzerland has had the **anti-racism law**. Among other things it forbids publicly demeaning people because of their religion. According to the **Federal Commission against Racism** (FCR), about **10 per cent** of all criminal proceedings under this law concerned anti-Muslim racism. In **2023** the FCR published a **topic dossier** on anti-Muslim racism.

The **EU Agency for Fundamental Rights** (FRA) surveyed Muslims in **13 EU states**. According to its report of **2024**, **47 per cent** of them experienced racist discrimination. The figure was highest in **Austria**, at **71 per cent**. Such figures help authorities and schools to act in a targeted way against prejudice.

gewusst: The Swiss anti-racism law was accepted in a popular vote in 1994 and came into force in 1995.

teile.einleitung: Amaterasu is the sun goddess in Shinto, the old religion of Japan. She is regarded as the most important deity in Shinto. According to tradition, the Japanese imperial family is descended from her.
wichtigste: Amaterasu is the sun goddess of Shinto.
Her name means roughly “the one who shines in the heavens”.
Her stormy brother is called Susanoo.
In the myth she withdrew into a rock cave, and the world became dark.
The myths are found in the Kojiki (712) and the Nihon Shoki (720).
A mirror, a sword and a jewel make up the Japanese imperial regalia.

abschnitte.text: In **Shinto**, many deities are worshipped, called **kami**. The most important of them is **Amaterasu**, the goddess of the sun. Her name means roughly “the one who shines in the heavens”. According to the myth, she came into being when the god Izanagi washed his face, and she has ruled the heavens ever since. The sun on the Japanese flag recalls the great importance of the sun in Japan.

Amaterasu had a wild brother, **Susanoo**, the god of storms and the sea. He did so much damage that Amaterasu, in anger, withdrew into a **rock cave**. Without her, it became **dark** everywhere in the world. The other gods discussed how they could lure the sun goddess out again.

The goddess **Ame-no-Uzume** danced so comically in front of the cave that all the gods laughed out loud. Curious, Amaterasu looked out. Then she saw her own reflection in a **mirror** that the gods had hung up. As she came closer, she was drawn out of the cave, and the light returned. This story is told in the **Kojiki** of 712 and the **Nihon Shoki** of 720, the oldest history books of Japan.

According to the myth, the first emperor, **Jimmu**, was a descendant of the sun goddess. In the past, this was used to explain the special position of the emperor. The three **imperial regalia**, a mirror, a sword and a jewel, come from Amaterasu according to tradition. They are used at the accession to the throne, but are never shown in public. The goddess’s most important sanctuary is the Grand Shrine of **Ise**.

gewusst: The buildings of the Ise shrine are traditionally rebuilt every 20 years.
In modern times, hardly anyone has ever seen the imperial regalia themselves.

teile.einleitung: Mary, the mother of Jesus, is called Maryam in the Quran. In Islam she is one of the most honoured women of all. The Quran tells of her childhood, her piety and the birth of her son Isa.
wichtigste: Mary is called Maryam in the Quran, and Jesus is called Isa.
Maryam is the only woman who is named by name in the Quran.
The 19th surah of the Quran bears her name.
According to the Quran her father was called Imran, and the 3rd surah is named after his family.
The prophet Zakariya looked after the young Maryam.
The angel Jibril announced the birth of Isa to her.
According to the Quran, Isa was born under a date palm.

abschnitte.text: In the Quran many women are mentioned, but only one by name: **Maryam**. Her name occurs more than thirty times. The **19th surah** is called “Maryam” after her. The **3rd surah** is called “Al Imran”, which means “the family of Imran”. According to the Quran, Imran was Maryam's father.

Already before her birth, her mother dedicated Maryam to the service of God. As a child Maryam lived in the temple, and the prophet **Zakariya** was responsible for her. Zakariya was also the father of the prophet **Yahya**, whom Christians know as John the Baptist. Whenever Zakariya came to Maryam, he found **food** with her each time. To his question Maryam replied that the food came from God.

One day the angel **Jibril** came to Maryam; in English he is called Gabriel. He brought her the news that she would have a son. Maryam asked in astonishment how that was possible. The angel replied that nothing is impossible for God: when he wants something, he only says “Be!”, and it is. This child was **Isa**, whom Islam reveres as a great prophet.

The 19th surah tells how Maryam leaned against the trunk of a **date palm**. There Isa was born. God told her to shake the trunk, and then **fresh dates** would fall down. God also let a little stream flow beneath her. When the people later reproached Maryam, according to the Quran the little Isa himself spoke and defended his mother.

The Quran says that God **chose** Maryam above all the women of the world and made her pure. She is regarded as an especially **pious** and God-fearing woman. Many Muslims name her, together with a few other women, as the best women of all. Because Christians too revere Mary greatly, her figure connects both religions.

gewusst: In the Quran Maryam is named more often than in the whole New Testament of the Bible.
In the Quran Isa is often called “Isa, the son of Maryam”, that is, after his mother.

teile.einleitung: Advaita Vedanta is an influential school of Indian philosophy. It teaches that ultimately there is only a single reality: Brahman. Its best-known teacher is Shankara.
wichtigste: “Advaita” means “non-duality”, literally “not two”.
According to this teaching, the only reality is Brahman.
The inner self, the atman, is not different from Brahman.
The variety of the world is regarded as maya, a deceptive appearance.
A well-known parable is the rope that one takes for a snake.
Ramanuja and Madhva later developed other schools of Vedanta.

abschnitte.text: The word **Vedanta** means “end of the Veda”. By this are meant the **Upanishads**, the last parts of India's holy scriptures, the Vedas. Different schools have interpreted these texts differently. The best known is **Advaita Vedanta**. Its most important teacher is the philosopher **Shankara**, who lived around the year 800.

**A-dvaita** literally means “not two”. The school teaches that ultimately there is only one reality, namely **Brahman**. The inner self of the human being, the **atman**, is also not different from Brahman. A famous sentence from the Upanishads runs “Tat tvam asi”, “That is you”. Whoever truly realises this is, according to the teaching, set free.

How does Advaita explain the variety of the world? It is regarded as **maya**, a deceptive appearance that arises through **ignorance** (avidya). A well-known parable: in the twilight one takes a **rope** for a **snake** and is frightened. As soon as one looks closely, the snake disappears and only the rope remains. In this way one is meant to recognise Brahman behind the world.

Not all Indian thinkers agreed with Shankara. **Ramanuja** taught **Vishishtadvaita**, “qualified non-dualism”: souls and world are real, but depend on God like a body. **Madhva** advocated **Dvaita** in the 13th century. He taught that God, souls and matter are eternally different. With that he clearly set himself against Shankara.

gewusst: In the West Advaita Vedanta became known at the end of the 19th century especially through the monk Vivekananda.
Shankara is said to have founded monasteries all over India that still exist today.

teile.einleitung: Rumi was a famous poet and mystic of the 13th century. He lived for a long time in Konya in present-day Anatolia and wrote mainly in Persian. His poems about love of God and longing are still read all over the world today.
wichtigste: Rumi's main work is the great didactic poem “Masnavi”.
He wrote most of his works in Persian.
The nickname “Rumi” refers to Anatolia, the land of Rum.
His followers call him “Mawlana”, which means “our master”.
In 1244 he met the wandering dervish Shams of Tabriz.
His followers call the day of his death, 17 December, the “wedding night”.

abschnitte.text: Rumi was born in **1207** in Central Asia. As a child he moved with his family far to the west. In the end they settled in **Konya** in Anatolia. This region was then called **Rum**, because it had earlier belonged to the Eastern Roman Empire. That is where his nickname **“Rumi”** comes from. His followers call him reverently **“Mawlana”**, which means “our master”.

Rumi was at first a respected scholar and teacher. In the year **1244** he met the wandering dervish **Shams of Tabriz**. This meeting changed his life. Shams became his most important spiritual friend. When Shams later disappeared, Rumi was deeply sad. He dedicated his great collection of lyric poems to him; it is called the **“Divan of Shams”**.

Rumi's main work is the **Masnavi**, a didactic poem in several volumes. It contains stories, parables and thoughts about God and human beings. He wrote it, like most of his works, in **Persian**. The Masnavi begins with the **lament of a reed flute**: it was cut from the reeds and longs to return to its origin. In this way Rumi describes the soul's longing for God.

After Rumi's death his followers founded the **Mevlevi Order**. Its members are known for their whirling dance, which is why they are often called **whirling dervishes**. Rumi died on **17 December 1273** in Konya. His followers call this day the **“wedding night”**, because his soul united with God. Every year it is observed in Konya with great celebrations.

gewusst: The ceremony of the whirling dervishes is part of UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage.
Rumi's tomb in Konya is today a museum that very many people visit.

t195h8pf.t: Federation of Islamic Umbrella Organisations of Switzerland

teile.einleitung: The Federation of Islamic Umbrella Organisations of Switzerland, FIDS for short, is an association of Muslim organisations. It is regarded as the largest Muslim umbrella organisation in Switzerland. It wants to represent the concerns of Muslims towards the authorities and the public.
wichtigste: The FIDS is an umbrella organisation of umbrella organisations.
Its members are cantonal associations and organisations by origin, for example Albanian, Bosnian or Turkish.
Through these organisations it represents, according to SRF, about 240 centres and associations.
Not all mosque associations in Switzerland are organised in an umbrella organisation.
In Switzerland the cantons decide on the recognition of religious communities.

abschnitte.text: The FIDS is a **private-law association**, so similar to a club. Its members are themselves organisations. They include **cantonal associations** and organisations that are organised by origin and language. According to a report by swissinfo, in 2020 the FIDS indirectly represented about two thirds of the mosque associations in Switzerland. Some of the associations belong to no umbrella organisation.

Muslims in Switzerland come from many countries. Many associations were founded by **origin and language**. Researchers at ETH Zurich pointed out in 2017 that it is therefore hard to speak with one voice. Umbrella organisations such as the FIDS try to bring this diversity together. In this way the authorities have a contact.

The legal **recognition** of a religious community is a matter for the **cantons** in Switzerland and a long road. According to swissinfo, the FIDS statutes of 2016 do not name this recognition as an aim. Muslim organisations often set other priorities, such as pastoral care, further training or exchange with other religions. The FIDS is represented by an elected board. According to SRF, Önder Günes was president in 2024, and before him Montassar BenMrad held the office for years.

gewusst: Montassar BenMrad also sits on the advisory board of the Swiss Centre for Islam and Society in Fribourg.

teile.einleitung: Al-Ghazali was a Persian scholar of the 11th century. He is regarded as one of the most influential thinkers of Sunni Islam. He is known for his criticism of the philosophers and for bringing together mysticism and faithfulness to the law.
wichtigste: Al-Ghazali was born around 1058 in Tus in Khorasan and died there in 1111.
From 1091 he taught at the famous Nizamiyya in Baghdad.
In 1095 he gave up his post after a crisis in his life and lived as a Sufi.
In the “Incoherence of the Philosophers” he criticised thinkers such as Avicenna.
His main work is the “Revival of the Religious Sciences”.
He bears the honorary title “Proof of Islam”.

abschnitte.text: Al-Ghazali came from **Tus** in the region of **Khorasan**, in the north-east of present-day Iran. He studied law and theology. The Seljuk vizier **Nizam al-Mulk** appointed him in 1091 to the **Nizamiyya**, a famous college in Baghdad. There he had many pupils and great standing.

In 1095 al-Ghazali fell into a deep crisis. He doubted whether his knowledge really led him to God. He gave up his post and for years lived as a **Sufi**, that is, as a mystic. In his work **“The Deliverer from Error”** he tells of his doubts and his search for certainty. He showed that mysticism and faithfulness to the law do not contradict each other.

In his work **“Tahafut al-falasifa”**, the “Incoherence of the Philosophers”, he engaged with thinkers such as **Avicenna**. They followed the teaching of the Greek Aristotle. On three points he accused them of unbelief, for example because of the teaching that the world is eternal. A well-known example concerns **fire and cotton**: according to al-Ghazali, the cotton does not burn necessarily because of the fire, but because God creates the burning each time.

His most extensive work is the **“Ihya ulum ad-din”**, the “Revival of the Religious Sciences”. In forty books it deals with worship, everyday life, bad habits and paths to salvation. In it he combines law, theology and mysticism. Because of his importance he received the honorary title **“Hujjat al-Islam”**, Proof of Islam.

gewusst: The philosopher Averroes later wrote a reply with the title “The Incoherence of the Incoherence”.
Al-Ghazali's works were also read in Christian Europe in the Middle Ages.

teile.einleitung: A madhhab is a school of law in Islam. The schools of law lay down how rules for life are derived from the Quran and tradition. Today there are four great Sunni schools of law and one important Shia one.
wichtigste: There are four great Sunni schools of law.
They are called Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali.
The Hanafi school goes back to Abu Hanifa of Kufa.
The Maliki school prevails in North and West Africa.
In Indonesia the Shafi'i school is predominant.
The Twelver Shia follow the Jafari school.

abschnitte.text: A **madhhab** is a **school of law**. It shows how scholars derive rules from the **Quran** and **hadith**, for example for prayer, fasting or trade. Today there are four great Sunni schools: the **Hanafi**, **Maliki**, **Shafi'i** and **Hanbali**. Other schools, such as the Zahiri, have died out. The schools recognise one another.

The **Hanafi school** goes back to **Abu Hanifa**, who taught in **Kufa** in Iraq and died in 767. His school gave much room to reasoned personal judgement. With **istihsan**, juristic preference, a jurist could depart from strict reasoning by analogy if it seemed more just. The Ottoman Empire promoted this school. That is why Sunnis in the **Balkans** and in **Turkey** traditionally follow the Hanafi school. Many Muslims in Switzerland come from these regions.

**Malik ibn Anas** founded the Maliki school. His work **al-Muwatta**, “the well-trodden path”, is one of the oldest collections of law. He also stressed the practice of the people of **Medina**. The Malikis shape **North and West Africa**. The **Shafi'i** school spread along trade routes to South-East Asia and East Africa. It is predominant in **Indonesia**. Its founder **al-Shafi'i** died in 820 in Egypt.

The **Hanbali school** keeps especially close to the Quran and hadith. It shapes the law of **Saudi Arabia**, and the Wahhabi movement relied on it. The **Twelver Shia** have a school of law of their own, the **Jafari**. It is named after the sixth imam **Jafar al-Sadiq** and is widespread in, for example, **Iran** and **Iraq**.

gewusst: The Muwatta of Malik ibn Anas is one of the oldest surviving collections of law in Islam.
Many Muslims in Switzerland follow the Hanafi school because of their origins.

teile.einleitung: The Alevis are a faith community that comes mainly from Turkey. They especially revere Ali, the cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad. Their services and customs differ clearly from those of many other Muslim communities.
wichtigste: Alevis gather in the cemevi, not in the mosque.
Their service is called cem, and women and men celebrate it together.
A spiritual leader is called a dede.
The long-necked lute saz is very important in the service.
According to estimates, about 15 per cent of the population of Turkey are Alevis.
In 2012 Basel-Stadt recognised two Alevi communities.

abschnitte.text: Most Alevis do not pray in mosques. They meet in the **cemevi**, the assembly house. The service is called **cem**. In it poems are recited, music is played and ritual dances are performed. Women and men celebrate together in the same room. The cem is led by a **dede**; the word means “grandfather”.

A special instrument is the **saz**, also called the **bağlama**. It is a long-necked lute with a long neck and a rounded body. Many Alevis see their songs as part of prayer. The texts often tell of God, of Ali and of love for people.

Alevis especially revere **Ali**. He was the cousin and son-in-law of Muhammad. Their world of faith also recalls the **twelve Imams**. In the month of **Muharram**, many Alevis therefore fast for twelve days. Afterwards they celebrate the **Aşure festival** and share a sweet dish. Also important is the saint **Hacı Bektaş Veli** of the 13th century. His tomb in the town of Hacıbektaş in central Anatolia is a popular place of pilgrimage.

abschnitte.titel: Alevis in Turkey and in Switzerland
abschnitte.text: Estimates assume that about **15 per cent** of the people in Turkey are Alevis. There are no exact figures. Through labour migration, many Alevis also live in Germany and Switzerland today. In October 2012 the Grand Council of **Basel-Stadt** recognised two Alevi communities. They were the first religious communities in Switzerland that are neither Christian nor Jewish to receive such cantonal recognition.

gewusst: Whether the Alevis belong to Islam is not seen the same way by everyone: some Alevis regard themselves as Muslims, others as a faith community of their own.
The ritual dance in the cem is called semah.

teile.einleitung: Anyone who enters a mosque often sees walls full of patterns. Stars, tendrils and script interlock. These decorations are called Islamic ornament.
wichtigste: Mosques are decorated with patterns and script instead of pictures.
Islamic ornaments are often very symmetrical.
Arabesques are intertwined plant tendrils.
Stars with six, eight or more points occur especially often.
Geometric patterns are drawn with compasses and ruler.
Muqarnas are honeycomb-like decorations on ceilings and arches.

abschnitte.text: In mosques there are usually no pictures of people or animals. Instead **patterns**, **plant tendrils** and **beautiful script** decorate the walls. The patterns repeat and could go on endlessly. This is meant to recall the **infinity of God**. Many ornaments are **symmetrical**: if you mirror them in the middle, both halves look the same.

Many Islamic patterns are built up from **stars** with six, eight or more points. Between them lie **polygons**. They are drawn with **compasses and ruler**, because these give exact circles and straight lines. A popular **eight-pointed star** arises when you lay two squares of equal size on top of each other and turn one by half a corner. You can try this yourself with paper.

**Arabesques** are patterns of tendrils, leaves and flowers. They wind into one another and seem to grow on endlessly. Often they fill the areas between bands of script or geometric shapes. In this way nature, mathematics and script combine into a whole.

Many walls are covered with **tiles** of fired clay. The tiles are painted and **glazed**, which is why they shine. A **mosaic**, by contrast, is made of many small stones or pieces of glass. In the **Dome of the Rock** in Jerusalem too there are magnificent mosaics.

A special decoration is the **muqarnas**. These are many small niches arranged one above another. They look like **honeycombs** or **stalactites**. You find them on ceilings, domes and arches, for example in the **Alhambra** in Spain.

gewusst: From two twisted squares a star with eight points arises.
The muqarnas in the Alhambra recall stalactites in a cave.

teile.einleitung: Islamic feminism is a movement that campaigns for equal rights for women. In doing so it argues from within Islam and draws on its sources. Its representatives read the Quran anew and criticise interpretations that are hostile to women.
wichtigste: Islamic feminists argue with the Quran, not against it.
They distinguish between the Quran and later patriarchal interpretations.
Amina Wadud wrote the book “Qur'an and Woman” in 1992.
Fatima Mernissi of Morocco wrote “The Veil and the Male Elite”.
In 1923 Huda Sha'arawi publicly took off her face veil in Cairo.
The movement Musawah was founded in 2009 in Kuala Lumpur.

abschnitte.text: The most important method of Islamic feminists is a **gender-just reinterpretation** of the Quran. They distinguish between the text of the Quran and the **patriarchal interpretations** of later scholars. Patriarchal means that men are favoured. The American theologian **Amina Wadud** read the Quran from the point of view of women in her 1992 book “Qur'an and Woman”. In 2005 she led a Friday prayer in New York in front of women and men, which caused a stir worldwide.

The Moroccan sociologist **Fatima Mernissi** wrote the book “The Political Harem” (in English “The Veil and the Male Elite”). She critically examined the origins of **hadiths** hostile to women, that is, transmitted sayings. In doing so she showed that women played an **active role** in the early period of Islam. Her work is still widely read and discussed today.

Already around 1900 there were debates about the role of women. The Egyptian author **Qasim Amin** published “The Liberation of Women” in 1899. He called for better **education** for women and criticised veiling. **Huda Sha'arawi** founded the **Egyptian Feminist Union** in 1923. In the same year she publicly took off her face veil at the railway station in Cairo, which became a symbol.

In **Malaysia** the group **Sisters in Islam** arose at the end of the 1980s. In 2009 the worldwide movement **Musawah** was founded in Kuala Lumpur, which means “equality” in Arabic. It campaigns for just **family laws** on the basis of Islamic sources. In Berlin **Seyran Ateş** founded the liberal **Ibn Rushd-Goethe Mosque** in 2017, where women and men pray together and women can lead the prayer. Many conservative scholars reject such innovations, which is why they are controversial.

gewusst: The mosque of Seyran Ateş is named after the philosopher Ibn Rushd and the poet Goethe.
Musawah means “equality” in Arabic.

teile.einleitung: Indonesia is a huge island state in South-East Asia. No other country in the world has so many Muslims. Even so, people of many other religions live together there too.
wichtigste: Indonesia is the country with the most Muslims in the world.
About 87 per cent of the people in Indonesia are Muslims (as of 2023).
Islam came mainly peacefully with traders across the sea.
In Aceh in the north of Sumatra, Islam first gained a foothold.
The foundation of the state is called Pancasila and has five principles.
The state officially recognises six religions.
The island of Bali is mostly Hindu.

abschnitte.text: Islam did not come to Indonesia through conquest but mainly through **traders**. Arab and Persian merchants sailed along the sea trade routes through the islands. They brought goods and their faith with them. Later came **scholars**, who spread Islam further. A gravestone from Lamreh in **Aceh** of 1211 is the earliest evidence of a Muslim ruler. After that the kingdom of **Samudera Pasai** arose there.

On the densely populated island of **Java**, nine scholars and preachers spread Islam in the 15th and 16th centuries. They are called the **Wali Songo**, the “nine saints”. They often combined the new faith with the local culture. Their graves are today important **places of pilgrimage** that many people visit.

The state ideology of Indonesia is called **Pancasila**. Sukarno, the first president, presented it in 1945. The first principle is **belief in one God**. The Pancasila does not prescribe a particular religion, however. Indonesia is therefore not an Islamic state, although most people are Muslims. Six religions are officially recognised: Islam, Protestantism, Catholicism, Hinduism, Buddhism and **Confucianism**.

Many Muslims in Indonesia are joined together in large organisations. The best known is **Nahdlatul Ulama**, founded in 1926 by scholars. It has over 30 million members and is among the largest Muslim organisations in the world. Such organisations run schools, help the needy and get involved in questions of society.

Besides Muslims, Christians, Hindus, Buddhists and Confucians live in Indonesia. On the island of **Bali**, **Hinduism** has held its ground, while the rest of the country became predominantly Muslim. In the capital **Jakarta** stands the **Istiqlal Mosque**, the largest mosque in South-East Asia. “Istiqlal” means “independence” and recalls the independence of the country.

gewusst: Over 230 million Muslims live in Indonesia, more than in any other state in the world (as of 2023).
The Istiqlal Mosque in Jakarta is the largest mosque in South-East Asia.
Confucianism was permitted again as a religion after the end of the Suharto era.

teile.einleitung: In the Andes in South America live peoples such as the Quechua and the Aymara. Their religion reveres the earth as a mother and the great mountains as powerful spirits. Today it is often combined with the Catholic faith.
wichtigste: Pachamama is regarded as “Mother Earth”.
In the Quechua tradition, the powerful mountain spirits are called Apus.
An offering bundle for the earth and the mountains is called a despacho.
August is regarded as a special month of Pachamama.
In the k’intu, three coca leaves are dedicated to the earth and the mountains.
The pilgrimage of Qoyllur Rit’i leads to a glacier on Mount Ausangate.

abschnitte.text: Many people in the Andes revere **Pachamama**, “Mother Earth”. She is seen as nourishing, but also as demanding: anyone who takes from her should also give something back. Before work in the fields and at festivals, people bring her offerings. In **August**, before sowing, the earth is regarded as “open” and hungry. That is why especially many offerings are brought to her at the start of the month.

In the Quechua tradition, the spirits of the great mountains are called **Apus**. They watch over water, herds and health. In rituals, people ask them for protection. In the time of the Incas, **Inti**, the sun god, was also worshipped, and Mama Quilla was regarded as the moon goddess. In Cusco, the sun festival **Inti Raymi** recalls this every June.

A **despacho** is an offering bundle wrapped in paper. It contains, for example, coca leaves, sweets, seeds and llama fat. It is usually burned or buried to thank the earth and the mountains. In the **k’intu**, people hold three fine **coca leaves** like a fan, breathe on them and dedicate them to the sacred powers. The idea of reciprocity, **ayni**, is also important: people help one another and give back what they have received.

Since the arrival of the Spanish, the Catholic faith has spread in the Andes. People often combine it with the old customs. One example is the pilgrimage of **Qoyllur Rit’i** near Cusco, which leads to a glacier on **Mount Ausangate**. It combines the worship of Christ with the honouring of sacred mountains and was recognised by UNESCO in 2011 as intangible cultural heritage. In La Paz in Bolivia, the **Alasitas** fair centres on the small good-luck figure **Ekeko**.

gewusst: At the Alasitas, people buy tiny houses, cars or banknotes and have them blessed so that their wishes come true.
Many people in the Andes let a few drops fall on the ground before drinking, as an offering for Pachamama.

teile.einleitung: The Taj Mahal is a magnificent tomb in the Indian city of Agra. The Mughal ruler Shah Jahan had it built for his late wife Mumtaz Mahal. The building of white marble is regarded as one of the most beautiful in the world.
wichtigste: The Taj Mahal stands in Agra in India, on the River Yamuna.
Shah Jahan had it built for his late wife Mumtaz Mahal.
It is a tomb, not a palace.
The outer shell is made mainly of white marble.
Four minarets surround the main building.
In 2007 it was chosen as one of the “New Seven Wonders of the World”.

abschnitte.text: The Taj Mahal is **a tomb**. The ruler **Shah Jahan** had it built for his **late wife**. She was called **Mumtaz Mahal** and died in the year 1631. Shah Jahan was deeply sad and had a unique monument put up for her. Later he himself was buried next to her.

When the Taj Mahal was built, Agra belonged to the **Mughal Empire**. The Mughal rulers were Muslims and governed large parts of India. Building began soon after the death of Mumtaz Mahal and lasted many years. Thousands of craftsmen worked on it. The architecture combines Persian, Indian and Islamic forms.

The gleaming outer shell is made mainly of **white marble**. Depending on the time of day it looks pink, golden or white. Coloured stones representing flowers are inlaid in the marble. Verses from the Quran in beautiful script also decorate the walls. The main building is surrounded by **four minarets**.

The Taj Mahal stands on the **River Yamuna**. In front of the tomb stretches a large garden with pools of water in which the building is reflected. Since 1983 it has been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. In **2007** it was chosen in a worldwide vote as one of the **“New Seven Wonders of the World”**. Millions of people visit it every year.

gewusst: The four minarets lean slightly outwards so that in an earthquake they would not fall on the tomb.
The name “Taj Mahal” is often translated as “Crown of the Palace”.

teile.einleitung: Sunnis and Shia are the two largest groups in Islam. They separated over the question of who should lead the community after Muhammad's death. Both believe in God, the Quran and Muhammad as a prophet.
wichtigste: The split arose above all over the question of Muhammad's successor.
“Shia” originally means “party of Ali”.
The name “Sunnis” is derived from the sunna.
The Sunnis form the great majority of Muslims worldwide.
In Iran the Shia form the great majority.
The largest group within the Shia are the Twelvers.

abschnitte.text: After Muhammad's death in the year 632, the question arose **who his successor** should be. A majority chose Abu Bakr as the first caliph. Others thought that **Ali**, Muhammad's cousin and son-in-law, should lead the community. From this dispute two branches developed. Ali later became the fourth caliph.

The name **Shia** comes from “Shiat Ali” and means **“party of Ali”**. The name **Sunnis** is derived from the **sunna**, the transmitted way of life of Muhammad. The **Sunnis** form the **great majority** of Muslims worldwide. The Shia are a minority, but in **Iran** they are the great majority. Many Shia also live in Iraq.

In the year **661** **Muawiya** founded the dynasty of the **Umayyads**. His son Yazid later became caliph. **Husayn**, a grandson of Muhammad and son of Ali, did not recognise him. He was killed at **Karbala** in **680**. On the day of remembrance **Ashura**, the Shia recall his death every year.

The Shia follow **imams**, special leaders from the family of Ali. The largest group are the **Twelver Shia**, who recognise twelve imams. Despite the differences, Sunnis and Shia have much in common. Both pray, fast in Ramadan and make the pilgrimage to Mecca. In Switzerland both groups live, and most Muslims here are Sunnis.

gewusst: Sunnis too revere Ali as the fourth caliph and a close relative of the Prophet.
Sunnis and Shia often pray in the same directions and with very similar prayers.

teile.einleitung: The Mahmood Mosque in Zurich is regarded as the first purpose-built mosque in Switzerland. It was opened in 1963. You can recognise it from afar by its minaret.
wichtigste: The Mahmood Mosque stands on Forchstrasse in Zurich.
It was opened in June 1963.
It belongs to the Ahmadiyya community.
It is regarded as the first building in Switzerland built specifically as a mosque.
Its minaret is about 18 metres high.
The call to prayer is not made from the minaret.

abschnitte.text: Before the Mahmood Mosque, Muslims in Switzerland prayed only in **converted rooms**. The **Mahmood Mosque** was the first building erected specifically as a mosque. The foundation stone was laid in 1962, and the opening followed in **June 1963**. It stands in **Zurich**, the largest city in Switzerland, on **Forchstrasse**. This is an important arterial road in the direction of Forch.

The mosque was built by the Muslim community **Ahmadiyya**. Its missionaries came to Switzerland in 1946. The Mahmood Mosque is still their **centre** in Switzerland. The Ahmadiyya is a smaller community that in some countries is not recognised as Muslim by other Muslims.

The **minaret** is about **18 metres** high. In proportion to the small mosque it looks strikingly tall. At the top stands a **crescent moon**. The **call to prayer is not made** from the minaret, however. It is above all a **mark of recognition**. It also stayed standing after the minaret initiative was accepted in 2009, because that forbids only new minarets.

At the opening in 1963 **Muhammad Zafrulla Khan** was guest of honour. He was then **President of the UN General Assembly**. The Zurich city president **Emil Landolt** also took part in the celebration. For the **50th anniversary** in November 2013 the minaret was covered in **rainbow colours**. This was meant as a sign of peace and tolerance.

gewusst: At the opening the President of the UN General Assembly was a guest.
In 2013, for the anniversary, the minaret wore a covering in rainbow colours.

teile.einleitung: In Islam the Day of Judgement is the day on which God judges all people. The dead are raised, and the deeds of each person are weighed. Belief in it is one of the six articles of faith.
wichtigste: According to Islamic teaching, the dead are raised on the Day of Judgement.
People's deeds are measured with a scale.
Only God knows when this day will come.
Believers receive their book of deeds in the right hand.
The narrow bridge over hell is called Sirat.
The time between death and resurrection is called Barzakh.

abschnitte.text: According to Islamic teaching, life does not end with death. The time in between until the resurrection is called **Barzakh**. According to tradition, two angels, **Munkar and Nakir**, question the dead in the grave. They ask about God, about the Prophet and about faith. When the Day of Judgement will come, **only God** knows.

On the Day of Judgement **the dead are raised**. All people then stand before God. Their good and bad deeds are measured with a **scale**. Each person receives a **book of deeds** in which their life is written down. According to the Quran, believers receive it **in the right hand**.

According to Islamic tradition, all people must cross a narrow bridge. It is called **Sirat** and leads over hell. For some it is easy to cross, for others very hard. That depends on how they have lived. The image is meant to show how important a good life is.

In the Quran paradise is often called a **garden**, in Arabic Jannah. It is described with rivers, shade and peace. Hell is called Jahannam. Muslims believe that God is just and at the same time merciful. Belief in the Day of Judgement is meant to encourage people to do good in life.

gewusst: Judaism and Christianity too know the idea of a Last Judgement.
The word “Jannah” originally means “garden”.

teile.einleitung: The Basmala is a short sentence that Muslims say very often: “In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate”. In Arabic it begins with “Bismillah”. Almost all surahs of the Quran begin with it, as do many everyday activities.
wichtigste: The sentence is “In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate”.
It is called “Bismillah” or “Basmala” for short.
Almost all surahs begin with it, only the 9th surah does not.
Many Muslims say Bismillah before eating and at the start of a task.
After eating many say “Alhamdulillah”, which means “Thank God”.

abschnitte.text: In Arabic the sentence is **“Bismillahi r-rahmani r-rahim”**. Translated it means “In the name of God, the **Merciful**, the **Compassionate**”. Merciful means that God is kind and has pity. In books about Islam the sentence is called the **Basmala**. In everyday life many people simply say “Bismillah”.

The Quran has 114 surahs, that is, chapters. Almost every one begins with the Basmala, before the first verse. Only a single surah starts without it: the **9th surah**. In the first surah, the Fatiha, the Basmala even counts as the first verse in the usual count today. In another surah the sentence also occurs in the middle of the text.

Many Muslims say “Bismillah” **before eating**. In this way they begin the meal in the name of God. According to a tradition, anyone who has forgotten it can make up for it during the meal. Then one says “Bismillah awwalahu wa akhirahu”, which means “In the name of God at the beginning and at the end”. After eating one gives thanks with **“Alhamdulillah”**, which means “Thank God” or “Praise be to God”.

The Basmala is not said only when eating. Many Muslims say it at the **start of a task**, for example before a child begins homework. It is also often heard before a journey, when entering a house or before reading the Quran. With it, people ask for God's blessing on what they do.

gewusst: The Basmala is one of the most frequent sentences in Islamic calligraphy and decorates many mosques.
The sentence occurs 114 times in the Quran, as often as there are surahs.

teile.einleitung: A mosque is a house of prayer for Muslims. Here they pray together, hear the Friday sermon and learn the Quran. Mosques look different all over the world but have many parts in common.
wichtigste: The Arabic word “masjid” means “place of prostration”.
In the prayer hall people sit and pray on rugs.
The prayer niche, the mihrab, shows the direction to Mecca.
The raised pulpit is called the minbar.
Before prayer the faithful wash in a washroom.
In many mosques women and men pray in separate areas.

abschnitte.text: In Arabic the mosque is called **masjid**, which means “place of **prostration**”. In prayer Muslims kneel down and touch the ground with the forehead. A large mosque for the Friday prayer is also called a **jami**. From the word masjid, by way of Spanish, came our word “mosque”.

In the wall that points to **Mecca** there is a niche, the **mihrab**. It shows the direction of prayer. Next to it there is usually the **minbar**, a raised pulpit with steps. From there the preacher gives the sermon on Friday. Many mosques also have a tower, the **minaret**, from which the call to prayer used to be made.

Before prayer the faithful wash their hands, face, arms and feet. For this many mosques have a **washroom** or a fountain in the courtyard. Shoes are taken off before the prayer hall. Inside, everyone sits and prays on the **carpet**, and there are usually no chairs. In many mosques women and men pray in **separate areas**.

A mosque is also a meeting place. **Children** often learn here to read the **Quran** in Arabic. There are classes, conversations and shared meals, for example in Ramadan. Anyone who visits a mosque dresses modestly. Women usually wear a **headscarf** for this. Many mosques in Switzerland also invite guests on open days.

Many large mosques have an open courtyard, the **sahn**. In Persian architecture there is the **iwan**, a tall hall open to the courtyard with a large arch. From the ceiling there often hang **large chandeliers**. You do not see pictures of people and animals. The decoration is **calligraphy**, tiles and geometric patterns.

gewusst: The Prophet's Mosque in Medina was at the beginning a simple building of mud and palm trunks.
The mosque in Mecca around the Kaaba is the largest mosque in the world.

teile.einleitung: In Islam, Jibril is the angel who brought the revelation of the Quran to the Prophet Muhammad. In the Bible he is called Gabriel. He is regarded as one of the most important angels in Islam.
wichtigste: Jibril is the Arabic form of the name Gabriel.
According to Islamic teaching he brought Muhammad the Quran over about 23 years.
The first revelation took place in the Cave of Hira near Mecca.
According to Islamic teaching, angels are created from light.
Jibril accompanied Muhammad on the night journey to Jerusalem and into heaven.

abschnitte.text: **Jibril** is the Arabic form of the name **Gabriel**. He appears in the Bible and in the Quran as a **messenger of God**. According to Islamic teaching he brought the Prophet Muhammad the words of the Quran, piece by piece over about **23 years**. That is why he is called the angel of revelation.

Muhammad often withdrew to the **Cave of Hira** on a mountain near Mecca to reflect. There, according to tradition, Jibril appeared to him for the first time and brought the first revelation. Later he also accompanied Muhammad on the famous **night journey**: the Isra led to Jerusalem, and the ascension, the Miraj, from there into heaven.

Belief in angels is one of the foundations of Islam. According to tradition, angels are created from **light**, jinn from smokeless fire and human beings from clay. Besides Jibril there are other well-known angels. **Mikail** corresponds to the angel Michael and, according to tradition, makes the rain fall. **Israfil** will blow the trumpet at the end of time and announce the Day of Judgement.

A well-known story is called the **“Hadith of Jibril”**. In it a stranger in very **white clothing** comes to Muhammad and his companions. He asks about **Islam**, **Iman** and **Ihsan**, that is, about duties, faith and good conduct. Afterwards Muhammad explains that this was Jibril. The story briefly sums up the foundations of the faith.

gewusst: Jibril and Mikail are named together in the Quran in surah 2, verse 98.
The angel Gabriel is known in Judaism, Christianity and Islam.

teile.einleitung: In 1258 the Mongols under Hulagu conquered the city of Baghdad. Baghdad had for over 500 years been the capital of the Abbasid caliphs. With the conquest the caliphate in Baghdad ended, and the city lost its role as the centre of the Islamic world.
wichtigste: The Mongol commander Hulagu, a grandson of Genghis Khan, conquered Baghdad in February 1258.
Before that, in 1256, he had subdued the fortress of Alamut of the Nizaris.
The last Abbasid caliph, al-Mustasim, was executed.
Hulagu founded the empire of the Ilkhans in Iran and Iraq.
In 1295 the Ilkhan Ghazan converted to Islam.
In 1401 Timur laid waste to Baghdad again.

abschnitte.text: **Hulagu** was a grandson of **Genghis Khan**. He led a large Mongol army westwards. First he subdued in Iran the castles of the **Nizaris**, who are also called Assassins. Their fortress **Alamut** surrendered in 1256. After that he marched against **Baghdad**, the capital of the Abbasids.

After a short siege, Baghdad was taken in February **1258**. Many inhabitants lost their lives, and large parts of the city were destroyed, including libraries. The last caliph, **al-Mustasim**, surrendered and was executed. According to Mongol custom, the blood of a ruler was not to flow onto the ground. So, according to tradition, he was killed wrapped in a carpet. With this the **caliphate in Baghdad** ended.

Hulagu founded an empire of his own, the **Ilkhanate**. It covered Iran, Iraq and parts of Anatolia and lasted until about 1335. The Persian scholar **Nasir al-Din al-Tusi** entered Hulagu's service and directed the observatory of **Maragha**, an important centre of astronomy. In 1295 the Ilkhan **Ghazan** converted to Islam. His vizier **Rashid al-Din** wrote a great world history.

For centuries Baghdad had been regarded as a centre of science and trade. After 1258 the city did not recover for a long time. In **1401** it was laid waste again by the Central Asian conqueror **Timur**, also called Tamerlane. The centre of gravity of the Islamic world shifted to other cities such as Cairo.

gewusst: Already in 1260 the Mamluks from Egypt stopped the Mongol army at the battle of Ain Jalut.
The descendants of the Mongols in Iran themselves became Muslims and promoted art and science.

teile.einleitung: The adhan is the Islamic call to prayer. With it the muezzin calls Muslim women and men to prayer. In many countries it can be heard several times a day.
wichtigste: The call to prayer is called the adhan, the caller the muezzin.
The call begins with “Allahu akbar”, which means “God is great”.
It sounds before each of the five daily prayers.
Traditionally the muezzin calls from the minaret of a mosque.
The first muezzin is regarded as Bilal, a companion of Muhammad.

abschnitte.text: Muslims pray five times a day at fixed times. Before each prayer the **muezzin** calls the **adhan**. In the past he climbed the **minaret**, the tower of the mosque, so that he could be heard far away. Today in many countries the call is transmitted by loudspeaker. The muezzin calls in Arabic and with a special, sung melody.

The adhan begins with **“Allahu akbar”**. Allah is the Arabic word for God, and “Allahu akbar” means “God is great” or “God is greater”. Then follows the **declaration of faith**: there is no god but God, and Muhammad is his messenger. Then the muezzin calls: “Come to prayer” and “Come to salvation”. In the call early in the morning he adds: “Prayer is better than sleep.”

According to tradition, in Medina Muhammad chose **Bilal** as the first muezzin. Bilal was a former slave with a beautiful, loud voice. That is why he is still regarded as a model for all muezzins. Shortly before the prayer begins in the mosque, there is a second, shorter call, the **iqama**.

In Switzerland one hardly hears the adhan in the street, it is usually called only inside the mosque. Since 2009 the Federal Constitution has said that no new **minarets** may be built.
