The voters had accepted the minaret initiative at that time. Many Muslim women and men today also use apps that show them the prayer times.

gewusst: Because the prayer times follow the position of the sun, the adhan sounds somewhere around the earth almost without a break.
Many parents whisper the adhan into a newborn baby's ear.

teile.einleitung: The crescent moon plays an important role in Islam. The Islamic calendar follows the moon: a new month begins when the fine crescent is seen again after the new moon. The crescent is also a well-known sign on mosques and flags.
wichtigste: An Islamic month begins when the new, slender crescent moon is seen.
The new crescent moon is called hilal in Arabic.
From one new moon to the next takes about 29 and a half days.
People look for the crescent in the evening after sunset in the west.
If the crescent cannot be seen, the month lasts 30 days.
The flag of Turkey shows a white crescent and a star on red.

abschnitte.text: The moon does not shine by itself; it is lit by the sun. At **new moon** it stands between the Earth and the sun. Then it can be seen **hardly at all**. One to two days later a very fine **crescent** appears. In Arabic this new crescent moon is called **hilal**. From one new moon to the next takes about **29 and a half days**.

The **Islamic calendar** is a purely lunar calendar. A new month begins when the **hilal** is spotted in the sky. That is why a month has either 29 or 30 days. An Islamic year is about eleven days shorter than our solar year. That is why, for example, the fasting month of **Ramadan** begins a little earlier every year.

abschnitte.titel: The search in the evening sky
abschnitte.text: The young crescent moon stands close to the sun. It can be seen only briefly **in the evening after sunset**, low in the **west**. At the end of a month many people therefore look out for it. If **clouds** hide the crescent, the month is counted through to the **30th day**. Today some countries and communities also use astronomical calculations.

At the very top of many **domes** and **minarets** you see a crescent moon. It became a widespread sign above all in the **Ottoman Empire**. The flag of **Turkey** shows a white crescent with a star on a red ground. Countries such as Tunisia, Algeria or Pakistan also have a crescent in their flags. The sign is not a religious requirement, however.

The aid organisation **Red Cross** was founded in **Geneva**. In many Muslim countries its counterpart is called the **Red Crescent**. Both signs are internationally protected. They show that people are helping here who care for the wounded in wars and disasters. Together they form the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement.

gewusst: Because Ramadan begins about eleven days earlier every year, it moves once through all the seasons in about 33 years.
The hilal is sometimes so thin that it can be seen for only a few minutes.

teile.einleitung: Ijtihad is a concept from Islamic law. It describes the independent finding of a legal ruling by a scholar from the sources. The question of how much ijtihad is permitted has been debated for centuries.
wichtigste: Ijtihad literally means effort or endeavour.
A scholar who is qualified to do it is called a mujtahid.
The counterpart is taqlid, following a recognised opinion of a school.
In 1984 the historian Wael Hallaq doubted that the “gate of ijtihad” was closed.
Among the Twelver Shia, ijtihad is still regarded as open and important today.

abschnitte.titel: One's own judgement from the sources
abschnitte.text: The word **ijtihad** comes from the same root as jihad and means **effort** or **endeavour**. What is meant is the independent effort to reach a legal ruling from the Quran and sunna. A scholar who can do this is called a **mujtahid**. He must have a thorough command of Arabic, the Quran, hadith and legal method. A classic proof is a hadith about **Muadh ibn Jabal**. When Muhammad sent him to Yemen as a judge, Muadh is said to have said that he would make an effort to reach a judgement of his own if the Quran and sunna are silent.

The counterpart is called **taqlid**. In it people adopt the judgement of a scholar or a school of law. Whoever follows in this way is called a muqallid, and for lay people this is regarded as the normal path. For a long time research said that from about the 10th century the **“gate of ijtihad”** was closed. The historian **Wael Hallaq** criticised this thesis in 1984. He showed that scholars continued to judge independently afterwards.

Around 1900 the Egyptian reformer **Muhammad Abduh** called for a renewal of ijtihad. He was Mufti of Egypt and wanted to combine Islam with modern times. Among the **Twelver Shia**, ijtihad is still regarded as open. There believers follow a living mujtahid as the highest authority. In the 18th century the **Usulis** prevailed there over the Akhbaris, who wanted to rely solely on transmitted reports.

gewusst: High Shia scholars whom believers choose as a model are called a “source of emulation”.

teile.einleitung: Giving presents is part of the Islamic festivals. Especially popular are sweets and pastries, which people share with family, friends and neighbours. Children too are gladly given presents on the festival day.
wichtigste: Baklava is a pastry made of many wafer-thin layers of dough, nuts and syrup.
Baklava often contains chopped nuts, for example green pistachios.
Lokum is a soft sweet in small cubes.
Maamoul are festival biscuits with dates or nuts.
Children often get some money or sweets from relatives.
Many people also bring their neighbours a plate of pastries.

abschnitte.text: **Baklava** is made of many wafer-thin sheets of dough. Between them people scatter **chopped nuts**, often walnuts or green **pistachios**. After baking, the pastry is drenched in sweet syrup. It is crisp and very sweet. Baklava is popular in Turkey, in the Balkans and in the Middle East, and in Switzerland too you can buy it.

**Lokum** is a soft, sweet treat in small cubes. It often tastes of roses or lemon and is dusted with icing sugar. **Halva** is often made from sesame paste and sugar. It is sweet and crumbles easily in the mouth. Both sweets are gladly given in pretty boxes.

In the Middle East people bake **maamoul**. These are round biscuits of semolina or flour, filled with dates or nuts. They are pressed in decorated wooden moulds. In Pakistan and India, **sheer khurma** is part of the festival breakfast. This sweet dish is cooked from fine noodles, milk, sugar and dates.

Children are especially spoiled on the festival day. From relatives they often get some **pocket money** or sweets. Many families bring their **neighbours** a plate of pastries, even if these have a different religion. Some send **greeting cards** or messages. On them a crescent moon and stars are often painted.

gewusst: For maamoul there are carved wooden moulds so that every biscuit gets a beautiful pattern.
Sharing with others is regarded in Islam as a good deed, so at the festival people also think of the poor.

teile.einleitung: Amen is a word that Christians say at the end of a prayer. It comes from Hebrew and means “So be it”. It is also known in Judaism and Islam.
wichtigste: Amen is said at the end of a prayer.
The word comes from Hebrew.
It means “So be it” or “Yes, truly”.
By saying Amen, people agree to a prayer or blessing.
Jews and Muslims also know the word; in Islam it is Amin.

abschnitte.text: When Christians finish a prayer, they say **Amen**. The word comes from **Hebrew**, the language of the Jewish Bible. It is related to a word for “firm” or “reliable”. That is why Amen means something like **“So be it”** or “Yes, truly”. Whoever says Amen confirms the prayer and makes it their own.

In a **church service**, the priest or minister often says a prayer or blessing. The congregation answers together with **Amen**. In this way everyone shows that they agree. The well-known prayer, the **Lord’s Prayer**, also ends with Amen. Many children also say Amen after grace at the table or the evening prayer.

In the Bible, Amen appears often. Jesus begins some important statements with “Amen, I say to you”, in many translations “Truly, I say to you”. In this way he stresses that his words are true. The last book of the Bible also ends with Amen. Because the word is so well known, it was taken into many languages without being translated.

Amen does not belong to Christianity alone. In **Judaism**, people answer prayers and blessings with Amen. In **Islam** people say **Amin**, for example after the first sura of the Koran during prayer. In this way this small word links three religions.

gewusst: Amen is one of the best-known words in the world and is said almost the same way in very many languages.
In German there is the saying “as sure as the Amen in church” for something that will certainly happen.

teile.einleitung: In Islam it is forbidden to eat pork. The ban is in the Quran and applies to all products from pigs. In Judaism too pork is not permitted.
wichtigste: The Quran forbids the eating of pork.
The ban also applies to wild boar.
Bacon, lard and gelatine from pigs are also forbidden.
Anyone who would otherwise starve may eat pork.
Judaism too forbids pork.
School kitchens often offer a meal without pork.

abschnitte.text: In the **Quran** it is said in several places that Muslims should not eat pork. Permitted foods are called **halal**, forbidden ones **haram**. The ban applies to all pigs, including the **wild boar**. Many Muslims keep to it very strictly. Other kinds of meat such as beef, lamb or chicken are permitted if the animal was slaughtered according to the rules.

Many foods come from the pig: **bacon**, ham, **lard** and many kinds of sausage such as most **salami**. It becomes difficult with hidden ingredients. Ordinary **gummy bears** often contain **gelatine from pigs**. That is why there are gummy bears with gelatine from cattle or with no gelatine at all. Instead of pork ham, many Muslims eat **turkey ham** or beef ham.

The Quran knows an important exception. If someone would otherwise **starve** and has nothing else, he may eat pork. Saving life is then more important than the food rule. This rule shows that protecting life has a high value in Islam.

In **Judaism** too pork is forbidden, and it is regarded there as not kosher. In Switzerland people of many religions live together. Many **school kitchens** and canteens therefore offer a **meal without pork** or a vegetarian meal. On packaging, the list of ingredients helps to recognise products from pigs.

gewusst: Some cakes, yoghurts and sweets can also contain gelatine from pigs.
The food ban on pork is also in the Torah, the holy book of Judaism.

teile.einleitung: Zakat is a compulsory donation in Islam. Anyone who has enough money or property gives a small part of it every year to poor people. It is one of the five pillars of Islam.
wichtigste: Zakat is one of the five pillars of Islam, alongside the declaration of faith, prayer, fasting and pilgrimage.
One gives it once a year.
Usually one gives 2.5 per cent of one's savings, that is, 1 franc out of every 40 francs.
Only someone who owns more than a certain amount has to give zakat.
The money is meant for the poor and for people in need.
Voluntary donations are called sadaqa.

abschnitte.text: In Islam there are five important duties, called the **pillars of Islam**. They include the declaration of faith, the daily prayer, fasting in Ramadan, the pilgrimage to Mecca and **zakat**. The word means roughly **purification** or **growth**. Anyone who gives is, so to speak, to purify their wealth. At the same time zakat helps to make things fairer in the community.

Only someone who owns more than a certain minimum amount has to give zakat. This limit is called the **nisab**. Anyone above it usually gives **2.5 per cent** of their savings, that is, one franc out of every 40 francs. With 4,000 francs that is 100 francs. Zakat is calculated and given **once a year**. Very poor people do not have to give anything, they receive zakat.

The money is meant for the **poor** and for people in need. The Quran names several groups who may receive zakat, for example the poor, the needy, people in debt and travellers without money. Many Muslims give zakat through a mosque or an aid organisation, others give it directly to people they know.

At the end of the fasting month of **Ramadan** there is a special donation, the **zakat al-fitr**. One usually gives food or money so that the poor too can celebrate the festival of the breaking of the fast. Besides the compulsory donations there is the voluntary donation **sadaqa**. One can give it as often as one likes. A well-known saying of Muhammad says that even a **smile** for another person is a good gift.

gewusst: In some countries the state collects zakat, in most countries people give it themselves.
Because the Islamic calendar is a lunar calendar, many calculate zakat by the lunar year, which is a little shorter than our year.

teile.einleitung: In Islam, alcohol is forbidden. The Koran prohibits intoxicating drinks, so devout Muslims do not drink alcohol. Many also make sure that there is no alcohol in their food.
wichtigste: The Koran forbids intoxicating drinks.
That is why devout Muslims do not drink alcohol.
What is allowed in Islam is called halal, and what is forbidden is called haram.
Many Muslims also avoid foods that contain alcohol.
In some countries alcohol is banned by law, in others it is not.

abschnitte.text: In the **Koran**, intoxicating drinks are forbidden. The Arabic word for them is **khamr**. According to tradition, the ban came in stages: first it was said that wine does more harm than good, and later came the clear ban. The reason given is that drunkenness clouds the mind and keeps people from prayer. That is why devout Muslims do not drink alcohol.

In Islam, a distinction is made between **halal**, which means allowed, and **haram**, which means forbidden. Alcohol is among the forbidden things. Many Muslims therefore also make sure that there is no alcohol in food, sauces or sweets. At celebrations there is then tea, juices and other alcohol-free drinks.

In countries shaped by Islam, the ban is handled in different ways. In some states, for example **Saudi Arabia**, alcohol is banned by law. In other countries it can be bought, but many people do not drink it for religious reasons. How strictly someone follows the ban is a personal decision for each believer.

Many Muslims in Switzerland do without alcohol. In Switzerland, **youth protection** rules apply to all young people anyway: in most cantons, beer and wine may only be sold from the age of 16, and spirits only from 18. Many people of other religions, or of no religion, do not drink alcohol either, for example for health reasons.

gewusst: Arab scholars in the Middle Ages studied distillation, and the word “alcohol” comes from Arabic.
During Ramadan, Muslims give up eating and drinking completely during the day, but alcohol is forbidden all year round.

teile.einleitung: Musa is the name of Moses in the Quran. He is one of the most important prophets in Islam, as in Judaism and Christianity. No other prophet is named by name so often in the Quran.
wichtigste: Moses is called Musa in the Quran.
Musa is the prophet who is named by name most often in the Quran.
His mother put him as a baby in a box on the Nile.
The wife of the pharaoh found him and took him in.
His brother Harun helped him.
According to Islam, Musa received the Torah.

abschnitte.text: At the time of Musa's birth the **Israelites** lived in Egypt and were oppressed by the **pharaoh**. According to the Quran, God inspired Musa's mother to put her baby in a **box** and set it on the **Nile**. The box drifted as far as the palace. There the **pharaoh's wife** found it and took the boy in. So Musa grew up, of all places, at the pharaoh's court.

As an adult Musa lived for some years far from Egypt. One day he saw a **fire** on a mountain. There God spoke to him and made him a prophet. That is why Musa is also called in Islam the one “with whom God spoke”. God commanded him to throw down his **staff**, and the staff became a **snake**. His brother **Harun** was to stand by him as a helper.

Musa and Harun went to the pharaoh and demanded that he let the people go. The pharaoh refused. Finally Musa led his people out of Egypt. When they came to the **sea**, Musa struck the water with the staff, and the sea **parted**. The people could pass through, but the pharaoh's pursuers drowned.

According to Islam, Musa received a holy scripture from God, the **Torah**. The Quran calls it a light and a guidance for people. Musa is named by name in the Quran more often than any other prophet, **more than a hundred times**. His story is told in many surahs, sometimes briefly, sometimes at length.

gewusst: Musa is named by name in the Quran much more often than Muhammad himself.
In Islamic tradition the wife of the pharaoh who rescued Musa is called Asiya.

teile.einleitung: The Alhambra is a magnificent fortress and palace complex in Granada in southern Spain. It was built by Muslim rulers and is regarded as a masterpiece of Islamic architecture. Today very many people from all over the world visit it every year.
wichtigste: The Alhambra stands in Granada in Spain.
The name comes from the Arabic “al-hamra” and means “the red one”.
The palaces were built by the ruling Nasrid family.
In the Court of the Lions, twelve marble lions support a fountain.
Next to the Alhambra lie the gardens of the Generalife.
In 1492 the surrender of Granada ended Muslim rule in Spain.

abschnitte.text: The Alhambra lies on a hill above the city of **Granada**. It is a large complex of walls, towers and palaces. The name comes from the Arabic **“al-hamra”**, which means “the red one”. The walls glow reddish in the sun. In the past the Muslim rulers of Granada lived here with their court.

The ruling family of the **Nasrids** governed the emirate of Granada from the 13th century until 1492. In this time the magnificent palaces were built. Their walls are decorated with fine patterns of stucco, coloured tiles and Arabic script. Wooden ceilings and domes are elaborately carved.

Most famous is the **Court of the Lions**. There **twelve lions** of marble support a fountain basin, and water flows from their mouths. Everywhere in the Alhambra there are fountains, channels and water basins. The water cools in the hot summer and splashes soothingly. Right beside it lie the gardens of the **Generalife**, a summer residence of the rulers.

On 2 January **1492**, the last emir handed Granada over to the **Catholic Monarchs** Ferdinand and Isabella. This ended Muslim rule on the Iberian Peninsula, which had lasted about 780 years. Later the Christian rulers built a palace of their own in the Alhambra. Today the complex is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

gewusst: On the walls of the Alhambra the sentence “There is no victor but God” appears many hundreds of times.
In the 19th century the American Washington Irving made the Alhambra famous in Europe with his stories.

teile.einleitung: An arabesque is an ornament of curving tendrils, leaves and flowers. It is typical of Islamic art and decorates mosques, palaces and books. The word is also used in music and in ballet.
wichtigste: Arabesques mostly show tendrils, leaves and flowers.
The word comes from the Italian “arabesco”, which means “Arabic”.
An arabesque can be continued without beginning or end.
Robert Schumann and Claude Debussy wrote piano pieces called “Arabesque”.
In ballet the arabesque is a pose on one leg.

abschnitte.text: An arabesque consists mainly of curving **plant forms**. Tendrils, leaves and flowers seem to grow endlessly into one another. The pattern has no fixed beginning and no end and can be continued in every direction. Many interpret this as a reference to the **infinity of God**. In mosques, people or animals are usually not depicted, so patterns and script are especially important there.

The word comes from Italian: **“arabesco”** means “Arabic”. Europeans used it for the decoration they knew from Islamic art. From the Renaissance, European artists also decorated walls, furniture and books with such tendril patterns.

Besides plant tendrils, Islamic art also has **geometric patterns**. The **girih** are band patterns of crossing lines that form stars and polygons. Girih means “knot” in Persian. In **Morocco** there is **zellige**: colourful mosaics of hand-cut clay tiles. They decorate fountains, walls and floors.

Pieces of music too can be playful and intertwined like the ornament. **Robert Schumann** composed his “Arabeske” for piano in 1839. The Frenchman **Claude Debussy** wrote two arabesques in his youth, which are among his best-known pieces. In **ballet** the arabesque is a pose: the dancer stands on one leg and stretches the other far backwards.

gewusst: Some old girih patterns follow such subtle rules that mathematicians were able to describe them exactly only in the 20th century.
The arabesque in ballet is so called because its long, sweeping line recalls the ornament.

teile.einleitung: The Ismailis are a branch of faith within Shia Islam. They arose from a dispute over who should be the rightful imam. The best-known group today is the Nizaris, with the Aga Khan as their head.
wichtigste: The Ismailis recognise Ismail ibn Jafar as the seventh imam.
The Ismaili Fatimids founded Cairo in 969.
In 1094 the Ismailis split into Nizaris and Mustalis.
The fortress of Alamut was the centre of the Nizaris from 1090.
Karim Aga Khan IV was born in Geneva in 1936.
Since February 2025 Rahim Al-Hussaini has been imam of the Nizaris as Aga Khan V.

abschnitte.text: After the death of the imam **Jafar al-Sadiq**, the Shia disputed over his succession. The **Ismailis** followed the line of his son **Ismail**. The **Twelver Shia**, the largest Shia group, followed Musa al-Kazim instead. That is how the Ismailis got their name.

An Ismaili dynasty were the **Fatimids**. They conquered Egypt in 969 and founded **Cairo** as a new capital. There they also founded the **al-Azhar Mosque**. After the death of the caliph **al-Mustansir** in 1094 there was a dispute: some supported his son **Nizar**, others his brother **al-Mustali**. In this way the **Nizaris** and the **Mustalis** arose. From the circle of the Fatimids the **Druze** also emerged in the 11th century, who today are a religious community of their own.

**Hasan-i Sabbah** took the mountain fortress of **Alamut** in present-day Iran in 1090. From there he built up a Nizari state with many castles. In 1256 the **Mongols** conquered the fortress. The Nizaris afterwards lived on scattered in various countries.

The title **Aga Khan** was given to Hasan Ali Shah in the 19th century by the **Persian Shah**. He later moved to British India. **Karim Aga Khan IV** was born in **Geneva** in 1936 and partly grew up in Switzerland. He led the Nizaris from 1957 to 2025, almost 68 years. After his death on 4 February 2025, his eldest son **Rahim Al-Hussaini** became the 50th imam as **Aga Khan V**.

The Mustalis also still exist. A well-known community are the **Dawoodi Bohras** with their centre in **Mumbai** in India. The Indian **Khojas**, by contrast, belong for the most part to the Nizaris. Ismailis live today in many countries of Asia, Africa, Europe and America.

gewusst: Karim Aga Khan IV was born in Geneva.
Al-Azhar in Cairo was founded by an Ismaili dynasty.

teile.einleitung: The Islamic calendar follows not the sun but the moon. That is why an Islamic year is shorter than our year. Festivals such as Ramadan therefore move slowly through all the seasons.
wichtigste: The Islamic calendar is a lunar calendar.
It has 12 months, and a year lasts about 354 days.
The Islamic year is about 11 days shorter than our year.
The first month is called Muharram, the ninth is Ramadan.
A new day begins at sunset.
The counting of the years begins in the 7th century AD.

abschnitte.text: Every month in the Islamic calendar begins with a **new moon**. That is why it is called a **lunar calendar**. Like our calendar it has **twelve months**. A lunar month, however, is only about 29 to 30 days long. Together this gives a year of about **354 days**, so about eleven days fewer than a solar year.

The Islamic year begins with the month of **Muharram**. On the first day the Islamic New Year is celebrated. The **ninth month** is **Ramadan**, the fasting month. It is the best-known month of the year. The **twelfth month** is called **Dhu al-Hijja**. In it the great pilgrimage to Mecca takes place.

Because the lunar year is shorter, Ramadan begins in our calendar **about eleven days earlier every year**. So it falls sometimes in summer and sometimes in winter. After about **33 years** it is in the same season again. In summer the fast is longer in Switzerland, because the days stay light for longer.

In the Islamic calendar a new day begins not at midnight but **at sunset**. That is why some festivals are already celebrated on the **evening before**. In the Jewish calendar too the day begins in the evening.

The Islamic counting of years begins only in the **7th century** AD. That is why the year number is much smaller than ours. In summer 2026, for example, the Islamic year **1448** began. Because the years are shorter, the Islamic count very slowly catches up with ours.

gewusst: Ramadan moves once through all the seasons in about 33 years.
In summer 2026 the Islamic year 1448 began.

teile.einleitung: Kalam is Islamic theology that works with arguments of reason. Its representatives defended articles of faith in debates. It dealt with big questions such as God's attributes and the free will of human beings.
wichtigste: Kalam literally means “speech”.
The representatives of kalam are called mutakallimun.
Many mutakallimun held an atomic doctrine with constant re-creation.
The Jabriyya taught strict predestination, the Qadariyya free will.
The Murji'a left the judgement on grave sinners to God.
Al-Maturidi of Samarkand founded a Sunni school of theology.

abschnitte.text: **Kalam** literally means “speech”. What is meant is a theology that defends articles of faith with **arguments of reason**. Its representatives are called **mutakallimun**, the “speakers” or debaters. They discussed, for example, **God's attributes** and **free will**. Kalam is still taught today at Islamic theological faculties.

Many mutakallimun had a special doctrine of nature. The world, they held, consists of **smallest parts**, that is, atoms, and their properties, the **accidents**. God creates these **anew in every moment**. With this they wanted to show that everything in the world constantly depends on God.

A great point of dispute was whether human beings act freely. The **Jabriyya** taught that human beings have no will of their own and that **God determines all deeds**. Jabr means compulsion. The **Qadariyya**, by contrast, upheld the **free will** of human beings. The early movement **Murji'a** wanted to **leave** the judgement on grave sinners **to God**. Its name comes from “irja”, to postpone, until the Last Judgement.

An important Sunni school is named after **Abu Mansur al-Maturidi**. He worked in **Samarkand** and died in 944. His school is closely linked to the **Hanafi** school of law. The scholar **al-Ghazali** wrote the work “The Incoherence of the Philosophers” against teachings such as the eternity of the world. **Ibn Rushd** later replied with “The Incoherence of the Incoherence”.

gewusst: Ibn Rushd answered al-Ghazali's polemic with a book whose title took up the title of his opponent.
Already in the Middle Ages, Muslim theologians thought about atoms.

teile.einleitung: Wudu is the name of the small ritual washing that Muslim women and men perform before prayer. In it certain parts of the body are washed with water in a fixed order. The washing is meant to make one clean outwardly and inwardly.
wichtigste: Wudu is the washing before prayer in Islam.
One begins with the hands, then follow the mouth, nose, face, arms, head and feet.
The arms are washed up to the elbows, the feet up to the ankles.
Usually one washes the right side first, then the left.
Much is washed three times.
Without water one may do a substitute washing with clean earth, the tayammum.

abschnitte.text: In Islam one should be clean when one stands before God and prays. The washing is called **wudu** in Arabic. It is an outer cleansing with water, but is also meant to prepare the heart for prayer. At the start one silently forms the **intention** to wash for prayer. Many say “Bismillah” with it, “in the name of God”.

First one washes the **hands**, usually three times and with the right hand first. Then one takes some water into the **mouth** and rinses it. After that one cleans the **nose** with water. This too is often done three times each. Then one washes the whole **face** from the forehead to the chin.

Now one washes the **arms** from the fingertips to the elbows, the right one first. The head is not washed completely: one passes wet hands over the **hair**, and many also clean the ears at this point. Last one washes the **feet** up to the ankles, again right first. After that one is ready for prayer.

The washing counts until it is cancelled, for example by going to the toilet or by sleep. That is why in many **mosques** there are fountains or washrooms, including in mosques in Switzerland. Where there is no water, a substitute washing is allowed: in the **tayammum** one touches clean earth or sand and passes it over the face and hands. Besides wudu there is also a great washing of the whole body, called **ghusl**.

gewusst: Many mosques have a fountain in their courtyard at which one can do the washing.
The tayammum shows that in Islam it is not water alone that counts, but also the readiness to pray.

teile.einleitung: Ibn Sina was one of the most important scholars of the Islamic world. He lived around the year 1000 and was a doctor and philosopher. In Europe he is known under the name Avicenna.
wichtigste: Ibn Sina lived from about 980 to 1037.
He was born in a village near Bukhara, which today lies in Uzbekistan.
In Europe he is called Avicenna.
His “Canon of Medicine” was a textbook in Europe until the 17th century.
His great philosophical work is called the “Book of Healing”.
Even as a child he is said to have known the Quran by heart.

abschnitte.titel: A child prodigy from Central Asia
abschnitte.text: Ibn Sina was born around **980** in a village near **Bukhara**. Bukhara lies today in **Uzbekistan** in Central Asia. In his autobiography he reports that at about ten years old he knew the whole **Quran by heart**. After that he studied logic, mathematics and medicine. Already as a young man he treated the sick. He died in **1037**.

Ibn Sina was a famous **doctor**. He worked for several rulers in Persia. His most important medical book is the **“Canon of Medicine”**. In it he summed up the medical knowledge of his time, including from Greek sources. He described illnesses, remedies and how to stay healthy.

Ibn Sina was also one of the most important **philosophers** of his time. His great work is called the **“Book of Healing”**, in Arabic **Kitab al-Shifa**. What is meant is the healing of the soul from ignorance. In it he deals with logic, natural science, mathematics and metaphysics. He built on Aristotle and developed his thoughts further.

In the Middle Ages Arabic names were often **Latinised**. In this way Ibn Sina became **Avicenna**. In the **12th century** Gerard of Cremona translated the Canon in Spain into **Latin**, the language of science in Europe. After that medical students at European universities learned from this book for over 500 years. Only in the **17th century** did it lose importance with the new medicine.

gewusst: Ibn Sina wrote over 100 works, among them poems.
In Hamadan in Iran there stands a large tomb for him.

teile.einleitung: “Salam” is the Arabic word for peace. It is in the greeting “Salam alaykum”, with which many Muslims all over the world greet one another. The greeting is a wish for peace and well-being.
wichtigste: “Salam alaykum” means “Peace be upon you”.
The reply is “Wa alaykum salam”, that is, “And upon you be peace”.
People say the greeting on meeting, or for short just “Salam”.
Related to “salam” is the Hebrew greeting “shalom”.
At the end of prayer Muslims speak the greeting of peace to the right and to the left.
“Ma'a salama” is an Arabic farewell.

abschnitte.text: Many Muslims greet one another with **“as-salamu alaykum”**, often said briefly as **“Salam alaykum”**. In English this means “Peace be upon you”. With it you wish the other person peace and well-being. Among friends a short **“Salam”** is often enough. You hear the greeting in Arab countries, in Turkey, in Pakistan and also in Switzerland.

To “Salam alaykum” you reply **“Wa alaykum salam”**. This means “And upon you be peace”. In this way both give each other the same good wish. In Islam it is regarded as polite and important to return a greeting. Some add longer blessings, for example for God's mercy.

The greeting of peace also plays a part in prayer. At the end of the prayer Muslims turn the head first to the right and then to the left. Each time they speak the **greeting of peace**. It is addressed to the people and angels on both sides. With this the prayer is concluded.

Arabic and Hebrew are related languages. That is why “salam” is similar to the Hebrew **“shalom”**, which also means peace and serves as a greeting. For farewell, in Arabic you say **“Ma'a salama”**, which means roughly “Go with peace” and is used like “goodbye”. The name of the city of Dar es Salaam in Tanzania also contains the word; it means “house of peace”.

gewusst: The word “Islam” has the same Arabic root as “salam”.
“Salam” and “shalom” come from related languages and both mean peace.

teile.einleitung: Ibn Battuta was a traveller from Morocco who in the 14th century saw a large part of the world known at that time. His journey began as a pilgrimage to Mecca and lasted almost a quarter of a century. His travel account is still an important source today.
wichtigste: Ibn Battuta was born in 1304 in Tangier in present-day Morocco.
In 1325 he set out on the pilgrimage to Mecca.
He travelled over 100,000 kilometres; experts estimate about 117,000.
In Delhi he worked for several years as a judge.
He dictated his travel account, the “Rihla”, after his return.
On his last great journey he visited the Mali Empire in West Africa.

abschnitte.text: Ibn Battuta was born in **1304** in **Tangier**. The city lies on the north coast of Africa in present-day Morocco. At 21 years old, in **1325**, he left his homeland. He wanted to make the **Hajj**, the pilgrimage to Mecca. After that, out of curiosity, he travelled on and on. Only about 24 years later did he return home.

abschnitte.titel: A journey round half the world
abschnitte.text: Ibn Battuta travelled through North Africa, the Middle East, Persia and East Africa. He visited Central Asia, India and South-East Asia and, by his own account, got as far as China. Experts estimate his route at about **117,000 kilometres**. That is almost three times round the Earth. He travelled on foot, on camels, on horses and on ships. In this way he travelled further than almost anyone before modern times.

In India there then ruled a Muslim **sultan in Delhi**. He appointed Ibn Battuta as a judge, a so-called **qadi**. Ibn Battuta had studied Islamic law. As a scholar he was well received at many courts. He stayed in India for about eight years.

On his last great journey he crossed the **Sahara** in **1352**. He visited the rich **Mali Empire** in West Africa. There he described, among other things, the city of **Timbuktu**. After that he returned for good to Morocco.

After his return Ibn Battuta told of his travels. A scholar wrote everything down. In this way the travel account **“Rihla”** came about, the Arabic word for “journey”. The book describes cities, rulers, customs and landscapes. For historians it is a valuable source on the 14th century.

gewusst: Ibn Battuta travelled even further than Marco Polo, who lived about 50 years before him.
In Dubai a large shopping centre bears his name.

teile.einleitung: The battle of Karbala took place in the year 680 in present-day Iraq. In it Husayn ibn Ali, a grandson of the Prophet Muhammad, fell. The event is of the greatest importance for the Shia to this day.
wichtigste: The battle took place in the year 680.
Husayn ibn Ali, a grandson of Muhammad, fell in the battle.
He fought against the troops of the caliph Yazid I.
Karbala lies in present-day Iraq.
His half-brother al-Abbas ibn Ali also has an important shrine in Karbala.

abschnitte.text: After Muhammad's death, Muslims disputed over who should lead the community. In the year 680 **Yazid I** of the Umayyad family became caliph. **Husayn ibn Ali**, son of Ali and grandson of Muhammad, did not recognise him. Supporters in Kufa in present-day Iraq invited him. Husayn set out with his family and a few companions.

At **Karbala** the small group was stopped by a large army of Yazid. On the 10th day of the month of Muharram, in the year **680**, the battle took place. Husayn and almost all his male companions fell. Among them was his half-brother **al-Abbas ibn Ali**, who carried the banner. Women and children were taken prisoner.

In Karbala today stand the shrines of **Husayn** and **al-Abbas**. The city is one of the most important places of pilgrimage for the Shia. Every year the Shia remember Husayn's death on **Ashura**, the 10th of Muharram. There are mourning gatherings, sermons and processions. For the Shia, Husayn is a model of courage and loyalty to justice.

The battle deepened the division between **Sunnis** and **Shia**. For the Shia it is a central event of their history and faith. Sunnis too mourn the death of the Prophet's grandson. To this day the memory of Karbala shapes the art, poetry and religious festivals of many Muslims.

gewusst: Karbala is visited by millions of pilgrims every year.
The shrines of Husayn and al-Abbas stand only a few hundred metres from one another.

teile.einleitung: Muslims in Switzerland come from very many countries. Most families came from the 1960s as workers or refugees. Today many of them hold a Swiss passport.
wichtigste: According to the 2000 census, the Muslims of Switzerland came from 105 states.
In 2000, 58 per cent came from the former Yugoslavia and 21 per cent from Turkey.
At that time only 11 per cent had Swiss nationality.
In the years 2019 to 2023 about 37 per cent were Swiss citizens.
About 31 per cent held the nationality of a Balkan state.

abschnitte.text: In the **boom years**, the Swiss economy looked for workers abroad. From the **1960s** many people also came from **Turkey** and **Yugoslavia**. Later their families followed. In the 1990s many people fled to Switzerland from the wars in the Balkans. According to the 2000 census, the Muslims of Switzerland came from **105 states**.

abschnitte.titel: The most important regions of origin
abschnitte.text: In 2000, **58 per cent** of Muslims came from the **former Yugoslavia**. The Historical Dictionary of Switzerland names above all **Albanians** from Kosovo and Macedonia as well as **Bosniaks** from Bosnia and Herzegovina. **21 per cent** came from **Turkey**, and many Turkish families have lived here for several generations. In addition, many come from North Africa, the Middle East, Asia and other parts of Africa.

In 2000 only **11 per cent** of Muslims had **Swiss nationality**. Since then this share has risen sharply. In the years **2019 to 2023** it was about **37 per cent**. This makes Swiss citizens the largest group. About **31 per cent** held the nationality of a **Balkan state**, such as Kosovo, North Macedonia or Bosnia and Herzegovina. Many became Swiss through **naturalisation**.

gewusst: Many mosque associations in German-speaking Switzerland were founded by Albanian or Bosnian families.
The Muslims of Switzerland speak very many different languages; in the mosques Albanian, Bosnian, Turkish or Arabic is often spoken.

teile.einleitung: The salat is the obligatory prayer in Islam. Muslims pray it five times a day at fixed times that follow the position of the sun. Prayer is one of the five pillars of Islam.
wichtigste: Salat is the Arabic word for the obligatory prayer.
There are five daily prayers: fajr, zuhr, asr, maghrib and isha.
The prayer times follow the sun.
Prayer is one of the five pillars of Islam.
In prayer people bow and prostrate themselves.
People pray in the direction of Mecca.

abschnitte.text: The first prayer is called **fajr** and is prayed at dawn. At midday **zuhr** follows, in the afternoon **asr**. After sunset people pray **maghrib**, at night **isha**. Because the times follow the **sun**, they shift over the course of the year. In Switzerland the intervals are different in summer from in winter.

Islam has **five pillars**, which are its most important duties. They include the declaration of faith, prayer, the donation for the needy, fasting in Ramadan and the pilgrimage to Mecca. Prayer is the second pillar. It is meant to remind people of God several times a day.

Before prayer Muslims wash in a particular way; this washing is called **wudu**. In it, for example, hands, face and feet are washed. People pray in a clean place, often on a prayer mat. The direction of prayer towards Mecca is called the **qibla**. In mosques a niche in the wall shows this direction.

A prayer consists of several units called **rak'as**. People stand, recite verses from the Quran and **bow**. Then they prostrate themselves so that the forehead touches the ground. After that they sit briefly. At the end they speak the greeting of peace to the right and to the left. On Friday at midday many Muslims pray together in the mosque.

gewusst: The prayer times are calculated exactly for every place, because the sun does not rise and set everywhere at the same time.
Anyone who is on a plane or travelling may shorten or combine some prayers.

teile.einleitung: All Saints’ Day is a Catholic holy day on 1 November. On this day the Church remembers all the saints. Many families also visit the graves of their dead on this day.
wichtigste: All Saints’ Day is on 1 November.
On this day the Catholic Church honours all the saints, including the unknown ones.
Many families go to the cemetery and decorate the graves.
The day after, 2 November, is All Souls’ Day.
In several Catholic cantons, All Saints’ Day is a public holiday.
Halloween is the evening before All Saints’ Day.

abschnitte.titel: A festival for all the saints
abschnitte.text: The Catholic Church has many **saints**. These are people who led an especially exemplary life. Many of them have their own day of remembrance during the year. On **All Saints’ Day**, 1 November, people think of all the saints together, including those whom nobody knows. A festive service is held in church on this day.

On All Saints’ Day, many Catholic families go to the **cemetery**. They decorate the graves of their dead with flowers, fir branches and arrangements. They often light a **grave candle**, a candle in a red or white glass. In some places the priest blesses the graves. Strictly speaking, 2 November, **All Souls’ Day**, is the day of the dead, but because All Saints’ Day is a day off in many places, people usually go then.

In Switzerland, All Saints’ Day is a **public holiday** in several Catholic cantons, for example in Lucerne, Valais and Ticino. Schools and many shops are closed there. In Protestant areas, 1 November is an ordinary working day. The Protestants have **Eternity Sunday** in November instead, when they remember the dead.

Even in early Christianity, people remembered the martyrs. In the 9th century, All Saints’ Day was introduced as a festival on 1 November throughout the whole Western Church. The evening before is called “All Hallows’ Eve” in English. From this came the name **Halloween**. This custom came from Ireland and North America and is now known in Switzerland too.

gewusst: In many cemeteries, hundreds of grave candles glow in the evening on All Saints’ Day.
The word Halloween is a short form of “All Hallows’ Eve”, the evening before All Saints’ Day.

teile.einleitung: The Mughal Empire was a great Islamic empire on the Indian subcontinent. It lasted from the 16th to the 19th century. Famous buildings such as the Taj Mahal date from this time.
wichtigste: Babur founded the Mughal Empire in 1526 after the first battle of Panipat.
Babur was descended on his father's side from the conqueror Timur.
Akbar was a well-known ruler who tolerated many religions.
Under Shah Jahan the Taj Mahal was built in Agra.
Aurangzeb reintroduced the jizya in 1679.

abschnitte.text: **Babur** was a prince from Central Asia. On his father's side he was descended from the famous conqueror **Timur**. In **1526** he defeated the Sultan of Delhi in the first **battle of Panipat**. With this the **Mughal Empire** began in the north of India. The name “Mughal” comes from “Mongol”, for Babur also counted Genghis Khan among his ancestors.

Under **Akbar** the empire became large and powerful in the 16th century. Akbar was known for tolerating people of different religions, including the many **Hindus**. He abolished the **jizya**, a special tax for non-Muslims. At court people spoke **Persian**, and art, painting and architecture flourished. His grandson **Shah Jahan** had the **Taj Mahal** built in Agra as a tomb for his wife.

The ruler **Aurangzeb** reintroduced the jizya in **1679**. Under him the empire did reach its greatest extent, but there were many wars and uprisings. After his death in 1707 the power of the Mughals fell apart more and more. The British gained the upper hand in India. In **1858** they deposed the last Mughal emperor.

gewusst: The Taj Mahal is today a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the best-known buildings in the world.
Babur wrote down his memoirs himself, and the book is called the “Baburnama”.

teile.einleitung: Since 2009 the Swiss Federal Constitution has said that no minarets may be built. The ban came about through a popular initiative. The vote was widely noticed and discussed in Switzerland and abroad.
wichtigste: The voters accepted the minaret ban on 29 November 2009.
57.5 per cent of those voting said yes.
The initiative won 19½ to 3½ cantons.
The ban is in Article 72 of the Federal Constitution.
The initiative was launched in 2007 by the Egerkingen Committee.
The four existing minarets were allowed to stay.

abschnitte.titel: The dispute in Wangen bei Olten
abschnitte.text: From **2006** there was a great dispute in **Wangen bei Olten** in the canton of Solothurn. A Turkish cultural association wanted to build a small **minaret** on its building. Many people in the municipality opposed it, while others supported the project. The case went as far as court, and the minaret was finally built. The dispute gave the impetus for a national initiative.

In **2007** the **Egerkingen Committee** launched the **federal popular initiative** “Against the construction of minarets”. The committee consisted mainly of politicians of the SVP and the EDU. With a popular initiative, citizens can demand a change to the Federal Constitution. For this, 100,000 valid signatures are needed. The Federal Council and Parliament recommended rejecting the initiative.

On **29 November 2009** Switzerland voted. **57.5 per cent** of those voting said yes. For a constitutional amendment the **majority of the cantons** is also needed: the initiative was accepted by **19½ to 3½ cantons**. Only Basel-Stadt, Geneva, Vaud and Neuchâtel rejected it. Basel-Stadt was thus the only German-speaking canton with a no.

Since then Article 72 of the Federal Constitution has contained the sentence: “The construction of minarets is prohibited.” The ban applies only to new minarets. The **four** existing minarets in Zurich, Geneva, Winterthur and Wangen bei Olten were allowed to **stay standing**. Mosques and prayer rooms without a minaret are still permitted.

Supporters saw in the minaret a sign of political claims to power that did not fit Switzerland. Opponents thought the ban violated **freedom of religion** and disadvantaged Muslims. There were also many reactions abroad. Complaints against the ban at the European Court of Human Rights were unsuccessful.

gewusst: At the time of the vote there were only four minarets in the whole of Switzerland.
The minaret of Wangen bei Olten is only about six metres high.

teile.einleitung: Arabic calligraphy is the art of beautiful writing with Arabic letters. In the Islamic world it is regarded as one of the most important arts, because the Quran is written with it. Over the centuries many different scripts developed.
wichtigste: Arabic is written from right to left.
Naskh is today the most common book script.
Thuluth is often used for large inscriptions in mosques.
Nastaliq comes from Persia, Maghribi from North Africa.
In the 10th century Ibn Muqla introduced fixed rules for the size of letters.
Ruq'ah is a fast everyday script for handwriting.

abschnitte.text: Because the Quran was revealed in Arabic, writing has a high value in Islam. Calligraphers write with a cut **reed pen**. Arabic is written **from right to left**. Beautiful script decorates mosques, books, plates and carpets. Many calligraphers practise for years with a master before they are regarded as masters themselves.

In the 10th century the scholar **Ibn Muqla** introduced fixed rules. He measured the letters with diamond-shaped **dots** made by the pen. In this way all letters received definite proportions to one another. These rules are still the basis of many scripts today.

**Naskh** is easy to read and the most common book script, including for the printed Quran. **Thuluth** looks solemn and suits large bands of writing on walls and domes. It is regarded as particularly difficult. **Nastaliq** came into being in Persia; its words seem to hang at a slant. **Maghribi** comes from North Africa and the former Muslim Spain and has round, wide curves. **Ruq'ah** is simple and fast, and many people write by hand with it.

The Ottomans developed the ornate script **Diwani** in their chancery, the diwan. It was beautiful and hard to forge and was used for official documents. A special form is the **hilye**: a panel of writing that describes Muhammad's appearance and character in words. Because many Muslims do not depict the Prophet in pictures, script here takes the place of the picture.

gewusst: From our point of view, an Arabic book begins “at the back”, because it is read from right to left.
Many computer fonts for Arabic are based on the Naskh style.

teile.einleitung: The Fatimids were a ruling family that governed a large empire in North Africa and the Middle East from 909 to 1171. They belonged to the Ismaili branch of Shia Islam. The Fatimids founded Cairo and the famous al-Azhar Mosque.
wichtigste: The Fatimids were Ismaili Shia and claimed the caliphate.
Their name refers to Fatima, the daughter of Muhammad.
In 909 they established their rule in Ifriqiya, in present-day Tunisia.
In 969 they conquered Egypt and founded Cairo.
From 970 to 972 they built the al-Azhar Mosque.
In 1171 Saladin ended their rule.

abschnitte.text: The Fatimids traced their descent through **Fatima** and **Ali** back to the Prophet Muhammad. That is where their name comes from. They belonged to **Ismaili Shia Islam** and saw their rulers as imams. In this way they stood in competition with the Sunni **Abbasids** in Baghdad. In 909, Ismaili missionaries with the help of Berber tribes overthrew the rulers in **Ifriqiya**, in present-day Tunisia. The first caliph was **Abdallah al-Mahdi**.

In 969 the Fatimids conquered **Egypt**. Their general **Jawhar** laid out a new palace city next to the old town of Fustat: **al-Qahira**, “the Victorious”. From it came **Cairo**, the capital of the empire. From 970 to 972 the **al-Azhar Mosque** was built, which soon became a place of learning. Today al-Azhar is an important Sunni institution.

The caliph **al-Hakim** at times persecuted Christians and Jews. In 1009 he had the **Church of the Holy Sepulchre** in Jerusalem destroyed, which caused a great stir in Europe. Some of his followers saw in him a divine manifestation. From this veneration the religious community of the **Druze** arose. Today they live mainly in Lebanon, Syria and Israel.

After the death of the caliph al-Mustansir in 1094 there was a dispute over the succession. Part of the Ismailis did not follow al-Mustali but his brother Nizar. In this way the **Nizaris** arose, who under Hasan-i Sabbah expanded the fortress of **Alamut**. The empire grew weaker. In 1171 **Saladin**, the vizier of the last Fatimid caliph, ended their rule. He founded the Sunni dynasty of the **Ayyubids**.

gewusst: The tradition of Ramadan lanterns in Cairo is often traced back to the time of the Fatimids.
Al-Azhar is among the oldest places of learning in the world that still exist today.

teile.einleitung: Islamic theology is the scholarly study of the Islamic faith. For some years it has also been possible to study it at universities in Germany and Switzerland. There, for example, religion teachers and imams are trained.
wichtigste: In 2010 the German Council of Science and Humanities recommended centres for Islamic theology in Germany.
In 2012 Tübingen opened the first such centre at a university.
In Switzerland the SZIG has existed since 2015 at the University of Fribourg.
The Islamkolleg Deutschland in Osnabrück has trained imams in German since 2021.
Important subjects are kalam, fiqh, tafsir and hadith studies.

abschnitte.text: For a long time there were hardly any courses in Islamic theology in Europe. In 2010 the **German Council of Science and Humanities** recommended setting up such centres at universities. It advises the federal government and the states on higher education. The first university to open a centre for Islamic theology was **Tübingen** in January 2012. Others followed later, for example at the **Humboldt University** in Berlin, where the course began in the winter semester of 2019/20.

In Switzerland the **Swiss Centre for Islam and Society**, **SZIG** for short, was founded in 2015 at the **University of Fribourg**. It offers further training for imams, chaplains and other professionals. In doing so it combines Islamic theology with questions of Swiss society, for example about living together or about pastoral care in hospitals.

In the past many imams came from abroad and spoke little German. The **Islamkolleg Deutschland** in **Osnabrück** was founded in 2019. Since 2021 it has trained imams in a practical way and in German. The aim is that imams know the language and society of their communities well.

Islamic theology has several subjects. **Kalam** is the doctrine of faith and deals with questions such as God's attributes and free will. **Fiqh** is Islamic law, **tafsir** the interpretation of the Quran and **sira** the life story of Muhammad. **Hadith studies** examines the transmitted sayings and deeds of Muhammad and checks the chain of transmitters, the **isnad**.

At the new centres new ideas also arise. **Mouhanad Khorchide** of Münster represents a “theology of mercy”. In 2012 he wrote the book “Islam ist Barmherzigkeit” (“Islam is mercy”), in which he stresses a loving rather than a punishing God. This triggered debates with Islamic associations. The influence of the associations on the centres is also discussed again and again.

gewusst: Kalam literally means “speech”.
Hadith studies examines not only the content of a report but above all who transmitted it.

teile.einleitung: The Asharites are an important school of Islamic theology. It was founded by al-Ashari in the 10th century and is regarded as the most significant school of theology in Sunni Islam. It tried to defend matters of faith with the means of reasoned argument.
wichtigste: The founder was Abu l-Hasan al-Ashari, who died around 935.
Al-Ashari was at first a Mutazilite but turned away from them around 912.
God's attributes are affirmed “without asking how”.
With the concept of kasb they explained the responsibility of human beings.
The Nizamiyya colleges spread the teaching in the 11th century.

abschnitte.text: **Abu l-Hasan al-Ashari** was at first a pupil of the Mutazilite **al-Jubbai**. The **Mutazilites** placed great value on reason. Around 912 al-Ashari broke with them, above all over the question of God's justice. After that he defended Sunni articles of faith with the methods of **Kalam**, the Islamic theology that works with arguments.

In the Quran there is mention, for instance, of God's “hand” or his “throne”. The Asharites accepted these statements as true but did not ask how exactly they are to be understood. The formula **“bila kaifa”**, “without how”, stands for this. God is not compared with created beings. They saw the Quran as the **eternal, uncreated speech of God**. From this they distinguished the written and recited text.

abschnitte.titel: God as the cause of everything
abschnitte.text: According to Asharite teaching, God creates all things and all actions. Human beings acquire their deeds; the term **kasb**, “acquisition”, stands for this. In this way God's omnipotence and human responsibility were meant to fit together. In nature too they saw God as the real cause: fire burns cotton because God creates the burning anew each time. This view is called **occasionalism**.

In the 11th century the Seljuk vizier **Nizam al-Mulk** founded the **Nizamiyya madrasas** in Baghdad and other cities. Asharite scholars such as **al-Juwayni** and **al-Ghazali** taught there. In this way Asharite theology became dominant in large parts of the Sunni world and has remained so in many places to this day.

gewusst: The well-known example of fire and cotton comes from al-Ghazali, one of the most famous Asharites.
Besides the Asharites there is a second great Sunni school of theology, the Maturidites.

teile.einleitung: Iran is a large country in West Asia with a long history. Since the revolution of 1979 it has been an Islamic Republic in which Shia clerics have great power. The majority of the population belongs to Shia Islam.
wichtigste: In 1979 Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini led the Islamic Revolution.
The Islamic Republic came into being in spring 1979 through a referendum.
Under the principle of Velayat-e Faqih, a legal scholar leads the state.
In 1989 Ali Khamenei became Supreme Leader.
The Guardian Council examines laws and admits election candidates, and the Assembly of Experts elects the leader.
In 2022 the death of Jina Mahsa Amini triggered nationwide protests.

abschnitte.text: Before 1979 Iran was ruled by a king, the **Shah**. After great protests he left the country. In February 1979 **Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini** returned from exile in Paris. On 30 and 31 March 1979 the population voted in a **referendum** for an Islamic Republic. On 1 April 1979 it was proclaimed. Khomeini became the first **Supreme Leader**.

The state is based on the principle of **Velayat-e Faqih**. That means “guardianship of the jurist”. Khomeini taught that until the return of the hidden imam, a Shia scholar should lead the state. The **Supreme Leader** therefore has more power than the president. After Khomeini's death, the former president **Ali Khamenei** became his successor in **1989**.

The **Guardian Council** has twelve members: six Islamic legal scholars and six jurists. It examines whether laws are compatible with Islam. It also decides who may **stand** in elections, and so has great influence. The **Assembly of Experts** consists of about 88 clerics who are elected by the people. It elects the Supreme Leader and is supposed to oversee him.

Most people in Iran are **Shia**. Their most important place of pilgrimage in the country is **Mashhad**. There lies the shrine of the eighth imam **Ali al-Ridha**, in Persian Reza. The shrine is one of the largest religious complexes in the world. Every year millions of pilgrims visit it.

In September 2022 the young woman **Jina Mahsa Amini** died in the custody of the morality police. She had been arrested because her headscarf was allegedly not worn correctly. After that **protests** broke out across the country. They stood under the cry **“Woman, Life, Freedom”**. The government took harsh action against the demonstrators.

gewusst: In Iran people speak mainly Persian, not Arabic.
The Iranian calendar begins the year with the spring festival of Nowruz around 21 March.

teile.einleitung: A fatwa is a legal opinion of an Islamic scholar. It answers a question about religion or law, for example how to pray correctly or what is allowed in trade. In principle a fatwa is a recommendation and not a court judgement.
wichtigste: A fatwa is a religious legal opinion.
A scholar who issues fatwas is called a mufti.
A qadi, by contrast, is a judge who passes binding judgements.
A fatwa is in principle not binding.
In the Ottoman Empire the Sheikh al-Islam was the highest mufti.
The fatwa against Salman Rushdie triggered a worldwide crisis in 1989.

abschnitte.text: When Muslims have a question about faith or law, they can ask a scholar. His answer is called a **fatwa**. The scholar who gives it is a **mufti**. Most fatwas concern quite everyday questions, for example about prayer, fasting, food or money matters. Today many questions are also asked by telephone or on the internet.

A fatwa is an **opinion** and not a court judgement. Judgements are passed by the **qadi**, a judge. His judgement is binding on the parties. A fatwa, by contrast, is in principle **not binding**: the person asking can also obtain the opinion of another mufti. Imam and muezzin have yet other tasks: they lead the prayer or call people to it.

In the **Ottoman Empire** the **Sheikh al-Islam** in Istanbul was the highest mufti and the highest religious authority. His fatwas could even justify decisions of the sultan. In 1989 a fatwa by **Ayatollah Khomeini** of Iran became known worldwide. It was directed against the writer **Salman Rushdie** because of his novel “The Satanic Verses” and called for his death. This led to an international crisis.

In 1997 the **European Council for Fatwa and Research** was founded in London; it has its seat in Dublin. It deals with questions of Muslims who live as a minority in Europe. In 2004 and 2005 hundreds of scholars confirmed the **Amman Message**. It mutually recognised eight schools of law. It also demanded that only qualified scholars may issue fatwas.

gewusst: In many countries there are state offices whose head bears the title Grand Mufti.
The great majority of fatwas deal with everyday questions and are never mentioned in newspapers.

teile.einleitung: The Twelver Shia is the largest branch of Shia Islam. Its name comes from the twelve imams whom its followers revere as the rightful leaders of the community. It is especially widespread in Iran, Iraq, Bahrain, Azerbaijan and Lebanon.
wichtigste: The Twelver Shia revere twelve imams, the first of whom is Ali ibn Abi Talib.
According to its teaching, the twelfth imam, Muhammad al-Mahdi, lives in concealment and will return at the end of time.
This concealment is called ghayba.
From 1501 the Safavids made the Twelver Shia the state religion in Persia.
Its school of law is called the Jaafari school, after the sixth imam, Jafar al-Sadiq.
Important centres of scholars are Qom in Iran and Najaf in Iraq.

abschnitte.text: After Muhammad's death, Muslims argued over who should lead the community. The Shia think that this should be **Ali ibn Abi Talib**, Muhammad's cousin and son-in-law, and his descendants. The Twelver Shia revere a line of **twelve imams**. Among them is also Ali's son Husayn, whose death at Karbala is remembered every year on the day of **Ashura**. Ali is buried in **Najaf**, and his shrine is an important place of pilgrimage.

The twelfth imam is called **Muhammad al-Mahdi**, and his father Hasan al-Askari was the eleventh imam. According to the teaching, the Mahdi went into the **ghayba**, the concealment. In the lesser concealment from 874 to 941, deputies kept up contact. Since 941 the greater concealment has lasted. The faithful expect that the Mahdi will return at the end of time and bring justice.

For a long time the Twelver Shia lived as a minority in many areas. In 1501 **Shah Ismail I** founded the rule of the **Safavids** and made the Twelver Shia the official religion. With that Persia, present-day Iran, was permanently shaped by Shia Islam. Today the Twelver Shia is the state religion there.

The school of law goes back to the sixth imam, **Jafar al-Sadiq**, who taught in Medina in the 8th century. The school of the Usulis prevailed, which stresses **ijtihad**: scholars derive rulings independently from the sources. Such a scholar is called a **mujtahid**. The highest ranking are called **marja al-taqlid**, “source of emulation”, and the faithful follow their legal opinions. They are trained above all in **Qom** and Najaf.

**Ruhollah Khomeini** advocated the principle of **velayat-e faqih**, the rule of the jurist. According to it, as long as the twelfth imam is hidden, a high scholar should lead the state. This principle was anchored in the constitution of the Islamic Republic of Iran in 1979. Not all Shia scholars agree with this, and some reject such a strong political role for the clergy.

gewusst: Most Shia worldwide belong to the Twelver Shia.
In Qom there are numerous theological colleges, called hawzas.

teile.einleitung: In the year 630 the Prophet Muhammad returned to Mecca with a great army and took the city almost without a fight. Eight years earlier he had had to leave Mecca. The conquest was a turning point in the history of Islam.
wichtigste: In 628 Muhammad and the Meccans concluded the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.
After the Meccans had broken the truce, Muhammad marched on Mecca in 630.
About 10,000 fighters went with him, and Mecca surrendered almost without a fight.
The idols at the Kaaba were removed and destroyed.
Muhammad pardoned most of his former opponents.
Muhammad died in the year 632 in Medina.

abschnitte.text: In 622 Muhammad and his followers had emigrated from Mecca to **Medina**. After that there was fighting with the Meccans. In 628 both sides agreed at the place **Hudaybiyyah**, in front of Mecca, on a **truce**. The Muslims were allowed to make the pilgrimage to Mecca in the following year. Later the Meccans broke the truce.

In the year **630** Muhammad marched on Mecca with about **10,000** fighters. The Meccans saw that resistance was hopeless. There were only a few skirmishes, and the city surrendered **almost without a fight**. Shortly before, **Abu Sufyan**, who had long led the Meccans against the Muslims, had accepted Islam.

In and around the **Kaaba** there then stood many idols. Muhammad had them removed and destroyed. In this way the Kaaba became the sanctuary of the **one God**. Towards his former opponents Muhammad declared a general **pardon**, with only a few exceptions. Many Meccans accepted Islam afterwards.

In the same year the Muslims defeated hostile Bedouin tribes in the **battle of Hunayn**. After that more and more tribes of Arabia joined Islam. Shortly before his death, Muhammad led the pilgrims on the **Farewell Pilgrimage** to Mecca and delivered his farewell sermon there. Its course is still regarded as a model for the pilgrimage today. Muhammad died in **632** in Medina.

gewusst: The emigration to Medina in the year 622 is called the Hijra, and with it the Islamic calendar begins.
Muhammad left no clearly appointed successor, and there was much dispute about this later.

teile.einleitung: “Inshallah” is an Arabic expression and means “God willing”. Muslims all over the world say it when they talk about the future. There are other such expressions for everyday life too.
wichtigste: Inshallah means “God willing” or “If God wills”.
People say it when making plans for the future.
The expression consists of three Arabic words: in, sha'a and Allah.
The Spanish word “ojalá” comes from Arabic.
Mashallah is said when one admires something beautiful.
After sneezing, many Muslims say Alhamdulillah.

abschnitte.text: People say **“inshallah”** when they talk about **plans**. An example: “I'll come to you tomorrow, inshallah.” That means: I want to come if nothing gets in the way and God wills it. Anyone who says inshallah shows that they cannot decide everything themselves. They **trust** that God guides the future.

The expression consists of **three Arabic words**: “in” means if, “sha'a” means wills, and “Allah” means God. Together that gives “if God wills”. Muslims say it not only in Arab countries. You also hear it in Turkey, in Bosnia, in Pakistan or in Switzerland.

In Spanish there is the word **“ojalá”**. It means “hopefully”. It comes from the Arabic **“law sha'a llah”**, which means “if God wills”. In the past, many Muslims lived in Spain for centuries. That is why the Spanish language took over many words from Arabic.

**“Mashallah”** means roughly “What God has willed”. People say it when they admire something beautiful, for example a healthy baby or a job well done. **“Alhamdulillah”** means “Praise be to God”. Many say it after sneezing. The others then reply with a blessing.

gewusst: Christians in Arab countries also often say “inshallah”, because Allah is simply the Arabic word for God.

teile.einleitung: Jesus is important not only in Christianity but also in Islam. In the Quran he is called Isa and is regarded as a great prophet. Muslims see him differently from Christians, however.
wichtigste: In the Quran Jesus is called Isa.
For Muslims Isa is a great prophet, but not the Son of God.
His mother is called Maryam.
According to Islam, Isa received the Gospel, in Arabic Injil.
In the Quran he bears the honorary title al-Masih, the Messiah.
Many Muslims believe that Isa will return at the end of time.

abschnitte.text: In the Quran Jesus is called **Isa**. For Muslims he is a **great prophet** and messenger of God. Unlike in Christianity, however, he is **not regarded as the Son of God**. In the Quran Isa bears the honorary title **al-Masih**, which means **Messiah** or “the Anointed”.

Isa's mother is called **Maryam** in the Quran, in English Mary. That is why he is often called “Isa, son of Maryam”. Maryam is very much revered in Islam. A whole **surah** of the Quran bears her name.

According to Islam, God gave a scripture to several prophets. **Musa** (Moses) received the **Torah**, **Isa** received the **Gospel**, in Arabic **Injil**. Muhammad received the **Quran**. In this way Muslims see a connection between Judaism, Christianity and Islam.

The Quran tells of miracles of Isa. Already as a **baby in the cradle** he could speak and in this way defended his mother. He shaped **birds out of clay**, breathed on them, and with God's permission they came alive. He healed the **blind and the sick**. What matters is that he always did everything **with God's permission**.

Many Muslims believe that Isa will **return at the end of time**. This teaching comes mainly from **tradition**, the hadiths. Christians too believe in a return of Jesus. So here there is something in common, even if the two religions understand Isa differently.

gewusst: A surah of the Quran is named after Maryam, the mother of Isa.
The story of the birds made of clay is in the Quran but not in the Bible.

teile.einleitung: The date is a sweet fruit that grows on the date palm. In hot, dry countries it has been an important food for thousands of years. For many Muslims it is a fixed part of the fasting month of Ramadan.
wichtigste: Dates grow in large clusters on the date palm.
Date palms grow in hot, dry regions, often in oases.
Many Muslims break the fast in the evening first with a date.
Dates contain a lot of sugar and give quick energy.
In every date there is an elongated stone.
Saudi Arabia and Egypt are among the biggest date harvesters (as of 2024).

abschnitte.text: Dates grow on the **date palm**. It has a tall trunk and at the top a crown of long, **feathery fronds**. These leaves are divided into many narrow parts, like feathers. The fruits hang in large **clusters** high up. A single palm can bear a great many dates.

Date palms love **sun and heat**. They grow in hot, dry regions. At their roots, however, they need water, for example from groundwater. That is why they often stand in an **oasis**, a green place with water in the middle of the desert. There the palms also give shade to other plants.

In Ramadan, devout Muslims neither eat nor drink from dawn until sunset. In the evening many break the fast first with a **date** and a little water. This is an old custom that is traced back to the Prophet Muhammad. The **sugar** of the date reaches the blood quickly, so the body soon gets energy again. In Switzerland too, bowls of dates then stand on the table in many families.

Fresh dates are yellow or red depending on the variety. When dried they usually turn **brown** and wrinkled and keep for a long time. In every date there is a hard, elongated **stone**. You eat only the sweet flesh around it. In 2024, **Saudi Arabia** and **Egypt** each harvested almost two million tonnes of dates. Algeria and Iran also harvest a great many.

gewusst: People have grown date palms for several thousand years; they are among the oldest cultivated plants.
The date palm is mentioned several times in the Quran.

t1wc5rbp.t: Swiss Centre for Islam and Society

teile.einleitung: The Swiss Centre for Islam and Society, SZIG for short, is an institute at the University of Fribourg. It researches how Muslims live in Switzerland and offers further training. At its founding there was a political dispute that went as far as the Federal Supreme Court.
wichtigste: The SZIG is an interfaculty institute of the University of Fribourg.
The theologian Hansjörg Schmid built it up from 2015.
The SERI funded the centre from the start until the end of 2024.
The training of imams expressly does not belong to its mandate.
The SVP launched a popular initiative against it in the canton of Fribourg.
The Grand Council declared the initiative invalid in 2016, and the Federal Supreme Court confirmed this.

abschnitte.text: The SZIG is an **interfaculty institute** of the **University of Fribourg**. That means that several faculties work on it. It deals with questions about Islam in Swiss society. From **2015** the theologian **Hansjörg Schmid** built up the centre. He leads it as managing director.

The centre does research, teaches and offers **further training**, for example for professionals from schools, hospitals or prisons. From 2015 the **Mercator Switzerland Foundation** financed the doctoral programme **“Islamic Theological Studies”**. From the start until the end of 2024 the **State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation** (SERI) funded the centre. The **training of imams** expressly does not belong to its mandate.

The **SVP** launched a **popular initiative** against the centre in the canton of Fribourg. It was submitted in 2015 and carried the subtitle **“No to state imam training”**. Supporters wanted to prevent the state from supporting such training. Opponents considered the initiative incompatible with freedom of religion and equal treatment.

The **Grand Council**, the parliament of the canton of Fribourg, declared the initiative **invalid** in **2016**. A court case was brought against this. The **Federal Supreme Court** confirmed the invalidity. It justified this by saying that the initiative was **one-sidedly directed against a single religion**. This violates the ban on discrimination in the Federal Constitution.

gewusst: The University of Fribourg is bilingual, and teaching there is in German and French.

teile.einleitung: The Mutazilites were a group of Islamic theologians in the Middle Ages. They wanted to base faith on reason. In the 9th century their teaching was for a short time even the official teaching of the caliphate.
wichtigste: The founder of the Mutazilites is regarded as Wasil ibn Ata.
The name comes from the Arabic word for “to withdraw”.
The Mutazilites taught that the Quran was created.
Among their five principles are God's unity and God's justice.
The caliph al-Mamun made their teaching binding in 833 with the test called the Mihna.
Ahmad ibn Hanbal refused to accept this teaching.

abschnitte.text: The Mutazilites arose in the 8th century in the city of **Basra** in present-day Iraq. The founder is regarded as **Wasil ibn Ata**. He heard the teachings of a famous scholar but disagreed on one question and **withdrew**. That is where the name comes from: “Mutazilites” means roughly “those who withdraw”.

At that time scholars argued about whether someone who commits a **grave sin** is still a believer. Some said yes, others no. The Mutazilites gave a third answer: such a person has an **intermediate position** between believer and unbeliever. This teaching became one of their **five principles**.

For the Mutazilites **reason** was very important. Among their principles were the **unity of God** and the **justice of God**. God does nothing unjust, they said, and human beings are themselves responsible for their deeds. They also taught that the **Quran was created** and has not existed from eternity. Many other scholars saw this quite differently.

The Abbasid caliph **al-Mamun** supported the Mutazilites. In the year **833** he introduced a test, the **Mihna**. Scholars and judges had to declare that the Quran was created. The scholar **Ahmad ibn Hanbal** refused and was punished for it. A few years later another caliph ended the Mihna, and the Mutazilites lost influence.

In Sunni Islam other schools later prevailed. Mutazilite thought lived on, however, especially in **Shia theology**, for example among the **Zaydis**. In our own time some Muslim thinkers have again taken an interest in the Mutazilites. They are interested in their combination of faith and reason.

gewusst: Ahmad ibn Hanbal, who resisted the Mihna, later gave his name to one of the four Sunni schools of law.

t1x6bc3w.t: The ECtHR ruling on swimming lessons

teile.einleitung: In 2017 the European Court of Human Rights, ECtHR for short, decided a case from Basel. Muslim parents did not want to send their daughters to mixed swimming lessons. The court ruled in favour of the school.
wichtigste: The ruling was made on 10 January 2017.
The case came from the canton of Basel-Stadt.
The parents had to pay a fine of 1,400 francs.
They appealed to freedom of thought, conscience and religion.
The ECtHR unanimously found no violation of the Convention.
According to the court, swimming lessons promote integration.

abschnitte.text: A family in **Basel-Stadt** did not want to send their daughters to **mixed swimming lessons** for religious reasons. The school offered accommodation: the girls were allowed to wear a **burkini** and **change separately**. The parents refused all the same. They then received a **fine of 1,400 francs**.

The parents fought the fine. In **2012** the **Federal Supreme Court** upheld it. Earlier the Federal Supreme Court had decided differently: in **1993** it granted a Muslim girl an **exemption**, that is, release from swimming lessons.
