From a small college in Aligarh a large university grew.

teile.einleitung: A large part of the Muslims in Switzerland have roots in the Balkans, above all in Kosovo, North Macedonia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. Many came from the 1960s as workers, others later as refugees from wars. Today many of them are Swiss citizens.
wichtigste: Albanian-speaking Muslims form the largest group among Muslims in Switzerland.
From the 1960s many men came from Yugoslavia as guest workers.
The Bosnian War of 1992 to 1995 and the Kosovo War of 1998 to 1999 brought many refugees.
The Bosniaks are the Muslim ethnic group of Bosnia.
Kosovo declared its independence in 2008, and Switzerland recognised the state a few days later.

abschnitte.text: From the **1960s**, Switzerland was looking for many workers for construction, industry and the hospitality trade. So many men came from what was then **Yugoslavia** as **guest workers**. At first they often stayed only a few months. Later their families frequently followed. In this way associations and prayer rooms arose in many Swiss municipalities.

In the 1990s Yugoslavia fell apart and wars broke out. During the **Bosnian War** of 1992 to 1995 many people fled from Bosnia, often to relatives in Switzerland. In the **Kosovo War** of 1998 to 1999 many Kosovo Albanians sought protection with relatives here. On 17 February **2008**, Kosovo declared its independence from Serbia, and Switzerland recognised the new state a few days later.

In **Kosovo**, in the 2011 census about 95 per cent of people described themselves as Muslims. In **Bosnia and Herzegovina** the **Bosniaks** are mostly Muslims, Croats mostly Catholic and Serbs mostly Orthodox. The most important mosque of Bosnia is the **Gazi Husrev-beg Mosque** in Sarajevo, from 1531. In **Albania** the communist ruler Enver Hoxha had all mosques and churches closed in 1967. Only from 1990 were people allowed to believe freely there again.

Today **Albanian-speaking Muslims** form the largest group among Muslims in Switzerland. Many families have already lived here for the second or third generation. They go to school, work in all professions and have often become citizens. Faith is lived in very different ways: for some it is very important, for others less so. Many combine Swiss everyday life with traditions from their parents' homeland.

gewusst: From 1967 to 1990 Albania was the only state in the world that had banned every religion.
Besides Muslims there are also many Catholic and Orthodox Christians who came to Switzerland from the Balkans.

teile.einleitung: Uthman ibn Affan was the third caliph of Islam. He followed Umar ibn al-Khattab, the second caliph. Both shaped the early history of Islam strongly, Uthman above all through the binding version of the Quran.
wichtigste: The second caliph was Umar ibn al-Khattab.
Under Umar Jerusalem was taken.
Umar was the first to take the title “Commander of the Faithful”.
The third caliph was Uthman ibn Affan.
Uthman had a binding version of the text of the Quran produced.
Uthman was killed by rebels in Medina in 656.

abschnitte.text: The **second caliph** was **Umar ibn al-Khattab**. He ruled from 634. Under him the empire was greatly enlarged. **Jerusalem** was also taken, and Umar visited the city himself. He was the first to take the title **“Commander of the Faithful”**. In the year **644** he was **murdered**.

The **third caliph** was **Uthman ibn Affan**. He came from a rich family of Mecca, the family of the Umayyads. Uthman was one of the first people to accept Islam. He bears the nickname **“the one with the two lights”**. For he **married two daughters of Muhammad one after the other**.

Already under Abu Bakr, leaves of the Quran were collected. Later they were kept **with Hafsa**, the **daughter of Umar** and widow of Muhammad. When Uthman was caliph, there were copies with small differences. He had a **binding version of the text of the Quran** produced. These copies were sent to important cities, and **differing copies** were to be **destroyed**.

Towards the end of his rule discontent grew. Critics accused him of favouring his relatives. In the year **656** Uthman was **killed by rebels in Medina**. After that Ali became the fourth caliph. Uthman's death led to quarrels and wars among Muslims.

gewusst: The text of the Quran that Muslims read today goes back to the version produced under Uthman.
Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali are called the “rightly guided caliphs” by Sunnis.

teile.einleitung: “One Thousand and One Nights” is a famous collection of stories from the Orient. In a frame story the clever Scheherazade tells a king new stories night after night. These include tales such as Aladdin, Ali Baba and Sindbad.
wichtigste: Scheherazade tells the many stories.
The king to whom she tells them is called Shahryar.
She stops at the most exciting point so that the king lets her live.
The collection includes Aladdin, Ali Baba and Sindbad the Sailor.
Antoine Galland translated the collection into French from 1704.
The caliph Harun al-Rashid appears in many of the stories.

abschnitte.text: King **Shahryar** has been disappointed by his wife. He decides to have each new wife executed the next morning. The clever **Scheherazade** marries him all the same and has a plan. Every night she tells him a story. At the **most exciting point** she stops so that the king **lets her live** to hear the end.

In **Aladdin** a poor boy finds a **magic lamp** in which a genie lives. **Ali Baba** opens the cave of the forty thieves with the words **“Open, Sesame!”**. **Sindbad the Sailor** makes **seven** adventurous voyages. On them he meets giant birds, islands that are whales, and many dangers. Children all over the world know these stories today.

In many stories the caliph **Harun al-Rashid** of **Baghdad** appears. He really lived and ruled around the year 800. In the tales he often walks through the city in disguise. In this way he finds out how his subjects are getting on. In his day Baghdad was one of the largest and richest cities in the world.

The stories were collected over centuries, with roots in Persia, India and the Arab world. The Frenchman **Antoine Galland** was the first to translate the collection into a European language, from **1704**. After that it became very popular in Europe. Galland added Aladdin and Ali Baba from oral tellings, for they are missing in the old Arabic manuscripts. To this day books, plays and films are made from them.

gewusst: In the end Scheherazade has told stories for so long that the king gives up his cruel plan.
The title “One Thousand and One Nights” means above all “very many nights”.

teile.einleitung: “Dependent origination” is a central teaching of Buddhism. It says that nothing exists out of itself: everything arises because certain conditions are present, and passes away when they fall away. In Sanskrit the teaching is called pratityasamutpada.
wichtigste: The Sanskrit term is pratityasamutpada, in Pali paticcasamuppada.
The basic formula runs: “When this is, that is; this arising, that arises.”
The teaching is often shown as a chain with twelve links.
At the start of the chain stands ignorance, at the end stand old age and death.
On the Tibetan wheel of life the twelve links form the outermost ring.
A well-known saying runs: “Whoever sees dependent origination sees the Dhamma.”

abschnitte.text: According to Buddhist teaching, nothing exists entirely on its own. A plant, for example, grows only if earth, water, light and warmth are there. The basic formula in the early discourses runs: “When this is, that is; this arising, that arises.” When the **conditions** fall away, what arose from them also passes away. According to the teaching, this applies to thoughts, feelings and suffering as well.

Dependent origination is often explained as a **chain with twelve links**. It begins with **ignorance** (avidya) about the true nature of things. From this follow, among other things, formations, consciousness, the senses, contact and sensation. From sensation arises **craving** (tanha), and from craving **clinging** (upadana), that is, holding on to things, views and the self. After that follow becoming and birth, and at the end stand **old age and death**.

In Tibet the teaching is painted on the **wheel of life** (bhavacakra). In its centre stand the three poisons of the mind, greed, hatred and delusion. Around them the realms of rebirth can be seen. In the **outermost ring** the twelve links are shown as pictures. The wheel is held by a figure that embodies death.

If ignorance is removed, then according to the teaching the whole chain ends and with it the cycle of suffering. That is why insight into conditionality is regarded as the **key**. A discourse of the Pali Canon says: “Whoever sees dependent origination sees the Dhamma.” A tradition tells that **Sariputta** became a disciple of the Buddha through a short verse of the monk Assaji about the causes of things. Later the thinker **Nagarjuna** linked the teaching closely with the idea of emptiness.

gewusst: Dhamma is the Pali word for the Buddha's teaching, in Sanskrit it is called dharma.
According to tradition, Sariputta recognised the core of the teaching on first hearing the short verse.

teile.einleitung: Arabic script is one of the most widely used scripts in the world. It is written from right to left, and many letters are joined to one another. Not only Arabic but also other languages such as Persian are written with it.
wichtigste: The Arabic alphabet has 28 letters; the first is called Alif, the second Ba.
There are no capital and small letters.
A letter can have up to four different forms.
Short vowels are often not written; in the Quran they appear as small marks.
Persian too is written with Arabic letters.

abschnitte.text: The Arabic alphabet has **28 letters**. The first is called **Alif** and is a simple vertical stroke. The second is called **Ba**, sounds like our B and looks like a small bowl with a dot underneath. Many letters differ only in the number and position of their dots. It is written **from right to left**.

In Arabic there are **no capital letters**. Instead, many letters change their form depending on their place in the word. A letter looks different when it stands alone, at the **beginning**, in the **middle** or at the **end** of a word. So it can have up to four forms. Most letters are joined to one another, in print as well.

Normally in Arabic only the consonants and the long vowels are written. Short vowels such as a, i and u are often left out. Anyone who knows the language still knows how a word sounds. In the **Quran** and in books for children, however, the short vowels appear as **small marks** above or below the letters. This way every word is read exactly right.

Arabic is, for example, an official language in **Egypt** and in many other countries of North Africa and the Middle East. **Persian**, the language of Iran, is also written with Arabic letters, with a few additional signs. Our digits 0 to 9 are called **Arabic numerals** because they came to Europe through Arab scholars. Words travelled too: **sugar** comes from the Arabic “sukkar”.

gewusst: In the Arab world itself, people often write numerals other than the “Arabic numerals” that we use.
The words “algebra” and “alcohol” also come from Arabic.

teile.einleitung: Ali ibn Abi Talib was a cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad. He was one of the first people to accept Islam and later became the fourth caliph. For the Shia he is the first Imam, for the Sunnis one of the four rightly guided caliphs.
wichtigste: Ali was the son of Muhammad's uncle Abu Talib.
He married Muhammad's daughter Fatima; their sons were called Hasan and Husayn.
He accepted Islam as a boy.
From 656 to 661 he was the fourth caliph.
He ruled from Kufa in present-day Iraq.
His tomb is revered in Najaf.

abschnitte.text: Ali was the son of **Abu Talib**, an uncle of Muhammad. He grew up in the house of the Prophet. Already as a boy of about ten he accepted Islam. In this way he is one of the very first Muslims. Later he married **Fatima**, the daughter of Muhammad. Through their sons **Hasan** and **Husayn**, the family of the Prophet lives on to this day.

After Muhammad's death, Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman led the Muslims in turn. After the death of Uthman, Ali became the **fourth caliph** in 656. He moved his seat of government from Medina to **Kufa** in present-day Iraq, where he had many followers. His rule, however, was marked by quarrels and fighting among the Muslims.

abschnitte.titel: Battle of the Camel and Siffin
abschnitte.text: In 656 Ali fought near Basra against an army that also included Muhammad's widow **Aisha**. She followed the events on a camel, which is why it is called the **Battle of the Camel**. Ali won. In 657 the fight against **Muawiya**, the governor of Syria, took place at **Siffin**. The battle ended without a clear winner, with an arbitration. One group rejected this and broke away from Ali: the **Kharijites**.

In the year 661 Ali was attacked by a Kharijite in the mosque of Kufa and died a few days later. His tomb is revered in **Najaf** in Iraq. The shrine is one of the most important places of pilgrimage for Shia. The name **Shia** comes from “Shiat Ali”, which means “party of Ali”.

gewusst: For the Shia, Ali should have taken over the leadership directly after Muhammad. The split between Sunnis and Shia arose over this question.
Ali was famous for his learning and his speeches, which were later collected.

teile.einleitung: A prayer mat is a small rug on which Muslims pray. It provides a clean place and is easy to take along. Many prayer mats are artfully patterned.
wichtigste: Muslims pray on the prayer mat.
The place for prayer should be clean, so people do not step on the mat with shoes.
Many prayer mats show an archway that looks like a prayer niche.
Prayer mats are mostly made of fabric or wool.
In Arabic the prayer mat is called a sajjada.

abschnitte.text: During prayer the place should be **clean**. That is why people like to pray on a rug of their own. Beforehand they take off their shoes and step on it barefoot or in socks. After the prayer they fold or roll up the mat. In this way it stays clean for the next prayer.

Many prayer mats show an **archway**. It recalls the prayer niche in a mosque, which is called the **mihrab**. When praying, people lay the mat so that the tip of the arch points towards **Mecca**. There are often flowers, tendrils or pictures of mosques as well. Prayer mats are mostly **woven or knotted from fabric or wool** so that you can kneel on them comfortably.

Muslims pray in the direction of the **Kaaba** in Mecca. Today a **compass** or a phone app helps with this. From Switzerland, Mecca lies roughly to the south-east. In the **prostration** people kneel and touch the mat with the forehead. This is also where the Arabic name **sajjada** comes from: it is related to the word for prostration.

A prayer mat is easy to **take along**. In this way people can pray at home, at work or on journeys. In the mosque people usually do not need one of their own, because the floor is already covered with rugs. Some prayer mats for travelling are especially thin and light.

gewusst: There are travel prayer mats with a small compass built in.
Old, precious prayer mats are displayed in museums.

teile.einleitung: Ashura is a day of remembrance on the tenth day of the Islamic month of Muharram. For Shia it is a day of mourning for Husayn, the grandson of the Prophet Muhammad. For many Sunnis, Ashura is above all a voluntary day of fasting.
wichtigste: Ashura falls on the 10th of Muharram; the word comes from the Arabic word for ten.
On this day Shia remember the death of Husayn near Karbala in the year 680.
In Iran, passion plays called Ta'zieh are performed.
Many Sunnis fast voluntarily on Ashura.
40 days later millions of people make the pilgrimage to Karbala for Arbaeen.

abschnitte.text: The name **Ashura** is derived from the Arabic word for **ten**. It is observed on the **10th of Muharram**, the first month of the Islamic calendar. Because this calendar follows the moon, Ashura falls about eleven days earlier each year than in the year before.

In the year 680, **Husayn**, the grandson of Muhammad and son of Ali, died with many companions in the battle of **Karbala** in present-day Iraq. On Ashura, Shia remember this event with mourning gatherings, sermons and processions. Especially in Iran the **Ta'zieh** are performed: dramatic plays of mourning that re-enact what happened at Karbala. They take place mainly in the first ten days of Muharram.

abschnitte.titel: A day of fasting for Sunnis
abschnitte.text: In the Sunni tradition, Ashura is above all a **voluntary day of fasting**. According to reports, Muhammad fasted on this day and recommended it. A link to the rescue of **Moses** and the Israelites from Egypt is also reported. Fasting on Ashura is not a duty like fasting in Ramadan.

**Arbaeen** means “forty”. Forty days after Ashura the traditional period of mourning for Husayn ends. Every year **millions of people** make the pilgrimage to Karbala on this day, many of them on foot over long distances. On the way, volunteers offer the pilgrims free food, drinks and places to sleep.

gewusst: The pilgrimage to Arbaeen is among the largest regular gatherings of people in the world.
The Alevis too know a festival at Ashura, at which a sweet dish is shared.

teile.einleitung: The Safavids were a ruling family that governed Iran from 1501 into the 18th century. They made the Shia branch of Islam the state religion. This still shapes Iran today.
wichtigste: Ismail I founded the Safavid Empire in 1501.
The Safavids made Twelver Shia Islam the state religion in Iran.
The name comes from the Sufi order of Safi al-Din of Ardabil.
Their Turkmen warriors were called Qizilbash, “Red Heads”.
In 1514 the Ottomans defeated the Safavids at Chaldiran.
Abbas I made Isfahan the capital.

abschnitte.text: The name of the Safavids goes back to **Safi al-Din**. In the city of **Ardabil** in the north-west of Iran he founded a **Sufi order**. His successors grew more and more powerful over time. Loyal warriors from Turkmen tribes supported them. Because of their **red headgear** these warriors were called **Qizilbash**, which means “Red Heads”.

In the year **1501** **Ismail I** had himself proclaimed ruler in Tabriz. With this the **Safavid Empire** began. Ismail made **Twelver Shia Islam** the **state religion**. At that time most people in Iran were still Sunnis. To build up the new state religion, the Safavids brought many Shia scholars from **Jabal Amil** in present-day **Lebanon**.

In the west the empire bordered the Sunni **Ottoman Empire**. The two empires were rivals for a long time. In the year **1514** the Ottomans defeated the Safavids in the **battle of Chaldiran**. The Ottomans had many cannons and guns, which helped them greatly. After that the two empires often fought over the territories in between.

The best-known ruler was **Abbas I**, also called Abbas the Great. At the end of the 16th century he made **Isfahan** the **capital**. He had magnificent mosques, palaces, bridges and gardens built there. In the middle of the city the huge square **Naqsh-e Jahan** was created. Today it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

In the 18th century the empire grew weaker. In the year **1722** Afghan warriors conquered Isfahan. The power of the Safavids was broken by this, and a few years later their rule ended completely. Their legacy remained, however: Iran is still the country with the most **Shia** Muslims.

gewusst: Isfahan was so magnificent under the Safavids that people said Isfahan was half the world.
Ismail I was still a teenager when he was proclaimed ruler in 1501.

teile.einleitung: Mindfulness means consciously noticing what is happening right now, without judging it at once. The idea comes from Buddhism. Today mindfulness is also practised without religion, for example in courses against stress.
wichtigste: The Pali term for mindfulness is sati.
Right mindfulness is one part of the Noble Eightfold Path.
The Satipatthana Sutta describes four foundations of mindfulness.
Jon Kabat-Zinn developed the MBSR programme against stress in 1979.
A classic MBSR course lasts eight weeks.
Well-known exercises are the body scan and the mindful eating of a raisin.

abschnitte.text: In Pali, an ancient language of Buddhism, mindfulness is called **sati**. The word originally also means “remembering” or “making present”. **Right mindfulness** is one part of the Noble Eightfold Path. The **Satipatthana Sutta** describes four foundations: mindfulness is directed at the body, the feelings, the mind and the objects of the mind. This text is regarded as an important source of mindfulness practice.

In 1979 the doctor **Jon Kabat-Zinn** developed at the University of Massachusetts Medical School a programme called **Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction**, MBSR for short. He combined meditation from Buddhist traditions with a course without religion. A classic course lasts **eight weeks** with weekly meetings, a day of practice and daily exercises at home. Kabat-Zinn described mindfulness as attention that is **deliberate**, **in the present moment** and **non-judgemental**.

In the **body scan** one usually lies down and moves one's attention through the body, part by part, without changing anything. Participants often practise mindful eating for the first time with a **raisin**: it is looked at, felt, smelled and eaten very slowly. In this way an everyday action is experienced consciously. Mindful breathing and slow walking are also part of it.

From MBSR came **Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy** (MBCT). The researchers Segal, Williams and Teasdale combined mindfulness in it with cognitive behavioural therapy, originally to prevent relapses of **depression**. Today mindfulness courses are offered in hospitals, companies and schools, including in Switzerland. Mindfulness was also made known in the West by the Vietnamese monk **Thich Nhat Hanh**.

gewusst: One can practise mindfulness anywhere, for example when brushing one's teeth or waiting for the bus.
Studies show that MBCT can help people who have already had depression several times.

teile.einleitung: Islamic banks work according to the rules of Islam. The most important rule: they must not charge interest. Even so they earn money, and in a different way.
wichtigste: In Islamic banking, interest is forbidden.
The forbidden interest is called riba in Arabic.
In murabaha the bank buys a good and sells it on with a mark-up.
In mudaraba the investor and the entrepreneur share the profit.
Sukuk are Islamic bonds, and takaful is Islamic insurance.
Business with alcohol or gambling is forbidden.

abschnitte.text: The Quran forbids **riba**, which is usually understood as **interest**. Riba literally means “increase”. What is meant is a fixed, agreed profit from lent money. At an ordinary bank you pay interest for a loan. Islamic banks have to find other ways to earn money.

A common method is called **murabaha**. The bank buys, for example, a car and sells it on to the customer at a **higher, fixed price**. The customer pays off the price in instalments, without interest. In **mudaraba** one party brings the **capital** and the other his **work** and knowledge. Both share the profit according to an agreed formula.

**Sukuk** are Islamic bonds. Whoever buys sukuk gets a share in a real asset, such as a building. The return comes from **rents or profits** instead of from interest. **Takaful** is the Islamic form of insurance. The members pay into a common pot and help one another from it in case of loss.

Islamic banks may not invest in everything. Business with **alcohol**, **pork** or **gambling** is regarded as **haram**, that is, forbidden. A **board of scholars** therefore checks the bank's investments. The **Islamic Development Bank** was decided on in 1973 and began its work in 1975. It has its seat in **Jeddah** in Saudi Arabia and promotes projects in Muslim countries.

gewusst: Riba literally means “increase”.
Takaful works like a community that helps one another.

teile.einleitung: Ancestor worship means that people honour their dead forebears and stay connected with them. Many people believe that the ancestors watch over the family. Such customs exist in many parts of the world, especially in Africa and in China.
wichtigste: Ancestors are the forebears of a family: grandparents, great-grandparents and everyone before them.
Many people believe that the ancestors protect the family.
The ancestors are often given food and drink as offerings.
For important decisions, people ask them for advice and blessing.
In China, the Qingming Festival is an important day for the ancestors.
In Ghana there are colourful coffins in the shape of fish or cars.

abschnitte.text: **Ancestors** are the forebears of a family: grandparents, great-grandparents and all the generations before them. In many cultures they are not seen as completely gone after their death. People believe that they still belong to the family and **watch** over it. They can give advice and protection. That is why people remember and honour them.

In many parts of **Africa**, the ancestors are revered. People offer them **food and drink**, and sometimes pour a little of a drink onto the ground for them. At important events such as a wedding or a birth, the ancestors are called upon and asked for advice and blessing. **Ancestor figures** are often carved from wood. Families pass on stories about their ancestors so that they are not forgotten.

Among the **Yoruba** people in Nigeria there are the **Egungun** dances. People in splendid cloth costumes represent the ancestors returning. In **Ghana**, craftsmen build colourful coffins in many shapes, for example as a fish, a car or an aeroplane. The shape recalls the job or the interests of the dead person.

In **China** too, ancestor worship is very old. It is based on the virtue of **xiao**, filial piety, which Confucianism stresses. It requires respect and care for parents and forebears, even beyond death. At the **Qingming Festival** in spring, families visit the graves, clean them and bring offerings. The festival is a public holiday in China.

In Europe too, many people remember their dead. In Switzerland, many Catholic families visit the graves on **All Saints’ Day** and **All Souls’ Day** and light candles. In Mexico, people celebrate the **Day of the Dead** with colourful altars. The forms differ, but the idea is similar: the dead should not be forgotten.

gewusst: The coffins from Ghana are so artistic that some are displayed in museums.
Ancestor worship exists on every continent, in very different forms.

teile.einleitung: In Islam, sharia is the whole body of rules that is meant to follow from God's will. It concerns prayer and fasting as well as living together. Scholars have interpreted it for centuries, so there are different views.
wichtigste: The word sharia originally means “path to the watering place”.
The human legal science that interprets the sharia is called fiqh.
Classical Sunni sources are the Quran, sunna, consensus and analogy.
Actions are divided into five categories.
The ibadat regulate prayer, fasting and pilgrimage.
The maqasid are the overarching aims of the sharia.

abschnitte.text: The Arabic word **sharia** originally meant **“path to the watering place”**. In the desert this path is vital. In a figurative sense it means the way that God shows to people. The sharia is not a single law book. It is a web of rules that scholars derive from the sources.

The human legal science that interprets the sharia is called **fiqh**. Classical Sunni teaching names four sources: the **Quran**, the **sunna**, the **consensus** of scholars and **analogy**. The discipline that examines the methods and sources of legal reasoning is called **usul al-fiqh**. The founding work is regarded as the **Risala** of the scholar al-Shafi'i. Because human beings interpret, different schools of law arose.

The Islamic theory of norms divides human actions into **five categories**. An action can be obligatory, recommended, permitted, disliked or forbidden. The area that regulates prayer, fasting and pilgrimage is called **ibadat**, that is, acts of worship. Besides this there are rules for living together, for example for trade and contracts.

The **maqasid al-sharia** are the overarching aims of the sharia. Scholars count among them, for example, the protection of life, reason and property. How the sharia should be applied today is disputed among Muslims. In many countries it concerns mainly personal religious life. In Switzerland Swiss law applies to everyone, and Muslims live their religious rules within this law.

gewusst: The Risala of al-Shafi'i came into being over 1,100 years ago.
Many rules of the sharia concern everyday matters such as cleanliness, food and politeness.

teile.einleitung: The Eightfold Path is in Buddhism the way that is meant to lead out of suffering. It consists of eight parts that one can practise like steps in everyday life. It is the fourth of the Four Noble Truths.
wichtigste: The Eightfold Path has eight parts, which all begin with the word “right”.
The parts are right view, intention, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness and concentration.
They are divided into three groups: wisdom, ethical conduct and mental development.
Right speech means, among other things, not lying and not slandering.
Right livelihood means practising an occupation that does not harm others.
The symbol of the path is a wheel with eight spokes.

abschnitte.text: The Buddha taught the **Four Noble Truths**: there is suffering, it has a cause, it can end, and there is a way to that end. This way is the **Eightfold Path**. It is regarded as the **middle way** between a life of excess and strict self-torment. In the usual English translation the word **“right”** stands before each part. By this is meant “correct” or “wholesome”.

Two parts belong to the group of **wisdom** (prajna). **Right view** means understanding the world correctly, for example the Four Noble Truths. **Right intention** means resolving on what is good: kindness instead of hatred and compassion instead of violence. These two parts set the direction for the whole path.

**Ethical conduct** includes right speech, right action and right livelihood. **Right speech** means speaking honestly, kindly and meaningfully and avoiding lies, slander, harsh words and gossip. **Right action** means, for example, not killing and not stealing. **Right livelihood** means earning one's money without harm to others. Things such as the arms trade or fraud are rejected.

The last group is called **mental development** or meditation. **Right effort** means avoiding bad thoughts and encouraging good qualities with perseverance. **Right mindfulness** means perceiving body, feelings and thoughts wakefully and without judgement. **Right concentration** (samadhi) is the eighth part: a calm, fully collected mind in meditation.

gewusst: The eight parts are not ticked off one after another, but are meant to be practised together.
The wheel with eight spokes, the dharma wheel, is one of the best-known signs of Buddhism.

teile.einleitung: Muslim burial sections are special areas in cemeteries where Muslims are buried according to their religious rules. In Switzerland such sections have existed since 1978. They are mostly in public cemeteries of the municipalities.
wichtigste: Muslim graves are aligned towards Mecca.
The first Muslim burial section in Switzerland was created in 1978 in Geneva.
Bern and Basel opened Muslim burial sections in 2000, and Zurich followed in 2004.
The deceased are, by tradition, buried in a shroud.
Islam rejects cremation.
In Switzerland the municipalities are usually responsible for cemeteries.

abschnitte.text: According to Muslim tradition, the deceased are laid in the grave so that their face points **towards Mecca**. That is why all the graves of a Muslim burial section are aligned in the same way. In an ordinary cemetery the graves often lie differently. That is why separate areas are needed, the **burial sections**.

Before the burial the body of the deceased person is carefully **washed**. Then it is wrapped in a white **shroud**. The burial should take place **as quickly as possible**, if possible within one to two days. Islam rejects **cremation**. Before the burial the relatives and guests pray together a special prayer for the dead.

The first Muslim burial section in Switzerland was created in **1978** in **Geneva**. In **2000** **Bern** and **Basel** followed, and in **2004** the city of **Zurich** opened its section. Today there are such areas in several more towns and municipalities. In Switzerland the **municipalities** are usually responsible for cemeteries. That is why they also decide about burial sections.

According to Muslim belief, a grave should remain **for ever**. In Swiss cemeteries, however, graves are usually **cleared** after a few decades so that the space can be used again. Here municipalities and Muslim communities are looking for solutions. Some families therefore have their dead buried in their country of origin.

gewusst: Many Muslim graves have a simple gravestone, often with Arabic script.
Jewish communities in Switzerland also want graves to remain undisturbed for ever and have cemeteries of their own.

teile.einleitung: Calligraphy is the art of beautiful writing. In the Islamic world it is one of the most important arts of all. With artful script people decorate books, walls and even whole mosques.
wichtigste: Calligraphy means writing letters especially beautifully.
In mosques people decorate with script instead of with pictures of people.
Often verses from the Quran or names of God are written.
Traditionally people write with a reed pen, the qalam.
Kufic is an old angular script, naskh a round and easily legible one.
Calligraphers learned for many years with a master.

abschnitte.text: In mosques there are no pictures of people or animals. Instead the rooms are decorated with **beautiful script** and patterns. Calligraphers often write **verses from the Quran** or the **names of God**. Because these words are holy, calligraphy is especially valuable for Muslims. A **calligrapher** was therefore very highly regarded in the Islamic world.

Traditionally people do not write with a fountain pen but with a **reed**. The reed is cut at a slant and dipped in ink. This pen is called a **qalam**. Because of the slanting cut, the lines become thick or thin depending on direction. This is how the sweeping forms of the Arabic letters arise.

There are many styles of script. The **Kufic script** is old and has angular letters. It is named after the city of **Kufa** in present-day Iraq. The **naskh script** has round, clear letters. Because it is easy to read, many books are still printed in it today.

Some calligraphers write words so that together they form a **shape**, such as a bird, a lion or a ship. In this way writing becomes a picture. The Ottoman sultans had an artful monogram, the **tughra**. It stood, for example, on documents and coins, like a signature.

Calligraphy cannot be learned quickly. Pupils practised **for many years with a master**. They copied the same letters again and again. Only when the master was satisfied were they allowed to **sign** their works themselves. Even today there are calligraphers who carry on this old art.

gewusst: The qalam is made from a reed cut at a slant.
The tughra of a sultan was so artful that it could hardly be forged.
The Kufic script bears the name of a city in present-day Iraq.

teile.einleitung: The sunna is the transmitted way of life of the Prophet Muhammad. It comprises what he said, did and silently approved. After the Quran it is the most important source of Islamic faith and law.
wichtigste: “Sunna” originally means custom or habitual way of acting.
After the Quran it is the second source of Islamic law.
It is recorded above all in the hadith collections.
The sunna also includes what Muhammad silently approved.
Sunna prayers are voluntary additional prayers.
Before eating, according to the sunna, people say “Bismillah”.

abschnitte.text: The Arabic word **sunna** originally means **custom** or **habitual way of acting**. In Islam it means the way of life of the Prophet **Muhammad**. This includes his **words**, his **deeds** and also what he **silently approved**. For Muslims he is a model in faith and in everyday life. The name “Sunnis” is also derived from this word.

The sunna is recorded in writing above all in the **hadith collections**. A hadith is a report of what Muhammad said or did. Scholars checked carefully who had passed a report on. In Islamic law the sunna is the **second source after the Quran**. It explains and supplements what the Quran says briefly.

Besides the obligatory prayers there are **sunna prayers**. These are **voluntary additional prayers** that Muhammad prayed regularly. Many Muslims pray them before or after the obligatory prayers. They are regarded as recommended but not as a duty. Whoever prays them follows the example of the Prophet.

Many small habits go back to the sunna. Before eating people say **“Bismillah”**, which means “In the name of God”. Anyone who has sneezed says **“Al-hamdu lillah”**, that is, “Praise be to God”. For dental care Muhammad used the **miswak**, a small wooden stick made from twigs. Even today some Muslims use the miswak alongside the toothbrush.

gewusst: The miswak is usually made from twigs of the toothbrush tree.
A single hadith often comes with a long list of the people who passed it on.

teile.einleitung: The Alpsegen is an old prayer that the herdsman calls out on the mountain pasture in the evening. He asks God and the saints to protect people and animals. The custom is heard above all in the Catholic Alpine regions of Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Alpsegen is a prayer that is half sung and half called out.
It is also known as the Betruf, or “prayer call”.
The herdsman usually calls it in the evening after work.
So that his voice carries far, he calls through a milk funnel.
The Alpsegen is meant to protect people and animals from bad weather and misfortune.
It is heard above all in central Switzerland, eastern Switzerland and Upper Valais.

abschnitte.text: In summer, many cows live on the **mountain pasture**, looked after by the **herdsman**, called the **Senn**. In the evening, when the work is done and it grows dark, he stands in a raised spot and calls the **Alpsegen**. It is half sung and half called. Because the herdsman is calling a prayer, the Alpsegen is also called the **Betruf**. It can be heard far across the meadows.

So that his voice carries as far as possible, the herdsman calls through a **milk funnel** made of wood or metal. The funnel works like a megaphone. Normally it is used to pour milk into churns. In the Alpsegen it becomes an instrument that sends the call across the whole pasture.

In the Alpsegen, the herdsman calls on **God**, **Mary** and various **saints**. He asks them to protect the **people and animals** on the pasture. Up on the mountain there are threats such as thunderstorms, rockfall and accidents, and the Alpsegen asks for protection from **bad weather and misfortune**. In some versions it says that a golden ring should be drawn around the pasture to keep all evil away. The texts differ from region to region.

The Alpsegen is a **Catholic** custom. It is heard above all in **central Switzerland**, for example in Uri, Obwalden and Nidwalden, but also in **eastern Switzerland** and **Upper Valais**. The call is often passed down within a family or on a pasture over many generations. The Alpsegen is one of the living traditions of Switzerland.

gewusst: An Alpsegen can last several minutes and is called from memory, without any music written down.
Because the texts were only passed on by word of mouth, every pasture has its own versions.

teile.einleitung: Nuh is the name of Noah in the Quran. He is one of the great prophets in Islam. His story of the ark and the great flood is also known to Judaism and Christianity.
wichtigste: Noah is called Nuh in the Quran.
At God's command Nuh built a great ship, the ark.
The ark saved him and his family from a great flood.
Of every kind of animal he took a pair with him.
According to the Quran the ark came to rest on Mount Judi.
The 71st surah is called Surah Nuh.

abschnitte.text: According to the Quran, God sent **Nuh** to his people. He was to call on people to believe in God alone and to do good. According to the Quran, Nuh lived **950 years** among his people and warned them again and again. But only a few listened to him. Most mocked him and stayed with their old gods.

God commanded Nuh to build a **great ship**, the **ark**. Nuh set to work. When people came past, they **laughed at him**, for there was no sea far and wide. Nuh was not put off. He took his family, the few believers and **a pair** of every kind of animal with him on the ship.

Then came the **great flood**. Water poured from the sky and from the earth, and the waves became as high as mountains. A **son of Nuh** refused to board the ark. He wanted to save himself on a mountain, but the flood seized him. The people in the ark, however, were saved.

When the water went down, according to the Quran the ark came to rest on Mount **Judi**. In the Bible the place is called Ararat instead. Nuh and the saved could leave the ship and begin anew. In the Quran a whole surah is named after him, **Surah Nuh**. It is the 71st surah.

gewusst: Stories of a great flood exist in many ancient cultures, for example in ancient Mesopotamia too.
According to the Quran, Nuh is one of the prophets with especially great steadfastness.

teile.einleitung: The minbar is the pulpit in a mosque. It looks like a small staircase leading to a raised place. From there the preacher gives the sermon at the Friday prayer.
wichtigste: A minbar is a pulpit with steps.
It is used mainly for the Friday sermon.
The sermon is called khutba in Arabic.
The minbar usually stands to the right of the mihrab.
Muhammad himself preached in Medina from a simple wooden minbar.

abschnitte.text: The **minbar** consists of a narrow **staircase** with several steps. At the top there is a small seat or platform, often with a roof above it. It stands at the wall that points to Mecca, usually to the **right** of the **mihrab**. From up there the preacher can be seen and heard in the whole room. Many minbars are carved from wood, others are made of marble.

On Friday at midday Muslims come to the mosque for the communal **Friday prayer**. Beforehand the preacher gives a sermon from the minbar, the **khutba**. It deals with faith, with living together and with good deeds. There is also such a sermon at the great festivals. At the daily prayers, by contrast, the minbar is not used.

According to tradition, the Prophet **Muhammad** at first preached in Medina leaning against a palm trunk. Later he got a simple wooden minbar with a few steps. Since then the minbar has been part of every larger mosque. One of the oldest surviving minbars stands in the Great Mosque of **Kairouan** in Tunisia and dates from the 9th century.

gewusst: According to tradition, the first caliph Abu Bakr, out of respect, stood one step lower than Muhammad had stood.

teile.einleitung: The Diyanet is the state religious authority of Turkey. Its full name in English is “Presidency of Religious Affairs”. It manages the mosques in the country and is also active abroad, for example in Germany and Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Diyanet was founded in 1924.
It is responsible for Sunni Islam in Turkey.
It employs the imams and sets the texts of the Friday sermon.
Since 2018 it has been under the president.
In Germany the mosque association DITIB is closely linked to it.
The Alevis do not feel represented by the Diyanet.

abschnitte.text: In Turkish the authority is called **Diyanet İşleri Başkanlığı**, in English the **Presidency of Religious Affairs**. It was founded in **1924**, shortly after the founding of the Republic of Turkey. It is responsible for matters of **Sunni Islam** in the country. It used to be attached to the prime minister. Since the introduction of the presidential system in **2018** it has been directly under the **president**.

The Diyanet manages tens of thousands of **mosques** in Turkey. The **imams** there are state employees and are paid by the state. Every week the authority issues a uniform **Friday sermon** that is read out across the whole country. In this way the state influences what is taught in the mosques.

The Diyanet sends **imams** to countries such as Germany, Austria or Switzerland. They stay for a few years and are paid as Turkish civil servants. In Germany the association **DITIB** is closely linked to the Diyanet. It was founded in 1984 and is one of the largest mosque associations there. In 2018 the **DITIB Central Mosque** in Cologne-Ehrenfeld was opened, designed by the architect Paul Böhm.

The Diyanet is much discussed. Supporters say it provides well-trained imams and an orderly religious life. Critics think the Turkish state thereby has too much influence on mosques abroad. Some therefore demand that more imams be trained in the country itself. The **Alevis** in Turkey pray in the **cemevi** and do not feel represented by the Sunni-oriented Diyanet. They demand recognition of their own.

gewusst: The Diyanet was founded in 1924, in the same year in which Turkey abolished the caliphate.
In Switzerland too there are Turkish mosque associations that are linked to the Diyanet.

teile.einleitung: The Islamic obligatory prayer follows a fixed sequence of body postures. People stand, bow, prostrate themselves and sit. Every posture has its own Arabic name and a meaning.
wichtigste: A complete unit of prayer is called a rak'a.
Standing upright is called qiyam, and during it passages are recited from the Quran.
The bow with the hands on the knees is called ruku.
In the prostration, sujud, the forehead touches the ground.
In every rak'a people prostrate themselves twice.
The prayer ends with the greeting of peace to the right and to the left.

abschnitte.text: A prayer consists of several **rak'as**. A rak'a is a sequence of standing, bowing, prostrating and sitting. Depending on the prayer there are two, three or four units. Before the prayer people wash and turn towards Mecca. The movements are the same for everyone, whatever country they pray in.

Every unit begins standing, in the **qiyam**. The word means “standing”. In this posture people recite the surah **al-Fatiha**, the first surah of the Quran. Its name means “the Opening”. Without it a unit of prayer is not complete. After it, further verses can follow.

After standing comes the **ruku**. People bow with a straight back and put their hands on their knees. In doing so they praise God with short words. Then they straighten up again. Only then does the prostration follow.

In the **sujud** people kneel and put the forehead on the ground. According to a hadith, **seven parts of the body** touch the ground: forehead with nose, both hands, both knees and the toes of both feet. This posture is regarded as a sign of the greatest **humility** before God. In every rak'a two prostrations follow. In between people sit briefly on their heels.

At the end people sit and speak a declaration of faith. Then they turn the head to the right and to the left and say **“As-salamu alaykum”**, peace be with you. This conclusion is called **taslim**. With it the prayer is finished. Many then stay sitting a little longer and speak personal requests.

gewusst: The Arabic word for mosque, masjid, means “place of prostration”.
Anyone who is ill may also perform the prayer sitting or lying down.

teile.einleitung: An astrolabe is an old instrument for measuring the night sky. With it people could measure the height of the sun and stars and work out the time and the compass directions. In the Islamic world it was greatly improved and was widespread for centuries.
wichtigste: With the astrolabe people determined the positions of stars and the time.
Muslims also used it to determine the times of prayer.
The basic idea comes from ancient Greece.
The word literally means “star taker”.
Most astrolabes were made of brass.
Mariam al-Astrulabi built famous astrolabes in Aleppo in the 10th century.

abschnitte.text: The word **astrolabe** comes from Greek: “astron” means star and “lambanein” to take. So it means roughly **“star taker”**. With the instrument you measure how high a star or the sun stands **above the horizon**. From this you can read off the time, the compass directions and much more. It is a kind of calculating device for the night sky.

An astrolabe is usually a round disc of **brass**, a mixture of copper and zinc. Brass is sturdy and can be engraved finely. On the back there is a rotating pointer with a **sighting device**: with it you aim at a star and read the angle on a scale. On the front lies the **rete**, an openwork grid with pointers for bright stars. When you turn it, it shows the sky at a particular time.

Greek scholars of antiquity already knew the basic idea. In the **Islamic world** the instrument was greatly improved and widely used. It was especially useful because the five daily **prayers** depend on the position of the sun. With the astrolabe the times of prayer could be determined exactly. Through Muslim Spain the knowledge later reached Europe.

In the 10th century there lived in **Aleppo** in present-day Syria a woman who was famous for her skilful astrolabes: **Mariam al-Astrulabi**. Her nickname means “the astrolabe maker”. She worked for the ruler of Aleppo. In her honour an **asteroid** was later named after her.

gewusst: For centuries a good astrolabe was something like a computer for astrologers, sailors and scholars.
Many astrolabes are so beautifully decorated that today they are displayed as works of art in museums.

teile.einleitung: Islam came to China with traders over 1,000 years ago. Today several ethnic groups are mostly Muslim, together over 20 million people. The largest groups are the Hui and the Uyghurs.
wichtigste: The Hui are Chinese-speaking Muslims and live in many parts of China.
The autonomous region of Ningxia is named after the Hui.
In China ten mostly Muslim ethnic groups are officially recognised.
The Huaisheng Mosque in Guangzhou is among the oldest mosques in China.
The Id Kah Mosque in Kashgar is regarded as the largest mosque in China.
Since about 2017 there have been reports of internment camps for Uyghurs in Xinjiang.

abschnitte.text: Arab and Persian **sea traders** came early by sea to **Guangzhou** in the south of China. There stands the **Huaisheng Mosque**, one of the oldest mosques in China. According to tradition it goes back to the **Tang period**. Other traders came along the Silk Road from Central Asia. Many settled in China.

In China **ten** mostly Muslim ethnic groups are officially recognised. They include **Hui**, **Uyghurs**, Kazakhs, Kyrgyz, Uzbeks, Tajiks, Tatars, Salar, Dongxiang and Bonan. The Hui speak **Chinese** and live in many parts of the country. They are partly descended from Arab, Persian and Central Asian traders who married Chinese women. The **Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region** is named after them, and about a third of the population there are Hui.

The **Great Mosque of Xi'an** looks like a Chinese temple. It has curved roofs, courtyards and a pagoda instead of a minaret. In this way Islam adapted to the local **architecture**. Quite different is the **Id Kah Mosque** in **Kashgar** in the west of the country. It is regarded as the largest mosque in China and was for a long time the religious centre of the Uyghurs.

Since **2015** the government under Xi Jinping has called for a **Sinicisation of religions**. Religions are supposed to adapt to Chinese culture. At many mosques, domes and minarets were therefore removed or rebuilt. Since about **2017**, media and UN bodies have reported **internment camps** for Uyghurs in **Xinjiang**. China describes them as vocational training centres. A report by the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights spoke in 2022 of possible crimes against humanity.

gewusst: In China mosques are often called “Qingzhensi”, which means roughly “temple of purity and truth”.
The Great Mosque of Xi'an has no classic minaret but a pagoda.

teile.einleitung: Muslims today form the third largest religious community in Switzerland. Their share of the population has grown strongly since 1970. Many of them come from families who immigrated from the Balkans or Turkey.
wichtigste: In 2023, according to the FSO, about 6 per cent of the population belonged to a Muslim community.
In 1970 it was only 0.2 per cent, and in 2000 about 4 per cent.
Muslim communities are in 2023 the third largest group after Catholics and Reformed.
In the canton of Zurich, according to a statement of 2025, about 100,000 Muslims live.
According to the FSO survey of 2024, about 37 per cent pray daily or almost daily.
The Ahmadiyya community has about 700 members in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: In **1970**, according to the Federal Statistical Office (**FSO**), only **0.2 per cent** of the population belonged to Islam. In the census of **2000** it was already **about 4 per cent**. In **2023** about **6 per cent** of the population belonged to a Muslim community. This puts them in **third place**, after Catholics and Reformed.

Many Muslims in Switzerland have roots in **Kosovo**, **North Macedonia**, **Bosnia** or **Turkey**. Their families often came to Switzerland as workers or refugees. Many were born here and hold a Swiss passport. In the **canton of Zurich**, according to a statement of the canton of 2025, about **100,000** Muslims lived.

How strongly someone lives their faith is very different. According to an FSO survey of **2024**, about **91 per cent** of Muslims in Switzerland believe in one single God. About **37 per cent** pray daily or almost daily. About **a fifth** attend a service or a religious event at least once a week. Others live their faith more privately.

The Muslims in Switzerland do not form a uniform group. Most are **Sunnis**; besides them there are **Shia**, Alevis and other branches. Many associations are organised by language and origin. A small community is the **Ahmadiyya** with about **700** members. It built the first mosque with a minaret in Switzerland in Zurich in 1963.

gewusst: The share of Muslims in Switzerland has grown many times over since 1970.
In Switzerland the cantons, not the federal government, regulate how religious communities are recognised.

teile.einleitung: Sawm is the Arabic word for fasting. In the fasting month of Ramadan, Muslims neither eat nor drink from dawn until sunset. Fasting is one of the five pillars of Islam.
wichtigste: People fast in Ramadan, the ninth month of the Islamic calendar.
The fast lasts every day from dawn until sunset.
The Quran commands fasting in surah 2, al-Baqara.
Ramadan shifts forward by about 11 days every year.
Sick people are exempt from fasting.
The meal before the start of the fasting day is called suhur.

abschnitte.text: People fast in **Ramadan**, the **ninth month** of the Islamic calendar. This calendar follows the moon and is shorter than our solar year. That is why Ramadan moves forward **by about 11 days** every year. So over the years it falls once in summer and once in winter. In the Quran fasting is commanded in **surah 2**, al-Baqara.

The fast begins with **dawn** and ends with **sunset**. During this time those fasting neither eat nor drink. Before morning many take a meal, which is called **suhur**. In the evening the fast is broken together, and this meal is called **iftar**. Often people begin with water and dates. In Switzerland the days of fasting are especially long in summer.

abschnitte.titel: Who does not have to fast
abschnitte.text: Not everyone has to fast. **Sick people** are exempt, as are children who are not yet grown up. Older people for whom fasting is harmful do not have to fast either. Anyone who misses days because of a **journey** **makes them up later**. Anyone who cannot fast permanently can instead support the needy with food.

In Ramadan many Muslims pray additional prayers in the mosque in the evening, which are called **tarawih**. Many read the whole Quran in this month. People should also be especially friendly and help the needy. At the end of Ramadan the **festival of breaking the fast** is celebrated, in Turkish also called the Sugar Festival. Then families visit one another and give presents to children.

gewusst: Because Ramadan moves, a person experiences Ramadan in all the seasons in about 33 years.
Depending on the place on Earth, a day of fasting is of very different length.

teile.einleitung: Amida Buddhism is a branch of Mahayana Buddhism. Its followers trust in the Buddha Amitabha and hope to be reborn in his Pure Land. It is especially widespread in China and Japan.
wichtigste: Amitabha means “Immeasurable Light”; in Japanese he is called Amida.
His Pure Land is called Sukhavati, the “Land of Bliss”.
According to tradition it lies in the west.
The central practice is the nembutsu, in Japanese “Namu Amida Butsu”.
Honen founded the Jodo-shu in 1175, and his pupil Shinran founded the Jodo Shinshu.
In China, Huiyuan is regarded as the first patriarch of the Pure Land school.

abschnitte.text: **Amitabha** means “Immeasurable Light”, and the related name Amitayus means “Immeasurable Life”. In Japanese he is called **Amida**. According to the longer **Sukhavati Sutra**, he was once a bodhisattva named **Dharmakara**. He made 48 vows and so became a Buddha. The 18th vow promises rebirth in his Pure Land to everyone who calls on him with trust.

Amitabha’s Pure Land is called **Sukhavati**, the “Land of Bliss”. According to tradition it lies in the **west**, which is why believers speak of the “Western Paradise”. Anyone who is reborn there can reach **enlightenment** under ideal conditions. Amitabha is often accompanied by two bodhisattvas, including Avalokiteshvara, called Kannon in Japan.

The most important practice is the **nembutsu**, the calling on the Buddha Amida. In Japanese the formula is **“Namu Amida Butsu”**, in Chinese “Namo Amituofo”. Believers often repeat it many times, sometimes with a string of prayer beads. In China, **Huiyuan** is regarded as the first patriarch of this school. In the year 402 he founded a community on Mount Lushan that focused on Amitabha.

In Japan, **Honen** founded the **Jodo-shu**, the Pure Land school, in 1175. He taught that simply reciting the nembutsu leads to rebirth in the Pure Land. In this way he opened the path to people of every social class. His pupil **Shinran** founded the **Jodo Shinshu**, the “True Pure Land school”. He stressed **tariki**, “other power”: liberation comes through Amida’s power alone, not through one’s own effort, which is called jiriki.

gewusst: The famous Great Buddha of Kamakura in Japan represents Amida.
The Jodo Shinshu became one of the largest Buddhist schools in Japan.

teile.einleitung: Turkey is a country in which most people are Muslims. At the same time its constitution has long separated state and religion. This mixture of old Islamic history and a modern state makes Turkey special.
wichtigste: Islam came to Anatolia in the 11th century with the Seljuks.
Most Muslims in Turkey are Sunnis and follow the Hanafi school of law.
Besides them there is a large Alevi minority.
Atatürk abolished the caliphate in 1924.
Since 1937 secularism has been in the constitution.
The state authority Diyanet manages mosques and imams.
The Hagia Sophia has been a mosque again since 2020.

abschnitte.text: After the battle of **Manzikert** in 1071 the Muslim **Seljuks** advanced into Anatolia. In this way Islam came to the area of present-day Turkey. Later the **Ottomans** founded a great empire. Their sultans also bore the title of **caliph**, the leader of the Muslims. In the Ottoman Empire the **Hanafi school of law** was the official branch.

After the First World War **Mustafa Kemal Atatürk** founded modern Turkey. In 1924 parliament abolished the **caliphate**. The last caliph, Abdulmejid II, had to leave the country. In 1937 **secularism** entered the constitution. This means that state and religion are separate.

Despite the separation, the state takes great care of religion. The **Presidency of Religious Affairs**, **Diyanet** for short, was created in 1924. It manages mosques, pays the **imams** and even writes the Friday sermons. In this way the state has influence over what is taught in the mosques.

The most famous master builder of the Ottomans was **Mimar Sinan**. In the 16th century he designed over 300 buildings, for example the **Süleymaniye Mosque** in Istanbul and the **Selimiye Mosque** in Edirne. The **Hagia Sophia** was first a church, then a mosque and from 1934 a museum. Since 2020 it has been used as a mosque again. The largest mosque in the country is the **Çamlıca Mosque**, opened in 2019, on the Asian side of Istanbul.

The great majority of Muslims in Turkey are **Sunnis**. Most still follow the Hanafi school of law today. Besides them there is a large minority of **Alevis**, who have their own customs and meeting places. In Switzerland many people with roots in Turkey live, and here too there are Turkish mosque associations.

gewusst: The Diyanet writes Friday sermons that are delivered in very many mosques at the same time.
The Çamlıca Mosque has room for tens of thousands of worshippers.
Mimar Sinan designed over 300 buildings.

teile.einleitung: “Halal” is an Arabic word and means “permitted”. It describes everything that Muslims may eat and do under the rules of their religion. The word is especially well known in connection with food.
wichtigste: Halal means permitted; the opposite, haram, means forbidden.
Vegetables, fruit and grain are halal.
Pork and alcohol are not permitted for devout Muslims.
Meat of chicken, beef, sheep or goat is halal if the animal was slaughtered according to Islamic rules.
Fish is regarded by most Muslims as halal.
Halal food may be eaten by everyone.

abschnitte.text: **Halal** means “permitted”, **haram** means “forbidden”. What is haram, devout Muslims should not eat or do. The rules come from the **Quran** and from tradition. They concern not only food but also behaviour in everyday life. When shopping, however, the word is heard most often.

Plant foods such as **vegetables, fruit and grain** are in principle permitted. Meat of **chicken, beef, sheep or goat** is halal if the animal was slaughtered according to the Islamic rules. **Fish** and other sea creatures are regarded by most Muslims as halal even without special slaughter. Halal food is completely normal food that meets certain rules. That is why everyone may eat it.

**Pork** is always forbidden. **Alcohol** too is not permitted in Islam, so devout Muslims drink no wine and no beer. Many also avoid alcohol that is hidden in foods such as sauces or cakes. Some also watch for ingredients such as gelatine, which can be obtained from pigs.

In the shop, halal products can often be recognised by a **halal mark** or seal on the packaging. In Switzerland, slaughtering mammals **without stunning is forbidden**. That is why a large part of halal meat is imported from **abroad**. In Swiss cities there are butchers and shops that offer halal meat.

gewusst: Judaism too has food rules; there, permitted food is called kosher.
The ban on slaughter without stunning has applied in Switzerland since 1893.

teile.einleitung: Devout Muslims pray five times a day at fixed times. These prayer times follow the course of the sun. That is why they shift over the course of the year.
wichtigste: The fajr prayer is at dawn.
The zuhr prayer is at midday, the asr prayer in the afternoon.
The maghrib prayer follows shortly after sunset.
The isha prayer at night is the last obligatory prayer.
On Friday the Friday prayer with a sermon replaces the midday prayer.
The maghrib prayer is the only obligatory prayer with three units of prayer.

abschnitte.text: The day begins with the **fajr** prayer. People perform it between dawn and sunrise. The second prayer is **zuhr**. It begins when the sun has passed its highest point. On Friday many people meet at this time in the mosque for the **Friday prayer**, in Arabic jumu'a. It begins with a sermon and then replaces the midday prayer.

In the later afternoon the **asr** prayer follows. Its time ends before sunset. Directly after sunset the **maghrib** prayer begins, the fourth of the day. Last comes the **isha** prayer, when it has become fully dark. After it no further obligatory prayer follows.

Every prayer consists of **units of prayer**, which are called rak'a. The morning prayer has two, the evening prayer three and the other obligatory prayers four units each. Maghrib is therefore the only obligatory prayer with three units. Many people also pray additional voluntary units.

The prayer times depend on the **position of the sun**, for example on twilight, midday and sunset. In Switzerland they are therefore far apart in summer and close together in winter. Mosques and apps publish tables with the exact times. According to tradition, people should not pray exactly at **sunrise**, at the highest point of the sun and at sunset. In this way the prayer is clearly distinguished from worship of the sun.

gewusst: The call to prayer, with which people are invited to the prayers, is called the adhan.
Because the times depend on the place, people in Geneva pray a few minutes later than in St Gallen.

teile.einleitung: In China, many families have honoured their dead forebears for thousands of years. They set out food for them, light incense sticks and look after their graves. Ancestor worship is closely linked to the teachings of Confucius.
wichtigste: On the household altar there are ancestor tablets with the names of the dead.
Incense sticks are lit for the ancestors.
Paper money and paper objects are burned as offerings.
Large extended families built their own ancestral halls.
At the Ghost Festival in the seventh lunar month, people feed wandering ghosts.
Traditionally, white is the colour of mourning in China.

abschnitte.text: In many Chinese families there is a **household altar**. On it stand **ancestor tablets**, wooden tablets with the names of the dead. In front of them people place food, fruit or tea. They light **incense sticks**, whose smoke is meant to create a link with the ancestors. People often bow in front of the altar as they do so.

Families often burn **paper money**, known as spirit money, for the dead. Houses, cars or clothes made of paper are burned too. According to the belief, the ancestors will receive these things in the afterlife. In this way the family goes on looking after its forebears, just as it did during their lifetimes.

Large extended families, called **clans**, often built their own **ancestral halls**. The ancestor tablets of many generations stood there, and people met there for ceremonies. Traditionally the **eldest son** led the offerings to the ancestors. That is why it used to be very important to have a son.

In **Confucianism**, ancestor worship is very important. The virtue of **xiao**, filial piety, requires respect for one’s parents. According to Confucian teaching, this respect does not end with death. Through offerings and remembrance, the family stays connected across many generations.

At the **Qingming Festival** in spring, families visit the graves, clean them and bring offerings. On the 15th day of the seventh lunar month, people celebrate the **Ghost Festival**. According to folk belief, the gates of the afterlife stand open during this month. People put out food for hungry ghosts that nobody honours any more. At funerals, relatives traditionally wear **white**, because white is the colour of mourning, while red is the colour of good fortune.

gewusst: The paper money for the ancestors often shows very large sums, so that the dead have enough in the afterlife.
Ancestor worship exists not only in China but also in Taiwan and among many Chinese people all over the world.

teile.einleitung: Islamism is a political ideology. Its followers want to reshape state and society according to their understanding of Islamic rules. Islamism must be distinguished from Islam as a religion: most Muslims are not Islamists.
wichtigste: Islamism is a political ideology, not a religion.
Hasan al-Banna founded the Muslim Brotherhood in Egypt in 1928.
Maududi founded the Jamaat-e-Islami in British India in 1941.
Sayyid Qutb wrote the book “Milestones”.
Legalist Islamists rely on elections, jihadists on violence.
Hamas emerged in 1987 from the Muslim Brotherhood.

abschnitte.text: In scholarship, **Islamism** describes political movements that want to enforce an **Islamic order** according to their understanding. This concerns state, law and society. Islamism must be distinguished from **Islam as a religion**. There are very different Islamist groups, from parties to violent organisations.

The teacher **Hasan al-Banna** founded the **Muslim Brotherhood** in 1928 in Ismailia in Egypt. It became the most influential Islamist organisation of the Arab world. In British India **Abul A'la Maududi** founded the **Jamaat-e-Islami** in 1941 in Lahore. After the partition of India it became active above all in Pakistan and Bangladesh.

Maududi and the Egyptian **Sayyid Qutb** put **hakimiyya** at the centre, the “sovereignty of God”. According to it, God alone is the lawgiver, and laws made by human beings were rejected. Qutb wrote the book “Milestones” in prison and was executed in 1966. He called societies that he regarded as un-Islamic **jahiliyya**. The word actually means the pre-Islamic time of “ignorance”. His ideas strongly influenced radical groups.

Research distinguishes various currents. **Legalist Islamists** pursue their aims through **elections and parties**. An example is the Tunisian party **Ennahda** under Rached Ghannouchi. It won the first free elections after the Arab Spring in 2011 and declared in 2016 that it wanted to separate religious mission and politics. **Jihadists**, by contrast, rely on **violence**. The Palestinian **Hamas** emerged in 1987 from the Palestinian branch of the Muslim Brotherhood.

gewusst: The Muslim Brotherhood was founded by a teacher.
The word jahiliyya originally described the time before Islam.

teile.einleitung: Saudi Arabia is a kingdom on the Arabian Peninsula. Here lie Mecca and Medina, the two holiest places of Islam. The country became rich through oil and is today trying to broaden its economy.
wichtigste: Abd al-Aziz ibn Saud proclaimed the kingdom in 1932.
The capital is Riyadh.
Since 1986 the king has borne the title “Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques”.
Non-Muslims may not enter the city of Mecca.
The Hajj takes place in the month of Dhu al-Hijja.
The reform programme “Vision 2030” was presented in 2016.

abschnitte.text: Saudi Arabia is an **absolute monarchy**, and the king has a great deal of power. The state is named after the **Saud** family. **Abd al-Aziz ibn Saud** united large parts of the peninsula and proclaimed the kingdom in **1932**. Since then his descendants have ruled. Since **1986** the king has officially borne the title **“Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques”**, meaning Mecca and Medina.

Every year very many Muslims come to Mecca on pilgrimage, the **Hajj**. It takes place in the month of **Dhu al-Hijja**, the last month of the Islamic calendar. The high point is regarded as the **standing at Mount Arafat**, without which the Hajj is not valid. **Non-Muslims** may not enter the city of Mecca. The country is therefore especially important for Muslims all over the world.

Saudi Arabia has very large **oil reserves** and is among the biggest oil exporters in the world. Selling oil brought the country great wealth. Because oil may one day become scarce, the government presented the programme **“Vision 2030”** in **2016**. It is meant to make the economy less dependent on oil. New areas such as tourism, entertainment and technology are to grow.

For a long time the country was largely closed to tourists. Since **2019** Saudi Arabia has issued **tourist visas** also to travellers with no religious or business purpose. The **religious police** used to watch strictly over rules in everyday life. In April **2016** it lost the power to arrest people. Since 2018 women have been allowed to drive. Human rights organisations, however, continue to criticise restrictions on freedom of expression.

gewusst: Saudi Arabia has no permanently flowing rivers.
A large part of the country is desert, including the Rub al-Khali, one of the largest sand deserts on Earth.

teile.einleitung: Khadija bint Khuwaylid was the first wife of the Prophet Muhammad. She was a successful businesswoman in Mecca. According to tradition she was the first person to believe in Muhammad's message.
wichtigste: Khadija was a wealthy businesswoman and widow in Mecca.
According to tradition she proposed marriage to Muhammad.
Muhammad was about 25 years old at the wedding.
She is regarded as the first Muslim woman.
The two had four daughters, among them Fatima.
Khadija died in 619, in the so-called “Year of Sorrow”.

abschnitte.text: Khadija lived in **Mecca**. She had been married before and had lost her husband, so she was a **widow**. After that she ran her business independently. As a wealthy **merchant** she sent goods with **caravans** on long journeys. Muhammad conducted trading business for her and was known for his honesty.

Khadija valued Muhammad's reliability. According to tradition she therefore had a **marriage proposal** passed on to him. Muhammad was then about **25 years** old; Khadija was clearly older, often about 40 is mentioned. For about 25 years Muhammad was married only to her. The two had four daughters: **Zaynab**, **Ruqayya**, **Umm Kulthum** and **Fatima**. Their sons died as small children.

When Muhammad, according to tradition, experienced his first **revelation**, he was frightened. Khadija comforted him and believed in his message. That is why she is regarded as the **first person** to accept Islam. She took him to her cousin **Waraqa ibn Nawfal**, who knew the scriptures of the Christians. He interpreted the experience as a divine revelation. With her wealth Khadija supported the small community.

Khadija died in the year **619** in Mecca. In the same year Muhammad's uncle and protector **Abu Talib** also died. The loss of the two hit Muhammad hard. That is why this year is called the **“Year of Sorrow”**. Muhammad entered further marriages only after Khadija's death.

gewusst: Through their daughter Fatima, many families still trace their descent back to Muhammad and Khadija today.
In Islam Khadija is revered as one of the most exemplary women.

teile.einleitung: Many mosques can be recognised by two parts of the building: the dome and the minaret. The dome spans the prayer hall, and the minaret is a slender tower. Some of the most famous buildings in the world have such domes and minarets.
wichtigste: A dome is a vaulted roof in the shape of half a sphere.
A dome spans a large space without columns in the middle.
From the minaret, people traditionally call to prayer five times a day.
The word minaret comes from the Arabic “manara”.
The Blue Mosque in Istanbul has six minarets.
The Hassan II Mosque in Casablanca has a minaret over 200 metres high.

abschnitte.text: A **dome** is a round, vaulted part of a roof. It looks like **half a sphere**. Its great advantage: it can span a **large space without columns** in the middle. In this way many people can pray together and have a clear view. A great model was the **Hagia Sophia** in Istanbul. It was built as a church and later became a mosque.

The **minaret** is a slender tower next to the mosque. The word comes from the Arabic **“manara”** and means roughly “place of light” or “lighthouse”. Traditionally the **muezzin** calls to prayer from there. Muslims pray **five times a day**, and before every prayer the call to prayer sounds. Today this is often done with loudspeakers.

The **Sultan Ahmed Mosque** in Istanbul has **six minarets**. This was something quite special when it was built. It is also called the **Blue Mosque** because the walls inside are covered with many **blue and white tiles**. Its domes rise step by step to the great main dome.

In **Casablanca** in Morocco the **Hassan II Mosque** stands right on the sea. Its minaret is **over 200 metres** high and is among the highest in the world. In **Agra** in **India** stands the **Taj Mahal**. It is a tomb with a large white dome and four minarets.

In Switzerland there are only very few minarets. In 2009 the voters accepted the **minaret initiative**. Since then the Federal Constitution has forbidden the **building of new minarets**. The existing minarets, for example at the **Mahmood Mosque** in Zurich, were allowed to stay. The vote was much discussed at home and abroad.

gewusst: The minaret of the Hassan II Mosque is over 200 metres high.
Minaret originally means roughly “lighthouse”.

teile.einleitung: In the year 622 Muhammad moved with his followers from Mecca to Medina. There the first Muslim community arose. Many rules and customs of Islam come from this time.
wichtigste: The community of all Muslims is called the umma in Arabic.
The Constitution of Medina regulated how the groups in the city lived together.
Jewish tribes also lived in Medina and were included in the arrangement.
The Friday prayer and fasting in Ramadan were introduced in Medina.
Around 624 the direction of prayer was changed from Jerusalem to Mecca.
Muhammad is buried in the Prophet's Mosque in Medina.

abschnitte.text: In Mecca, Muhammad and his followers were harassed. In the year **622** they moved to **Medina**. This emigration is called the **Hijra**. With it the Islamic calendar begins. In Medina the first Muslim community arose, the **umma**. The word still describes the community of all believers today.

In Medina there lived various tribes, among them **Jewish tribes**. The **Constitution of Medina** set out the rights and duties of these groups. It was meant to prevent quarrels and to protect the city together. Many see in it an early kind of **constitution**. The arrangement included the Jewish tribes as part of the city community.

In Medina the **Friday prayer** with a sermon was introduced. It is still the most important communal prayer of the week today. In the year 624, the second year after the Hijra, **fasting in Ramadan** became a duty. At first the Muslims prayed in the direction of **Jerusalem**. Around 624 the direction of prayer, the **qibla**, was changed to Mecca, to the Kaaba.

Fighting broke out between Medina and Mecca. In 624 the Muslims won the **battle of Badr** against a larger army. In 625 they lost at **Uhud**, a mountain near Medina, but Medina was not taken. In 627 a large army besieged the city. On the advice of the Persian Salman, the Muslims dug a **trench** that the horsemen could not cross, and the siege failed.
