Later Muhammad was able to return to Mecca. He died in 632 in Medina and was buried in his house next to the mosque. Today the grave lies inside the **Prophet's Mosque**. After Mecca, Medina is the second holiest city of Islam. Many pilgrims visit the mosque.

gewusst: The name Medina simply means “the city”; the place used to be called Yathrib.
The Islamic calendar counts the years from the Hijra in the year 622.

teile.einleitung: Ibn Khaldun was an Arab scholar of the 14th century. He thought about why empires arise and fall apart again. Today he is regarded as a forerunner of sociology.
wichtigste: Ibn Khaldun was born in 1332 in Tunis and died in 1406 in Cairo.
His best-known work is the Muqaddimah of 1377.
The Muqaddimah is the introduction to his world history, the “Kitab al-Ibar”.
At the centre of his explanation is asabiyyah, group solidarity.
According to him a dynasty usually declines after about three generations.
In 1401 he met the conqueror Timur outside Damascus.

abschnitte.text: Ibn Khaldun was born in **1332** in **Tunis**. His family came from Andalusia in Spain and had emigrated to Tunis. He worked at many royal courts in North Africa and Spain. Later he lived in **Cairo**. There the Mamluk sultan appointed him several times as **Maliki chief judge**, that is, the highest judge of a school of law. Besides this he taught at colleges. He died in **1406** in Cairo.

In the year **1377** Ibn Khaldun wrote the **Muqaddimah**. The word means “introduction”. It introduces his world history, the **“Kitab al-Ibar”**, which deals especially with the history of the Arabs and Berbers. In the Muqaddimah he develops a theory of **society, economy and history**. He asked not only what happened but also why.

A central concept is **asabiyyah**. It means group solidarity or togetherness. According to Ibn Khaldun, groups with strong solidarity, often from the desert, seize power. In the cities they become rich and lose their solidarity again. A dynasty therefore usually lasts only about **three generations**, around 120 years. The founders are tough, he said, and their descendants grow soft in luxury.

Ibn Khaldun examined **systematically** how tribes, cities and states work. That is why he is regarded as an early pioneer of **sociology**, the science of how people live together. He also wrote about work, trade and taxes. In **1401**, during the siege of Damascus, he met the conqueror **Timur**. He held several conversations with him and reported on them in his autobiography.

gewusst: Ibn Khaldun wrote an autobiography, which was rare for scholars of his time.
In Tunis there stands a large statue of him.

teile.einleitung: Muslims from many countries live in Switzerland. They have joined together in mosque associations and larger umbrella organisations. These organisations represent Muslims towards the authorities and the public.
wichtigste: Most mosque associations are private associations.
Many associations are organised by origin and language.
The FIDS has been a nationwide umbrella organisation since 2006.
The KIOS was founded in 2000 in Bern.
The VIOZ represents mosque associations in the canton of Zurich.
In the Swiss Council of Religions, Christians, Jews and Muslims advise together.

abschnitte.text: In Switzerland most Muslim communities are organised **under private law as associations**. Unlike the national churches, they are mostly not recognised under public law in the cantons. They are therefore not allowed to levy **church tax**. The members finance their mosques with contributions and donations.

Many mosque associations are organised by **origin and language**. There are, for example, Albanian, Bosnian, Turkish and Arabic associations. There, preaching is often in the language of the country of origin. The associations often keep close ties to that country. One umbrella organisation even links communities of **eastern Switzerland** and the Principality of **Liechtenstein**; it was founded in 2003.

To appear together, many associations have joined in **umbrella organisations**. The **KIOS**, the Coordination of Islamic Organisations of Switzerland, arose in 2000 in Bern. In 2006 the **FIDS** was founded, the Federation of Islamic Umbrella Organisations of Switzerland. It unites many regional organisations and ones organised by origin. In the canton of Zurich there is the **VIOZ**, the Association of Islamic Organisations in Zurich.

Since 2006 there has been the **Swiss Council of Religions**. There leaders of Christians, Jews and Muslims advise together. Representatives of Muslim umbrella organisations also sit on this body. It wants to promote peace between the religions.

Not all Muslims think alike. The **Forum for a Progressive Islam** was founded in 2004 in Zurich and represents a liberal interpretation. The **Islamic Central Council of Switzerland**, founded in 2009, named about 3,700 members in 2016. That was fewer than one per cent of the Muslims in Switzerland, and other organisations distanced themselves from it several times.

gewusst: There is a joint umbrella organisation for eastern Switzerland and Liechtenstein.
Muslim associations in Switzerland are not allowed to levy church tax.

teile.einleitung: The Cave of Hira lies on a mountain near Mecca. According to Islamic tradition, Muhammad received the first revelation there around the year 610. With it the story of the Quran begins.
wichtigste: The Cave of Hira lies on Jabal al-Nour, the “Mountain of Light”, near Mecca.
Muhammad often withdrew there to reflect and pray.
Around 610 he received the first revelation there, when he was about 40 years old.
The first revealed verses are in surah 96 and begin with “Read!”.
Over about 23 years Muhammad received revelations.
Around 613 he began to preach publicly in Mecca.

abschnitte.titel: A cave on the Mountain of Light
abschnitte.text: The Cave of Hira lies on **Jabal al-Nour** near Mecca. The name means **“Mountain of Light”**. The cave is small and can be reached only by a steep path. Muhammad often spent several days there alone. He reflected and prayed. Today many pilgrims climb the mountain to see the cave.

According to tradition, the angel Gabriel appeared to Muhammad around the year **610**. Muhammad was then about **40 years** old. The revelation began with the command **“iqra”**, which means “Read!” or “Recite!”. These first verses are in **surah 96**, which is called al-Alaq. Muslims believe that the sending down of the Quran began on the **Night of Power**. In Arabic it is called Laylat al-Qadr and falls in the last nights of Ramadan.

After this experience Muhammad was deeply **shaken**. He hurried home to his wife **Khadija** and asked to be covered up. Khadija comforted him and believed him. She is regarded as the first person to accept Islam. The revelations went on after that for about **23 years**, until Muhammad's death. So the Quran did not arise all at once.

At first Muhammad spoke about his message only with family and friends. Around **613** he began to preach publicly in Mecca. Many powerful families of the city rejected him and harassed his followers. Around **615** Muhammad sent a group to **Abyssinia**, present-day Ethiopia. The Christian king there took in the refugees and protected them.

gewusst: The Cave of Hira is only a few metres long, and an adult can barely stand in it.
The first revelation begins with a word that has to do with reading and learning.

teile.einleitung: The House of Wisdom was a famous library and place of scholars in Baghdad. There many books were translated from Greek and other languages into Arabic. In this way valuable knowledge of antiquity was preserved.
wichtigste: The House of Wisdom stood in Baghdad, the capital of the Abbasids.
Its heyday was in the 9th century, especially under the caliph al-Ma'mun.
Scholars translated Greek works on philosophy, medicine and mathematics into Arabic.
Aristotle was translated especially often.
Cheap paper helped to spread books.
In 1258 the Mongols conquered Baghdad, and many libraries were lost.

abschnitte.text: From 750 the **Abbasids** ruled the Islamic empire as caliphs. They founded **Baghdad** as a new capital on the River Tigris. The city quickly became large and rich. The caliphs promoted **science and translations**. In the **House of Wisdom** there were many books, and scholars met there to read, translate and do research.

The House of Wisdom experienced its greatest flowering under the **caliph al-Ma'mun**. He ruled from 813 to 833. He promoted scholars and translators very strongly and even had people search for Greek **manuscripts**. The great translation movement took place mainly in the **9th century**. That was about 200 years after the life of Muhammad.

Many works of Greek **philosophy, medicine and mathematics** were translated into Arabic. The writings of **Aristotle** on logic, nature and ethics were translated almost completely. One of the most famous translators was the Christian doctor **Hunayn ibn Ishaq**. He translated numerous medical works, for example by Galen. He worked very precisely and compared different manuscripts.

In Baghdad, around **795**, a **paper mill** was built. The technique of papermaking came from China. Paper was much cheaper than parchment made of animal skin. That is why more books could be copied and spread. Baghdad soon had many bookshops and libraries.

In the year **1258**, **Mongol troops** conquered Baghdad and severely destroyed the city. Many libraries and books were lost in the process. This meant the end of the House of Wisdom. But much knowledge had already been passed on, and later it also reached Europe by way of Spain.

gewusst: Socrates, another famous Greek philosopher, wrote no books himself.
Arabic translations were later translated into Latin, and in this way scholars in Europe got to know Aristotle anew.

teile.einleitung: The mihrab is a niche in the wall of a mosque. It shows those who pray which direction they should turn: towards Mecca. Almost every mosque in the world has a mihrab.
wichtigste: A mihrab is a prayer niche in the mosque.
It shows the direction of prayer towards Mecca.
This direction is called the qibla in Arabic.
In communal prayer the imam stands in front of the mihrab.
Many mihrabs are decorated with calligraphy and ornaments.

abschnitte.text: Muslims pray in the direction of the **Kaaba** in **Mecca**. This direction of prayer is called the **qibla**. The wall of a mosque that points to Mecca is called the qibla wall. In its middle lies the **mihrab**, a niche, often with an arch at the top. In this way everyone sees at once where to turn in prayer. From Switzerland, Mecca lies roughly to the south-east.

In communal prayer the **imam** stands at the front, before the mihrab. He leads the prayer, and the others pray in rows behind him. The niche also helps the sound: the imam's voice is slightly amplified by the curve. The mihrab itself is not a holy object; it is a signpost.

In many mosques the mihrab is the most beautiful part of the room. It is decorated with **calligraphy**, that is, artfully written verses of the Quran. In addition there are **ornaments** of plants and geometric patterns, coloured tiles or mosaics. A famous example is the gold-glittering mihrab of the Mezquita of Córdoba in Spain. You do not see pictures of people there.

gewusst: The word mihrab already occurs in the Quran: there Zakariya visits the young Maryam in her mihrab.
Next to the mihrab there is usually the minbar, the pulpit for the Friday sermon.

teile.einleitung: Medina is a city in the west of Saudi Arabia. After Mecca it is the second holiest city of Islam. Here the Prophet Muhammad lived his last years, and here he is buried.
wichtigste: Medina used to be called Yathrib.
In the year 622 Muhammad moved with his followers from Mecca to Medina.
This emigration is called the Hijra.
Muhammad lived about ten years in Medina and died there in 632.
His grave lies in the Prophet's Mosque under a green dome.
Medina is also called the “City of the Prophet”.

abschnitte.text: The oasis town used to be called **Yathrib**. In Mecca, Muhammad and his followers were harassed. In the year **622** they therefore moved to Yathrib, where they were received kindly. This emigration is called the **Hijra**, and the word means “emigration”. Since then the city has been called **Medina**, short for “City of the Prophet”.

The Hijra was so important that the **Islamic calendar** begins with it. In Medina the first Muslim community arose. The people from Mecca were called **emigrants**, and the inhabitants of Medina who helped them were called **helpers**. Muhammad lived about ten years in Medina. In the year **632** he died there.

In the centre of the city stands the **Prophet's Mosque**. Muhammad had it built right after his arrival, at that time still quite simply from mud and palm trunks. Today it is huge and has room for a very great number of people. Under the famous **green dome** lies the **grave of Muhammad**. Next to him the first two caliphs, Abu Bakr and Umar, are buried.

On the edge of Medina lies the **Quba Mosque**. It is regarded as the **first mosque** of Islam. Muhammad is said to have founded it on his way to Medina. It too was later rebuilt and enlarged several times. Many pilgrims visit it when they are in Medina.

Every year millions of people come to Medina. Many combine the visit with the pilgrimage to **Mecca**, although it is not part of the pilgrimage duty. The inner area of the city around the Prophet's Mosque is reserved for Muslims. Medina also bears the honorary name “the enlightened city”.

gewusst: The Islamic year 1 begins with the Hijra in the year 622.
The first Prophet's Mosque had columns of palm trunks and a roof of palm leaves.

teile.einleitung: The Umayyads were the first ruling family to make the caliphate hereditary. From 661 to 750 they ruled a huge empire from Damascus. A branch of the family then ruled for a long time in Spain.
wichtigste: The Umayyads ruled from Damascus from 661 to 750.
Under al-Walid I the Umayyad Mosque in Damascus was built.
Abd al-Malik made Arabic the language of administration.
Tariq ibn Ziyad crossed over to Hispania in 711.
Charles Martel stopped an Umayyad army at Tours and Poitiers in 732.
Abd al-Rahman I founded an emirate of his own in Córdoba in 756.

abschnitte.text: In the year 661 **Muawiya** founded the dynasty of the Umayyads. The capital became **Damascus** in present-day Syria. Under the Umayyads the empire grew greatly, from Spain to Central Asia. Under the caliph **al-Walid I** the **Great Mosque of Damascus** was built, the Umayyad Mosque. It is among the oldest surviving large mosques in the world.

The caliph **Abd al-Malik** introduced important reforms. He made **Arabic the language of administration** throughout the empire. Before that, Greek and Persian were often used. Under him Islamic coins of their own also appeared. In Jerusalem he had the **Dome of the Rock** built.

In the year **711** the commander **Tariq ibn Ziyad** crossed over with Muslim troops to **Hispania**, present-day Spain. The name Gibraltar comes from “Jabal Tariq”, the “Mountain of Tariq”. In a short time the troops conquered large parts of the Iberian Peninsula. In **732** **Charles Martel** stopped the advance of an Umayyad army into the Frankish Empire at the **battle of Tours and Poitiers**.

Under the Umayyads, **non-Arab Muslims**, the **mawali**, were often at a disadvantage compared with Arabs. Discontent grew. In **750** the Umayyads were overthrown in Damascus by the **Abbasids**. The Umayyad **Abd al-Rahman I** managed to flee. In **756** he founded in **Córdoba** an emirate of his own, which later became a caliphate.

gewusst: The name Gibraltar goes back to the commander Tariq ibn Ziyad.
The Great Mosque of Córdoba was built under the Spanish Umayyads and is today a cathedral.
